papers.ja_title: 長文脈の継続事前学習は早くやめるべきでない、という経験則スケーリング則
papers.summary: 長い文章を扱う能力を上げるための継続事前学習(LCCP)は、トークン数を増やすとどこまで効果が伸びるのかが分かっていなかった。5 つのモデル規模と 100 通り以上のトークン配分で実験し、モデルサイズと事前学習・LCCP それぞれのトークン量から長文脈性能を予測できる経験則(累乗則)を作り、12.2 億パラメータのモデルを約 1000 億トークンで学習した軌跡にもよく当てはまることを確認した。評価の範囲内では性能の伸びが頭打ちになる様子は見られず、128K への文脈拡張や instruction tuning の後も効果が残り、長文理解やエージェント的なタスクにも転用できた。
papers.why: 長文脈対応の継続学習にどれだけトークン予算を割くべきかを、頭打ちを心配せず予測できる定量的な根拠を与える。
papers.summary_en: Long-context continual pre-training (LCCP) is widely used to improve long-context capability, but how its benefits scale with the number of LCCP tokens has remained unclear. The authors establish an empirical additive power law relating long-context performance to model size and to the token budgets of short-context pretraining and LCCP, fitting it across five model scales and over one hundred budget configurations and showing it extrapolates well to held-out model scales; they also introduce Constant-Last4, a protocol that averages the four most recent checkpoints from a constant-learning-rate run for stable monitoring, under which the same scaling-law form accurately predicts the LCCP trajectory of a 1.22B-parameter model trained on about 100B LCCP tokens. Downstream evaluations along this trajectory show continued improvements in long-context performance with no clear sign of saturation within the evaluated range, with gains persisting after both 128K context extension and supervised fine-tuning and transferring to long-context understanding and agentic tasks.
papers.why_en: Provides a quantitative, extrapolatable scaling law plus a practical monitoring protocol (Constant-Last4) for deciding how many LCCP tokens to budget, arguing against stopping long-context continued pretraining early on intuition alone.

papers.title: Right On Q: Recovering Reasoning under Quantization via Self-Generated Trajectories
papers.abstract: Quantization-aware training (QAT) aims to recover reasoning capabilities in low-bit large language models (LLMs). Existing recipes typically supervise the quantized student with the original full-precision model on fixed response sequences. However, the resulting low-bit quantized models still struggle on long-horizon reasoning tasks and often fail to terminate within a token budget that suffices for the full-precision model. We identify two challenges in closing this gap. First, fixed-response supervision leaves a mismatch between training prefixes and those encountered during student generation, and this trajectory divergence grows as responses lengthen. Second, on its own prefixes, the student underpredicts some next-token candidates and overpredicts others, and this distributional misalignment becomes more frequent at high-entropy prefixes. We present OnQ, a low-bit recovery pipeline that combines on-policy distillation and candidate-wise Dynamic KL. Starting from block-wise calibration, the quantized student generates responses and receives full-precision teacher supervision on its own prefixes. Dynamic KL weights forward and reverse KL by each candidate's teacher-student probability ratio to balance correction of under- and overprediction. Across Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, and 8B at 2- and 3-bit precision, OnQ achieves the highest nine-benchmark average, with the largest gains on long-horizon reasoning benchmarks. At 2 bits, it outperforms every baseline on every benchmark at every model size, improving the Qwen3-8B average by 10.26 points over the strongest baseline. It also produces shorter responses with fewer truncations and repetitive errors.
papers.ja_title: 量子化した LLM の推論力を自分が作った軌跡で取り戻す OnQ
papers.summary: LLM を低ビットに量子化(数値の精度を落として軽量化)すると、長い推論を要するタスクで答えが出し切れなくなる問題がある。従来の量子化対応学習は元のモデルが書いた固定の回答文で量子化後のモデルを教えていたが、生成が長くなるほど量子化モデル自身の出力とその固定回答文がずれていく問題があった。OnQ は量子化モデル自身に答えを生成させ、その続きに対して元の精度のモデルが教師として添削を行う方式に切り替え、Qwen3 の 1.7B・4B・8B モデルの 2 ビット・3 ビット量子化で 9 個のベンチマーク平均が最良となり、8B モデルの 2 ビットでは既存最強手法より 10.26 点改善した。
papers.why: 低ビット量子化後の推論性能の落ち込みを、学習データの作り方だけで大きく改善できることを示し、量子化デプロイの実務に効く。
papers.summary_en: Quantization-aware training aims to recover reasoning capability in low-bit LLMs, but existing recipes that supervise the quantized student with a full-precision teacher on fixed response sequences leave low-bit models struggling on long-horizon reasoning and often failing to terminate within a token budget that suffices for the full-precision model. The authors identify two causes, a training-generation prefix mismatch that grows as responses lengthen and a distributional misalignment where the student under- or over-predicts next-token candidates more often at high-entropy prefixes, and address them with OnQ, which combines on-policy distillation, where the quantized student generates responses and the full-precision teacher supervises its own prefixes, with candidate-wise Dynamic KL that weights forward and reverse KL by each candidate's teacher-student probability ratio. Across Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, and 8B at 2- and 3-bit precision, OnQ achieves the highest nine-benchmark average, outperforms every baseline on every benchmark at every model size at 2 bits, improves the Qwen3-8B average by 10.26 points over the strongest baseline, and produces shorter responses with fewer truncations and repetitive errors.
papers.why_en: Names and diagnoses a specific failure mode, a training/generation prefix mismatch that worsens with response length, behind low-bit reasoning degradation, giving a reusable diagnosis for anyone doing quantization-aware training on reasoning models.

papers.title: Nominate-then-Adjudicate: LLM-Assisted One-Pass and Per-Instance MIP Solver Tuning
papers.abstract: Mixed-integer programming solvers expose hundreds or even thousands of parameters whose best setting varies per instance, yet per-instance search is prohibitively expensive. We frame this as configuration for heterogeneous Big Data optimization workloads and propose a nominate-then-adjudicate pipeline built around two design choices. First, a fixed portfolio is sampled once and reused across instances, removing per-instance configuration search at inference; on the evaluated families, the resulting shortlist retains substantial oracle headroom, making selection within it the empirical focus. Second, the fixed 20-feature representation can map structurally different instances to the same vector, preventing a feature-only selector from distinguishing them even when they prefer different configurations. The foundation model receives no task-specific weight updates, and selection is one-pass: one model call and no solver calls at inference. The study represents structural Variety through distinct formulation families and decision Value through solver-performance outcomes; the one-call, zero-solve protocol specifies the decision interface and leaves end-to-end latency unmeasured. Among comparisons exceeding a 20% practical-difference threshold, the complete adjudicator records 538 wins and 185 losses against the top nominee, while its win rate against the default rises from 84.9% to 90.2%. Against per-instance configuration baselines under a matched one-pass protocol it leads the cluster-level methods and the best-performing evaluated per-instance baseline, ISAC+.
papers.ja_title: LLM が混合整数計画ソルバーの設定を 1 回の呼び出しで選ぶ Nominate-then-Adjudicate

papers.title: A Strong MoE Is All You Need for Process Supervision
papers.abstract: Process reward models (PRMs) provide fine-grained supervision for multi-step reasoning, yet obtaining reliable process labels remains a central bottleneck. Existing approaches typically rely on human annotation, rollout-based estimation, or auxiliary verification. In this work, we explore a different source of process supervision natively exposed by Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models: expert routing. We show that simple routing statistics provide an intrinsic process-confidence signal that is competitive with conventional output-logit confidence. Building on this observation, we construct routing confidence by combining overall routing mass, head routing mass, and within-step routing variation, and introduce RoCo-Rethink, which identifies the least confident reasoning step and selectively regenerates the subsequent trajectory. We further introduce RoCo-PRM, which uses a strong MoE to automatically annotate reasoning trajectories with routing-derived step scores and distills them into a standalone PRM. Across multiple MoE architectures and diverse reasoning tasks, both RoCo-Rethink and RoCo-PRM consistently outperform strong baselines, while RoCo-PRM transfers effectively across both model architectures and tasks. Our findings suggest that expert routing is more than a computational dispatch mechanism: it provides an architecture-native source of process supervision for reasoning.
papers.ja_title: MoE の経路選択(ルーティング)情報を推論の途中経過の信頼度として使う RoCo
papers.summary: 複数ステップの推論を監督する「プロセス報酬モデル」を作るには、各ステップが正しいかのラベルが必要だが、人手のラベル付けや追加の検証はコストが高い。この研究は MoE(入力ごとに得意な専門家ネットワークへ振り分ける仕組み)が本来持っている、どの専門家にどれだけ振り分けたかという情報自体が、ステップの確信度を表す信号として使えることを示した。これを使って自信の低いステップを見つけて再生成する RoCo-Rethink と、その信号でプロセス報酬モデルを自動的に作る RoCo-PRM を提案し、複数の MoE モデルと推論タスクで既存手法を上回った。
papers.why: MoE のルーティング情報を単なる計算の振り分けでなく推論品質の信号として再利用するという着眼点は、MoE アーキテクチャ設計の価値を広げる。
papers.summary_en: Process reward models need reliable step-level labels, normally obtained through human annotation, rollout-based estimation, or auxiliary verification. The authors instead use a signal natively exposed by Mixture-of-Experts models, expert routing, showing that simple routing statistics give an intrinsic process-confidence signal competitive with conventional output-logit confidence; combining overall routing mass, head routing mass, and within-step routing variation, they build RoCo-Rethink, which identifies the least confident reasoning step and selectively regenerates the subsequent trajectory, and RoCo-PRM, which uses a strong MoE to auto-annotate trajectories with routing-derived step scores and distills them into a standalone PRM. Across multiple MoE architectures and diverse reasoning tasks, both RoCo-Rethink and RoCo-PRM consistently outperform strong baselines, with RoCo-PRM transferring effectively across both model architectures and tasks, suggesting expert routing is more than a computational dispatch mechanism.
papers.why_en: Offers a label-free, architecture-native source of process supervision that comes for free from an MoE model's own routing statistics, directly useful for training process reward models without expensive step-level annotation.

papers.title: D-Pingmesh: Dynamic Probing and Fault Localization for Reconfigurable Datacenter Networks
papers.abstract: Pingmesh monitors datacenter networks through periodic pings between servers. In reconfigurable datacenter networks, topology engineering (TPE) and traffic engineering (TE) make uniform server-pair probing inefficient: a pinglist wastes budget retesting common paths while missing low-probability interfaces. Frequent control-plane updates further require rapid pinglist refresh, and cause path ambiguity at control-plane boundaries for fault localization. We present D-Pingmesh, a probing and fault-localization system co-designed with the TPE/TE control plane. Its control-plane-aware generator builds task-efficient pinglists by greedily admitting probes with high interface coverage under the current TPE/TE snapshot. An incremental replay-and-repair mechanism updates pinglists across reconfigurations rather than recomputing from scratch. At control-plane boundaries, a Rho-EM localizer jointly infers per-task old/new-path mixture weights and the fault set through EM-style iteration. We evaluate D-Pingmesh on an 8-pod reconfigurable topology under dynamic TPE/TE. At a 0.99 coverage target, D-Pingmesh uses 17.7x fewer tasks than Pingmesh and generates each pinglist about 5.1x faster than RD-Probe. In ns-3 simulation, boundary-aware localization improves micro F1 from 0.871 to 0.953 over the deTector PLL baseline. A testbed deployment demonstrates second-scale fault localization with low host overhead. These results demonstrate that D-Pingmesh is practical for reconfigurable datacenter networks with control-plane-aware monitoring.
papers.theme: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.ja_title: 構成が変わり続けるデータセンターネットワークに合わせて探索経路を調整する D-Pingmesh
papers.summary: データセンター内のネットワークを定期的に ping で監視する Pingmesh という仕組みは、経路や配線をソフトウェアで動的に変える「再構成可能なネットワーク」では非効率になる。D-Pingmesh はネットワークの制御系の状態に合わせて監視先を選び直し、設定が変わるたびに監視リストを作り直すのではなく差分だけ修正する仕組みと、切り替えの境目で起きる経路のあいまいさに対応する故障特定の仕組みを組み合わせた。評価では同じ監視カバー率(0.99)を達成するのに必要な監視回数が Pingmesh の 17.7 倍少なく、故障箇所特定の精度指標(F1)も 0.871 から 0.953 に上がった。
papers.why: GPU クラスタ内のネットワークを再構成しながら運用する場合の監視コストを大きく下げる発想で、大規模クラスタの運用設計に直結する。
papers.summary_en: Pingmesh monitors datacenter networks through periodic server-pair pings, but in reconfigurable networks that use topology engineering (TPE) and traffic engineering (TE), uniform probing wastes budget retesting common paths while missing low-probability interfaces, and frequent control-plane updates require rapid pinglist refresh while causing path ambiguity for fault localization at control-plane boundaries. The authors present D-Pingmesh, co-designed with the TPE/TE control plane: a control-plane-aware generator greedily builds task-efficient pinglists under the current TPE/TE snapshot, an incremental replay-and-repair mechanism updates pinglists across reconfigurations rather than recomputing from scratch, and a Rho-EM localizer at control-plane boundaries jointly infers per-task old/new-path mixture weights and the fault set through EM-style iteration. On an 8-pod reconfigurable topology at a 0.99 coverage target, D-Pingmesh uses 17.7x fewer tasks than Pingmesh and generates each pinglist about 5.1x faster than RD-Probe; in ns-3 simulation, boundary-aware localization improves micro F1 from 0.871 to 0.953 over the deTector PLL baseline, and a testbed deployment demonstrates second-scale fault localization with low host overhead.
papers.why_en: A deployed system for keeping network health monitoring efficient and accurate specifically under reconfigurable datacenter topologies, relevant as training and inference clusters increasingly run on dynamically reconfigured optical/electrical fabrics.

papers.title: UlaCache: Unified Logical Addressing for Sparse LLM Serving
papers.abstract: Long contexts increase the memory cost of the key-value (KV) cache in large language model (LLM) inference. Sparse attention reduces attention computation and memory traffic by selecting historical tokens, but the retained KV cache must remain available for later decoding steps. We present UlaCache, a KV cache management system built around a unified logical address space spanning GPU KV pools and optional CPU memory. Stable logical references let the inference engine allocate and select KV independently of physical placement. Common allocation and sparse-access interfaces support data-parallel (DP) and tensor-parallel (TP) attention. For distributed storage, local GPU buffers retain selected KV across decoding steps, so only missing entries require transfers. When CPU storage is enabled, Parallel Bucketed LRU (PB-LRU) manages a GPU pool shared across requests. It updates recency metadata and selects eviction victims in parallel. UlaCache transfers KV and then updates the address mappings. With speculative decoding enabled under matched CPU and GPU memory budgets, UlaCache achieves peak decoding throughput speedups of 1.16 $\times$ (DP) and 1.70 $\times$ (TP) on H200, and 1.73 $\times$ (DP) and 2.51 $\times$ (TP) on B300, compared with the state-of-the-art baseline.
papers.ja_title: 疎な注意機構向け LLM サービングのための統一論理アドレス方式 KV キャッシュ UlaCache
papers.summary: 長い文章を扱う LLM 推論では KV キャッシュ(過去の計算結果を覚えておく領域)のメモリ消費が増える。スパースアテンション(注目する過去のトークンを絞る手法)はこの消費を減らせるが、選んだ KV キャッシュは後の生成でも使える状態で残しておく必要がある。UlaCache は GPU のメモリ領域と任意で CPU メモリにまたがる「論理アドレス」を導入し、物理的な置き場所を気にせず KV キャッシュを割り当て・選択できるようにし、並列処理向けの LRU(最近使われていないものを捨てる)方式でキャッシュを管理する。H200 では既存最良手法に比べてデコードのスループットが最大 1.70 倍、B300 では最大 2.51 倍に向上した。
papers.why: 長文脈かつスパースアテンションを使う本番サービング環境での KV キャッシュ管理を、データ並列・テンソル並列の両方に対応させた実装設計として参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Long contexts inflate the KV cache memory cost of LLM inference, and sparse attention reduces computation and memory traffic by selecting historical tokens, but the retained KV cache must still remain available for later decoding steps. The authors present UlaCache, a KV cache management system built around a unified logical address space spanning GPU KV pools and optional CPU memory, so the inference engine can allocate and select KV independently of physical placement, with common allocation and sparse-access interfaces supporting both data-parallel and tensor-parallel attention; local GPU buffers retain selected KV across decoding steps so only missing entries require transfer, and when CPU storage is enabled, Parallel Bucketed LRU (PB-LRU) manages a GPU pool shared across requests by updating recency metadata and selecting eviction victims in parallel. With speculative decoding enabled under matched CPU and GPU memory budgets, UlaCache achieves peak decoding throughput speedups of 1.16x (DP) and 1.70x (TP) on H200, and 1.73x (DP) and 2.51x (TP) on B300, compared with the state-of-the-art baseline.
papers.why_en: A unified logical addressing abstraction that decouples KV placement from physical memory is directly relevant to building sparse-attention-aware KV cache systems that must span GPU and CPU memory under data- and tensor-parallel attention.

papers.title: HAWK: Heterogeneity-Aware KV Cache Transfer for Efficient GPU-NPU Phase-Disaggregated LLM Inference
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference exhibits distinct computational characteristics across its two phases: prefill is compute-intensive, whereas decode is more memory-bound. As a result, AI accelerators achieve varying levels of efficiency across the two phases. GPUs are well suited to prefill, but are often underutilized during decode. By contrast, NPUs can utilize their compute resources more effectively during decode. Motivated by this observation, we explore a heterogeneous architecture that integrates GPUs and NPUs, mapping prefill to GPUs and decode to NPUs to achieve high performance and efficiency. However, realizing such heterogeneous integration is challenging because LLM phase disaggregation requires KV cache transfer from prefill to decode (that is, from GPUs to NPUs), which is complicated by differences in inter-device communication mechanisms and KV cache tensor layouts. To address this, we propose HAWK, a transfer mechanism that enables rapid KV cache transfer across heterogeneous devices. HAWK establishes a remote direct memory access (RDMA) path for direct cross-device transfers while handling inter-device tensor layout discrepancies as part of the transfer process. In particular, HAWK allocates tensor-layout-aware RDMA buffers on the NPU side to match the target tensor layout. Leveraging these buffers, HAWK orchestrates data transfer from a conventional contiguous GPU RDMA buffer to the corresponding NPU buffers, allowing transferred tensors to be consumed directly without additional data rearrangement while maintaining transfer efficiency. We implement and evaluate HAWK on a system built with commercially available GPUs and NPUs, demonstrating performance within 7.88% of a GPU-only system under the same SLO constraints while achieving up to 1.26$\times$ higher power efficiency and 1.72$\times$ higher cost efficiency.
topics: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.ja_title: GPU と NPU を跨いだ KV キャッシュ転送で推論を分離配置する HAWK
papers.summary: LLM 推論はプロンプトを読み込む「プリフィル」段階と文章を生成する「デコード」段階で計算の性質が異なり、GPU はプリフィルが得意、NPU はデコードで計算資源を効率的に使える。この性質を利用してプリフィルを GPU、デコードを NPU に分担させる構成を試みたが、GPU から NPU へ KV キャッシュを渡す際に通信方式やデータの並べ方の違いが壁になっていた。HAWK は RDMA(機器間で直接メモリをやり取りする技術)を使い、NPU 側のバッファをあらかじめ目的のデータ形式に合わせて用意することで、並べ替えなしに直接データを渡せるようにし、GPU 単体構成に対して性能差を 7.88% に抑えつつ、電力効率を最大 1.26 倍、コスト効率を最大 1.72 倍高めた。
papers.why: GPU と NPU といった異種アクセラレータを同じ推論パイプラインに混在させる際の KV キャッシュ転送設計は、今後のヘテロジニアスなサービング基盤構築の実例として参考になる。
papers.summary_en: LLM inference has two phases with different characteristics: prefill is compute-intensive while decode is more memory-bound, so GPUs suit prefill well but are often underutilized during decode, whereas NPUs can use their compute more effectively during decode. Motivated by this, the authors explore a heterogeneous GPU-NPU architecture that maps prefill to GPUs and decode to NPUs, which requires transferring the KV cache from GPU to NPU despite differing inter-device communication mechanisms and KV cache tensor layouts. They propose HAWK, which establishes an RDMA path for direct cross-device transfer while handling tensor-layout discrepancies as part of the transfer, allocating tensor-layout-aware RDMA buffers on the NPU side so transferred tensors can be consumed directly without extra rearrangement. On a system built with commercially available GPUs and NPUs, HAWK performs within 7.88% of a GPU-only system under the same SLO constraints while achieving up to 1.26x higher power efficiency and 1.72x higher cost efficiency.
papers.why_en: A concrete mechanism for making GPU-NPU phase-disaggregated serving practical by solving the KV cache tensor-layout mismatch at the RDMA transfer layer, rather than requiring extra data rearrangement after transfer.

papers.title: Unintended Side Effects of Value Training in LLMs
papers.abstract: As LLMs are increasingly deployed in value-sensitive contexts, aligning them with human values has emerged as a post-training objective in NLP, aimed at instilling additional values and guiding model behaviour. However, current evaluations remain narrow. Because values are interconnected, it is unclear how fine-tuning for specific values alters unrelated capabilities and behaviours. In this work, we adapt four instruction-tuned LLMs across individual Hofstede's value dimensions and evaluate them on both cross-value transfer and broader behaviours. We find that value-specific training produces unintended side effects on untrained values, risk preferences, social cognition, and safety traits. Consequently, we suggest that value alignment after post-training should incorporate broader behavioral evaluations, and we highlight the need to investigate where additional value training might best fit into the pipeline.
topics: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.theme: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.ja_title: LLM の価値観調整が意図しない副作用を引き起こす

papers.title: Looped Uniform Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract: Uniform diffusion language models (UDLMs) generate text by iteratively denoising sequences of ordinary vocabulary tokens, any of which may be corrupted and subsequently revised. During training, UDLMs must denoise from a context that may itself be unreliable, whereas masked diffusion language models (MDLMs) always condition on a clean context. This challenging training objective makes UDLMs more FLOP-intensive to train than MDLMs, but it yields stronger downstream reasoning performance. Recently, selective looping, which recursively applies a few early Transformer layers within each denoising step, has been shown to improve training efficiency in MDLMs under an iso-FLOP budget. We investigate looping in UDLMs while keeping the training objective and sampler unchanged. We find that looping significantly improves training efficiency: looped UDLMs reach the validation NLL of a non-looped UDLM trained on about 0.5 trillion tokens with up to 2.8x fewer training FLOPs on OpenWebText and 3.3x fewer on FineWeb-Edu. We also find that, at a matched NFE budget, looped UDLMs reach up to 9.8% lower generation perplexity than the non-looped UDLM, with most gains achieved at moderate loop counts. Finally, we study different loop-count distributions and find that sampling smaller loop counts more frequently during training improves inference efficiency: on downstream tasks, this strategy uses 12% fewer loops than uniform loop-count sampling without degrading accuracy.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 一様拡散言語モデルにループ構造を入れて学習効率を上げる
papers.summary: 拡散言語モデルには、文脈の一部をマスクしてから生成する MDLM と、文脈のどのトークンも壊れている可能性がある状態から生成する UDLM(一様拡散言語モデル)があり、UDLM は訓練に多くの計算量(FLOP)が必要だが推論の精度は高い。この研究は、Transformer の初期の数層を 1 回のノイズ除去ステップの中で繰り返し使う「ループ」構造を UDLM に適用し、同じ計算量の制約下での学習効率を調べた。ループを使った UDLM は、ループなしの UDLM を約 0.5 兆トークンで学習した水準の性能に、OpenWebText で最大 2.8 倍、FineWeb-Edu で最大 3.3 倍少ない計算量で到達し、同じ生成ステップ数ではループなしより生成時の困惑度(ばらつきの指標)が最大 9.8% 低かった。
papers.why: 拡散言語モデルの訓練コストを下げつつ推論品質も上げられるループ構造という設計を示し、拡散型 LLM の学習・推論基盤を検討する際の選択肢になる。
papers.summary_en: Uniform diffusion language models (UDLMs) denoise sequences where any token, including context tokens, may be corrupted and revised, unlike masked diffusion language models (MDLMs) which always condition on a clean context; this harder training objective makes UDLMs more FLOP-intensive to train but gives stronger downstream reasoning. The authors apply selective looping, recursively applying a few early Transformer layers within each denoising step, previously shown to improve MDLM training efficiency, to UDLMs while keeping the training objective and sampler unchanged, and find looped UDLMs reach the validation NLL of a non-looped UDLM trained on about 0.5 trillion tokens using up to 2.8x fewer training FLOPs on OpenWebText and 3.3x fewer on FineWeb-Edu. At a matched NFE budget, looped UDLMs reach up to 9.8% lower generation perplexity than the non-looped UDLM, with most gains at moderate loop counts, and sampling smaller loop counts more frequently during training uses 12% fewer loops at inference on downstream tasks without degrading accuracy.
papers.why_en: Extends a training-efficiency trick already validated for masked diffusion models to the more expensive, stronger-reasoning uniform diffusion model family, with a concrete FLOP-reduction number (up to 2.8-3.3x) for training efficiency.

papers.title: The End of Consensus Research?
papers.abstract: Consensus is a fundamental problem in distributed computing and at the core of state machine replication (SMR). Despite decades of active human research, discovering practical low-latency solutions to the problem is still open, as it requires combining protocol knowledge, correctness reasoning, implementation, and experimental evaluation. We report on how AI helped us discover A-greement, a new consensus protocol for geo-replicated state machines that significantly outperforms state-of-the-art solutions. Averaged across six deployments with 5 or 9 replicas, A-greement reduces the mean latency of a geo-distributed key-value store over the fastest baseline by 12.2% and 33.3% on write-heavy and read-heavy workloads, respectively, and matches the fastest baseline on read-only workloads. A-greement combines lease-authorized local reads, direct client learning for leader-ordered writes, and a fast fixed-quorum per-key write path, selected according to network topology and workload. At the heart of our discovery lies AI-greement, an agent harness for the "autonomous" discovery, implementation, experimentation, and verification of candidate protocols. AI-greement integrates (1) a concept-oriented protocol knowledge base, (2) a modular implementation skeleton, and (3) a Lean-based verification framework with reusable safety definitions, reference specifications, and proofs. AI-greement is of independent interest: its Lean formalization uncovers several previously unreported vulnerabilities in existing consensus protocols, and it provides guidelines on how domain-specific harnesses can turn general-purpose coding agents into effective tools for (distributed) computing research. Yet we argue that human consensus experts remain essential before, during, and after the search: agents reshape the researcher's role rather than end consensus research.

papers.title: LongZero: Enhancing Long-Context Reasoning in LLMs from Zero Data
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is an effective way to strengthen the long-context reasoning of large language models (LLMs), but it needs training data that are long, diverse, challenging, and verifiable. Human annotation of such data is expensive, naturally occurring data are too scarce to sustain RL, and existing synthesis methods depend on external corpora or stronger teacher models, which become harder to obtain as the trained models get stronger. Recently, RL from zero data, in which a model learns from tasks it proposes itself, has achieved excellent performance, but existing methods target short-context tasks. Therefore, we propose $\textbf{LongZero}$, a method that lets an LLM improve its own long-context reasoning without any external data. Instead of writing questions and answers over existing documents, LongZero first has the model synthesize the question and answer with its supporting evidence in a compact structured form, and only then separately expands the evidence into a long multi-document context. LongZero combines these self-written multi-hop reasoning tasks with self-written multi-round retrieval tasks and trains the model with GRPO. We evaluate LongZero on two LLMs across five long-context reasoning benchmarks and compare it with RL on data synthesized from external corpora. Experimental results show that LongZero can generalize to real tasks, and outperforms both baselines, suggesting a viable and promising path to improving long-context reasoning of LLMs.
papers.ja_title: 外部データなしで長文脈推論力を伸ばす自己生成タスク強化学習 LongZero

papers.title: AI Mindmeld: A Latent Interconnect Protocol
papers.abstract: LLMs can act as scientific agents using tools to consult specialists and run experiments. Yet specialist information must enter their context, generally as text, images, audio or video: a bottleneck between models with rich, high-dimensional representations. We advocate direct representation exchange: a mindmeld conveying many properties, including information an LLM would not think to request. It should be extensible to new specialists, flexible across questions and tasks, and compositional across independently connected specialists without joint training. The Latent Interconnect Protocol (LIP) learns connectors mapping specialist representations into LLM internal states. Training only connectors keeps this practical as LLMs grow and evolve. We connect three protein and three small molecule specialists to Gemma 3 (4B and 12B parameters) and Kimi K2.6 (1T total, 32B active), freezing all pretrained models. Independently trained connectors provide useful information without changing the LLM or existing connectors, supporting familiar and new question types about unseen objects. We demonstrate zero-shot transfer to cross-domain tasks without joint training. Task performance and compositionality generally improve with LLM capability, with especially strong gains in zero-shot task transfer. Limitations remain: current LLMs were not trained for specialist representations as native inputs; access does not ensure reliable interpretation, integration or use in reasoning. We call on specialist developers to provide consistent representation interfaces and, especially, on LLM developers to train models to receive, combine and reason with these inputs. These efforts could expand scientific agents' information while preserving conventional tools' flexibility. Data, pretrained connectors, and code for training, evaluation and interactive inference: https://github.com/PolymathicAI/AI-Mindmeld

papers.title: Edit, Don't Imitate: Minimal-Edit On-Policy Distillation for Multimodal Reasoning
papers.abstract: Visual mathematical reasoning can fail before reasoning begins: when a vision-language model (VLM) misreads a diagram, subsequent reasoning proceeds from false premises. This perceptual bottleneck is especially pronounced in smaller models, while accurate textual descriptions can substantially narrow the gap to larger models. Because obtaining such descriptions at inference requires additional annotation or model calls, we propose minimal-edit corrective on-policy distillation. Using reference figure descriptions and verified reference solutions as training-only information, a teacher scores incorrect student rollouts under a minimal-edit objective, and only teacher-disfavored tokens contribute to the corrective loss. Correct rollouts receive task-reward reinforcement learning. This preserves on-policy supervision while avoiding full-response imitation. Across model scales, the method requires no descriptions at test time and meets or exceeds the corresponding base model supplied with a reference figure description at inference. It also improves perception-oriented performance, particularly low-level geometric perception, and transfers to external mathematics and perception benchmarks. Because the minimal-edit teacher evaluates corrections rather than generating its own solution, the method remains effective with a frozen same-size teacher, although its gains are smaller than with a larger teacher on most metrics.
papers.ja_title: 図の説明を学習のときだけ先生に見せる、最小限の書き直しによるオンポリシー蒸留
papers.summary: 小さな画像つきの言語モデルは、図を読み違えた時点で数学の問題を間違える。そこで学習のときだけ、正しい図の説明と確かめた正解を先生に見せ、生徒の間違った答案のうち先生が「ここは違う」と判断した語だけを直す。正しい答案には普通の強化学習の報酬を与える。本番では図の説明が無くても、図の説明を渡した元のモデルと同等か上回り、先生が生徒と同じ大きさで固定のままでも効いた（大きい先生の方が伸びは大きい）。
papers.why: 本番では手に入らない情報（特権情報）を先生にだけ見せ、直す語を絞るという点で DOPD と同じ問題を別の形で解いている。答案全体をまねさせないので、同じ大きさの先生でも使える。
papers.summary_en: Visual mathematical reasoning can fail before reasoning even begins: when a vision-language model misreads a diagram, subsequent reasoning proceeds from false premises, and this perceptual bottleneck is especially pronounced in smaller models, while accurate textual descriptions can substantially narrow the gap to larger models, though obtaining such descriptions at inference requires extra annotation or model calls. The authors propose minimal-edit corrective on-policy distillation: using reference figure descriptions and verified reference solutions as training-only information, a teacher scores incorrect student rollouts under a minimal-edit objective so only teacher-disfavored tokens contribute to the corrective loss, while correct rollouts receive task-reward reinforcement learning, preserving on-policy supervision without full-response imitation. Across model scales, the method requires no descriptions at test time and meets or exceeds the corresponding base model supplied with a reference figure description at inference, improves perception-oriented performance (particularly low-level geometric perception), transfers to external mathematics and perception benchmarks, and remains effective with a frozen same-size teacher, although its gains are smaller than with a larger teacher on most metrics.
papers.why_en: Shows that a frozen, same-size teacher that only evaluates and minimally corrects student rollouts, rather than generating its own full solutions, can still meaningfully improve a VLM's diagram perception without needing figure descriptions at inference time.

papers.title: EgoHand: Monocular 3D Hand Reconstruction from Egocentric Video
papers.abstract: We introduce EgoHand, a monocular 3D hand reconstruction model that achieves state-of-the-art performance on egocentric video. Central to our approach is the curation of a high-quality training corpus of 14 million images, combining synthetic data, in-the-wild video, and multi-camera motion capture to balance scene diversity and supervision quality. The model adopts SOMA-Hand as its parametric representation and processes 2D hand crops with a transformer encoder, incorporating camera cues and an auxiliary 2D branch to improve geometric consistency and image alignment. Zero-shot evaluations on HOT3D, ARCTIC, and H2O demonstrate strong out-of-domain generalization, with lower joint-position, root-translation, and acceleration errors than competing baselines at an inference latency of approximately 9.01 ms. A blinded user preference study further shows that participants favor EgoHand's reconstructed hand poses over those from Apple EgoDex and Ropedia Xperience-10M. We release the EgoHand model and source code under the OpenMDW license, allowing free commercial use of the model.
papers.ja_title: 一人称視点動画からの単眼 3D 手指姿勢推定モデル EgoHand

papers.title: SciFusion: Physics-Guided Compositional Diffusion for Multimodal 3D Scientific Image Generation
papers.abstract: Existing 3D generative approaches are typically developed for individual imaging modalities, requiring substantial modality-specific data and limiting their ability to exploit shared structure across scientific imaging domains. We present SciFusion, a multimodal framework for unified 3D scientific image generation built on a latent diffusion backbone, with two key contributions. First, we introduce a compositional conditioning scheme that factorizes each modality into domain, object, and contrast representations. Sharing these factors across related modalities enables knowledge transfer across heterogeneous imaging domains and allows the factors to be recombined at inference time to synthesize unseen domain-object-contrast compositions in a zero-shot manner. Second, we incorporate domain-specific physics-informed objectives: Fourier spectral consistency for MRI, Radon projection consistency for CT, and multislice diffraction consistency for electron microscopy, to encourage generated samples to respect modality-dependent image formation processes. Extensive experiments across 15 medical and scientific imaging modalities demonstrate that SciFusion improves generation fidelity and cross-domain generalization over modality-specific and flattened multimodal conditioning strategies, while enabling zero-shot synthesis of unseen compositions without training on those target compositions. These results demonstrate that compositional, physics-guided conditioning provides a scalable framework for unified 3D scientific image generation, particularly for emerging modalities where large-scale training data are difficult to obtain.
papers.ja_title: 物理制約付き合成拡散モデルによる科学画像生成 SciFusion

papers.title: Cambium: Participant-Built Commitment Roots for Shared Digital Infrastructure
papers.abstract: Commitment services, such as timestamping, transparency logs and provenance registries, let a party prove that it bound itself to a record without publishing the record. Today an operator runs them, or a blockchain replaces the operator at the cost of network-wide agreement on every write. We present Cambium, a permissioned peer-to-peer service in which participants build each cycle's commitment root together, so that no single party decides which inputs the root includes. Fixed-size committees certify inputs and use a recursive-doubling merge, in which disjoint groups recompute every intermediate value, to spread root construction across all participants. A successful cycle costs each node $O(c\log(n/c))$ messages for committee size $c$, and each node stores its own $O(\log(n/c))$ proof per cycle, along with the $O(n)$ membership roster. A Go prototype on AWS with $c=4$, 8-256 nodes and simulated stragglers completes cycles in 12-148 ms and verifies proofs in under 1.5 ms, and demonstrates logarithmic growth. We show that conflicting certificates identify their signers, that a proof binds a signed input to its root, and that two conflicting roots both become final only if at least a third of the nodes are Byzantine, except with probability exponentially small in the number of committees. We also set out the membership, proof-availability and exclusion questions a community deploying Cambium must answer.
papers.ja_title: 参加者全員で作るコミットメントルート基盤 Cambium

papers.title: Self-Assessment Reinforcement Learning for Search-State Awareness in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Recent advances in search agents have enabled large language models to tackle complex tasks by retrieving and synthesizing external information. However, existing search agents often lack search-state awareness, i.e., the ability to recognize what information has been obtained and what remains missing, leading to hallucinated reasoning and prematurely terminated search. To address this limitation, we propose Self-Assessment Reinforcement Learning (SARL), a reinforcement learning framework in which models learn to recognize their own search state during training and improve their search behavior accordingly, without requiring additional assessment at test time. SARL achieves this through a dual reward design that captures the corrective effect of each assessment while penalizing excessive reliance on it, jointly encouraging effective and efficient search trajectories. Under this setup, SARL achieves a 24.3% relative improvement over the strongest baseline, with average gains of 35.9% on multi-hop reasoning and 27.9% on deep research benchmarks against the strongest per-benchmark baselines. SARL further surpasses methods built on auxiliary supervision or multi-agent coordination, despite operating as a standalone RL framework with no inference-time scaffolding. Beyond final performance, SARL maintains training stability under extended search horizons, a regime where existing methods consistently degrade, enabling sustained gains as task complexity grows.

papers.title: Flow-based Spectral Kernel Learning for Nonstationary Attention
papers.abstract: Kernelized attention provides a useful perspective for understanding self-attention as a similarity-based aggregation mechanism, but existing approaches often rely on fixed or stationary kernels, limiting their ability to adapt the similarity structure to complex token interactions. In this paper, we propose flow-based spectral kernel attention (FSKA), a framework for learning expressive nonstationary attention kernels. FSKA formulates kernelized attention through spectral density learning and parameterizes the resulting bivariate spectral density with normalizing flows. This design enables flexible and regularizable kernel learning while remaining compatible with scalable linear-attention computation. We further show that expressive kernel learning enables a simplified attention design with removed query--key projections and fixed orthogonal value projections, resulting in a more parameter-efficient architecture. Controlled experiments on classification, ablation, and scalability profiling show that FSKA achieves competitive or improved performance over existing attention mechanisms, while reducing projection-related trainable parameters by approximately $40\%$--$47\%$ compared with most baselines and maintaining favorable linear-attention memory scaling. Code Available: https://github.com/ziyang18/FSKA.
papers.ja_title: 正規化流で非定常なアテンションカーネルを学習する FSKA
papers.summary: 自己注意機構(セルフアテンション)はトークン同士の似ている度合いをカーネル(類似度の計算方法)として捉えられるが、従来手法は固定された類似度の形(定常カーネル)しか使えず、複雑なトークン間の関係に対応しづらかった。FSKA はスペクトル密度(カーネルを周波数の成分に分解した表現)を正規化流というモデルで学習し、入力に応じて形が変わる非定常なカーネルを、線形アテンションの計算量を保ったまま実現する。さらにこの表現力の高さを使うとクエリ・キーの射影を省き値の射影を固定した簡易構成でも精度を保てることを示し、分類実験で既存のアテンション機構と同等以上の性能を出しつつ、射影に関わる学習パラメータを約 40〜47% 削減した。
papers.why: 線形アテンションの計算量を保ったまま表現力を上げ、かつパラメータも削れるという設計は、効率的なアテンション機構を検討する際の具体的な選択肢になる。
papers.summary_en: Kernelized attention is a useful way to understand self-attention as similarity-based aggregation, but existing approaches typically rely on fixed or stationary kernels that limit adapting similarity structure to complex token interactions. The authors propose flow-based spectral kernel attention (FSKA), which formulates kernelized attention through spectral density learning and parameterizes the resulting bivariate spectral density with normalizing flows, enabling flexible, regularizable kernel learning that stays compatible with scalable linear-attention computation; they further show that expressive kernel learning allows a simplified attention design with query-key projections removed and fixed orthogonal value projections, giving a more parameter-efficient architecture. On classification, ablation, and scalability profiling, FSKA achieves competitive or improved performance over existing attention mechanisms while reducing projection-related trainable parameters by about 40-47% compared with most baselines and maintaining favorable linear-attention memory scaling.
papers.why_en: Suggests that a sufficiently expressive, learnable attention kernel can let a model drop the usual query-key projections entirely, trading a common architectural component for a smaller, more flexible parameterization while staying linear-attention compatible.

papers.title: Can LLMs Improve Their Own Harness? A Controlled Study on ARC-AGI-3
papers.abstract: A generally intelligent system acquires new skills efficiently without requiring humans to redesign its software scaffold for every new task. Yet language models rarely act alone. A harness is a symbolic program that orchestrates calls to the model, handling perception, memory, tool use, recovery, and inference allocation on the model's behalf. ARC-AGI-3 is an interactive benchmark in which agents must explore unfamiliar environments, figure out their goals on the fly, and keep learning as they go. On it, human-steered systems already report ceiling scores across the public games, so we know effective designs exist. We ask whether frontier models can build and improve such a harness on their own. Through a fixed coding bootstrap, each model constructs a complete task harness, acts through that harness on five development games, and revises the entire codebase twice. Every version is evaluated on twenty games that never influence adaptation. We measure task performance with Relative Human Action Efficiency (RHAE), which combines level completion with action efficiency relative to human baselines, and record dollar-denominated inference cost as a practical resource measure. Across 27 lineages, harness performance ranges from zero to near-ceiling scores. Two revisions raise mean held-out RHAE by only 2.80 points (95% interval [-1.44,7.35]). Development gains overstate held-out improvement, and reductions in inference cost can come at the expense of task performance. Human-steered systems demonstrate further headroom. These findings reveal a gap between autonomous harness construction and reliable adaptation under this two-revision protocol: even strong task performance does not ensure that subsequent revisions generalize or preserve existing capabilities.
papers.ja_title: LLM は自分用の実行枠組みを自分で改善できるか(ARC-AGI-3 での検証)

papers.title: OMRC: Multipath Reliability for Direct-Connect Optical Interconnects
papers.abstract: Network failures degrade Multipath Reliable Connection (MRC) in direct-connect optical datacenters. We propose Optical MRC (OMRC), which remaps collectives and circuits, preserving 95.7% of training throughput, restoring stalled inference, and achieving 4.7x MRC's simulated bandwidth.

papers.ja_title: 光直結データセンターでの集団通信の経路を故障時に再構成する OMRC
papers.summary: 直結型光データセンターでは通信経路の故障が集団通信(複数の GPU がまとめてデータをやり取りする処理)の信頼性を落とす。OMRC は集団通信と光回路の割り当てを障害発生時に組み替える方式を提案し、訓練のスループット(処理速度)を故障前の 95.7% まで保ち、止まった推論を復旧させ、既存方式 MRC のシミュレーション帯域の 4.7 倍を達成した。
papers.why: 光直結インターコネクトでの障害耐性のある集団通信設計は、EFA や NCCL のような既存の通信層にない新しい復旧手段を示す。
papers.summary_en: Network failures degrade Multipath Reliable Connection (MRC) in direct-connect optical datacenters. The authors propose Optical MRC (OMRC), which remaps collectives and circuits around failures, preserving 95.7% of training throughput, restoring stalled inference, and achieving 4.7x MRC's simulated bandwidth.
papers.why_en: A short but concrete result for keeping collective communication and inference serving alive on direct-connect optical fabrics when links fail, with a specific throughput-retention number (95.7%) rather than only a qualitative claim.

papers.title: Future of Time Series Anomaly Detection: From Historical Review to Unified Outlook
papers.abstract: Time series anomaly detection (TSAD) is a foundational problem in data mining, aiming to identify observations that deviate significantly from nominal temporal patterns. Driven by escalating data volumes and application complexity, recent research has yielded diverse architectures, including diffusion models, state space models, and large language models (LLMs). However, existing surveys provide limited coverage of these emerging designs and lack a unified treatment of multivariate anomalies, cross-domain unified modeling, metric reliability, and contemporary evaluation challenges. To bridge these gaps, this survey delivers three core contributions: (1) We establish a refined anomaly categorization and a structured taxonomy of paradigms reflecting modern advances, comparing detection mechanisms and charting developmental trajectories across paradigms. (2) We provide an extensive analysis of evaluation methodologies and conduct comprehensive experiments to assess metric fidelity, complemented by an open-source benchmark repository encompassing algorithms, datasets, and evaluation tools. (3) We outline key open challenges, offering forward-looking perspectives on dynamic thresholding, model interpretability, zero-shot transfer, multi-modal alignment, and foundational models for time series. By addressing existing theoretical and empirical limitations, this survey establishes a coherent framework to guide future TSAD research and practical deployments.
papers.ja_title: 時系列異常検知の手法サーベイ、過去から統一的な展望まで

papers.title: Scaling Laws for Safety Probes
papers.abstract: Safety probes trained on a model's activations are a standard tool for monitoring language models in real time. Each time a new model is released or a new harm area needs to be monitored, the probe must be retrained, which requires new labels and a choice of probe architecture. Yet neither the model nor the labels tell us in advance how well the resulting probe will perform. Finding out requires training and comparing many probe configurations. In this paper, we ask whether probe performance can instead be predicted in advance from model size and the number of labels. Existing safety datasets are insufficient for this, as they are either limited in scale or already saturated. We therefore construct six new safety datasets of sufficient size and difficulty. On these datasets, we train two probe architectures on 20 base models from five model families, with 32 to $10^{6}$ labels for each model. We measure performance using probe error, defined as 1 - AUROC, where lower values are better. We find that probe error follows two simple scaling laws. First, the lowest probe error a model can reach falls as a power law in its size. Second, probe error decreases towards its floor as the number of examples increases; the slope increases as the target model size increases. Both laws hold across tasks, model families and probe architectures, and only their fitted constants differ. When fitted on the smallest models of a family, the laws predict the error of the next larger model to within 0.02 in 72% of cases. They also identify whether more labels or a larger model is the cheaper way to reach a target error in 73% of cases. Finally, they choose the probe architecture with an extra error of only 0.006 on average when they pick the worse one. These laws allow safety researchers to determine how to create the best probe for any given model and label budget.

papers.title: Random Remasking Scales Masked Diffusion Inference
papers.abstract: Masked diffusion models (MDMs) generate sequences by progressively unmasking tokens, but errors introduced during decoding are typically irreversible. Recent work has shown that iterative correction can improve sample quality, yet existing theory fails to explain this given a learned, imperfect denoiser model. We re-formulate MDM inference as a Markov chain on the clean sequence space, defined by a remask-denoise kernel that randomly re-introduces masks and then denoises. This helps us analyze the actual denoising trajectory towards the data distribution. The analysis motivates Random Remask-Denoise (R$^2$D) inference, a purely test-time, finetuning-free, reward-free procedure. To further improve performance, we propose Trajectory Correction Training (TCT), a denoiser-training procedure that exposes the model to its own errors along the generation trajectory. On logical tasks, our approach exhibits a striking near-log-linear test-time scaling, achieving over 97% accuracy on hard Sudoku puzzles and over 99% accuracy on 3-SAT. Our approach also applies to pretrained models on actual language tasks, beating iterative correction baselines and the official Q-mode accuracy of LLaDA2.1-mini on HumanEval+.

papers.ja_title: マスク拡散モデルの推論をランダムな再マスクで精度向上させる手法
papers.summary: マスク拡散モデル(トークンを少しずつ隠した状態から復元して文章を生成する仕組み)は一度確定した誤りを直せない。提案手法 R2D はランダムにマスクを戻してから再度復元する処理を繰り返すテスト時の手続きで、誤りを学習時から経験させる訓練(TCT)と組み合わせると、難しい数独で 97% 超、3-SAT で 99% 超の正解率に達し、HumanEval+ でも既存の反復修正手法や LLaDA2.1-mini の公式設定を上回った。
papers.why: 拡散型言語モデルの推論時スケーリング(計算を増やすほど精度が上がる挙動)を理論的に整理し、サービング時の品質とコストのトレードオフ設計に使える。
papers.summary_en: Masked diffusion models (MDMs) generate sequences by progressively unmasking tokens, but decoding errors are typically irreversible, and while iterative correction has been shown to improve sample quality, existing theory fails to explain this given a learned, imperfect denoiser. The authors reformulate MDM inference as a Markov chain on the clean sequence space via a remask-denoise kernel that randomly re-introduces masks and then denoises, motivating Random Remask-Denoise (R2D) inference, a purely test-time, finetuning-free, reward-free procedure, and Trajectory Correction Training (TCT), a denoiser-training procedure that exposes the model to its own errors along the generation trajectory. On logical tasks, their approach shows a striking near-log-linear test-time scaling, reaching over 97% accuracy on hard Sudoku puzzles and over 99% on 3-SAT, and on pretrained models on actual language tasks it beats iterative-correction baselines and the official Q-mode accuracy of LLaDA2.1-mini on HumanEval+.
papers.why_en: Provides a theoretical account, via a remask-denoise Markov chain, for why iterative correction helps an imperfect masked-diffusion denoiser, and turns that theory into a concrete, finetuning-free test-time procedure with near-log-linear scaling on hard logical tasks.

papers.title: AgentDP: Towards Automated Model Deployment for Heterogeneous Embedded AI Applications
papers.abstract: This paper presents AgentDP, which aims to deploy pre-trained AI models on heterogeneous embedded devices by fully automating model optimization and adaptation (O&A) with Large Language Model (LLM) agents. AgentDP not only significantly reduces human effort via automation but also enhances model inference efficacy by integrating LLMs with device-specific domain knowledge. To deliver a robust automation framework, AgentDP develops novel solutions to address three key technical challenges: 1) To help users elicit clear requirements, we propose a user requirement standardization module; 2) To mitigate the execution environment mismatch between AI models and heterogeneous embedded devices, we design an operator-aware model partition paradigm that enables different parts of the model to be efficiently executed on distinct inference engines. 3) To avoid re-searching optimization hyperparameters for new tasks, we propose a configuration reuse module that heuristically retrieves previous hyperparameter configurations for efficient reuse. Extensive experiments demonstrate that by fully automating the entire O&A process, AgentDP reduces entire model adaptation time by up to 80% compared with manual O&A while achieving higher task accuracy (more than 13% on average) than the baselines. Additionally, a comprehensive user study also exhibits the robust generalizability of AgentDP in adapting to different user requirements for heterogeneous embedded devices.
papers.ja_title: 異種組み込みデバイス向け AI モデル配置を LLM エージェントで自動化する AgentDP

papers.title: Scaling Laws for Generative Reward Models
papers.abstract: We study generative reward models (GenRMs) as online preference providers for policy optimization in creative writing. Across Qwen3 reward-model sizes from 0.6B to 14B, Thinking judges trained with GRPO have higher static Gold-label accuracy than Answer-Only judges trained with SFT. This ranking often reverses when the judges train policies through online DPO: Answer-Only rewarders yield higher peak and top-five-average policy Elo in seven of eight matched settings under a fixed, learned 32B Gold evaluator. Intermediate Thinking-judge checkpoints can also outperform later, more statically accurate checkpoints as rewarders. Sweeps over rewarder size, policy size, training duration and DPO regularization show substantial benefits from reward-model capacity, including judges larger than the policy. We analyze trajectories with evaluator-specific Elo arenas, conditional match-resampling intervals and descriptive scaling fits. These results demonstrate an evaluator-rewarder gap in the studied pipelines: fixed-distribution judging accuracy does not determine downstream optimization quality. The comparison changes judge-training objective as well as response format, and the main ranking is conditional on its learned reference rather than a universal human-quality result. A limited follow-up using a different learned judge is inconclusive overall.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 生成型報酬モデルのスケーリング則、静的な採点精度と方策改善効果はずれる
papers.summary: 創作文章タスクで、Qwen3 の報酬モデル(出力の良さを採点するモデル)を 0.6B から 14B まで変えて比較すると、GRPO で訓練した「思考あり」採点器は固定基準での採点精度は高いが、実際に方策(応答を生成するモデル)をオンライン DPO で学習させた際の強さはしばしば逆転し、8 設定中 7 設定で SFT 訓練の「回答のみ」採点器の方が高い Elo(強さの指標)を出した。
papers.why: 報酬モデルの静的な採点精度だけでは RL 後学習の最終性能を予測できないことを定量的に示し、報酬モデル選定の評価軸を見直す材料になる。
papers.summary_en: The authors study generative reward models (GenRMs) as online preference providers for policy optimization in creative writing. Across Qwen3 reward-model sizes from 0.6B to 14B, Thinking judges trained with GRPO have higher static Gold-label accuracy than Answer-Only judges trained with SFT, but this ranking often reverses when the judges train policies through online DPO: Answer-Only rewarders yield higher peak and top-five-average policy Elo in seven of eight matched settings under a fixed, learned 32B Gold evaluator, and intermediate Thinking-judge checkpoints can outperform later, more statically accurate checkpoints as rewarders. Sweeps over rewarder size, policy size, training duration, and DPO regularization show substantial benefits from reward-model capacity, including judges larger than the policy, and the authors report this as an evaluator-rewarder gap, with the main ranking conditional on its learned reference rather than a universal human-quality result; a limited follow-up using a different learned judge is inconclusive overall.
papers.why_en: Demonstrates, with explicit hedging about its own generality, that a reward model's static judging accuracy does not determine how well it works as an online optimization signal, a distinction directly relevant to anyone selecting or training reward models for RLHF-style pipelines.

review.note: 静止データでの正解率が高い判定モデルほど、実際にポリシーを最適化する報酬として優れている、とは限らないことを 8 設定中 7 設定で示した。評価指標 (静的正解率) と使い道 (報酬としての性能) を分けて測る、という評価設計の観点。著者自身も「別の judge では結論が出なかった」と限定を明記している。
review.note_en: Shows across seven of eight matched settings that a judge's static held-out accuracy does not predict how well it works as an online optimization reward, a reminder to measure an evaluator's downstream-use performance separately from its labeling accuracy; the authors themselves flag that a follow-up with a different learned judge was inconclusive.

papers.title: Gandalf: Flash Shall Not Die! Increasing Flash Storage Lifetime for KV Cache Offloading in LLM Serving
papers.abstract: KV caching reduces the serving cost of large language models (LLMs), but the growing KV cache footprint is increasingly exceeds GPU and host-memory capacity. Therefore, people use SSD to expand the KV cache storage capacity with high I/O bandwidth. However, in production LLM workload, such as multi-round conversation and LLM agents, the total amount of KV cache writes significantly exceeds SSD capacity, shortening SSD lifetime from years to months. To improve SSD lifetime, a natural solution is to reduce the KV cache writes by gating the KV cache writes via historical access patterns. However, that significantly lowers the KV cache hit rate (and increase the LLM serving cost) since KV caches from different attention types might have identical historical access pattern but different future access patterns. Our insight is that, to reduce KV cache writes without hurting KV cache hit rate, one need to not only consider the access pattern, but also application-level information such as the attention type of KV cache. Leveraging this observation, we propose Gandalf , the first SSD KV cache offloading system with SSD life time awareness. Gandalf prioritize the admission of full-attention KV cache into SSD over the cache generated by other types of attention, which significantly increases SSD lifetime without sacrificing cache hit rate. Our evaluation shows that Gandalf extends the SSD lifetime by 7.3X on average, while having negligible impact on cache hit rate across multiple workload traces and wide range of hardware capacity. Gandalf design can be extended to other flash-based storage, such as High Bandwidth Flash (HBF).
papers.ja_title: KV キャッシュの SSD オフロードで寿命を 7.3 倍延ばす Gandalf
papers.summary: LLM サービングでは KV キャッシュ(過去の計算結果を覚えておく領域)を SSD に逃がして容量を増やすが、書き込み量が多いマルチターン対話やエージェント利用では SSD の寿命が数年から数か月に縮む。Gandalf は注意機構の種類(フルアテンションか他方式か)という応用層の情報を使って、将来も使われやすいキャッシュだけを優先的に SSD に書き込むことで、キャッシュのヒット率をほぼ落とさずに SSD 寿命を平均 7.3 倍に延ばした。
papers.why: SSD 耐久性をハードウェア仕様ではなくアプリケーション層の情報(アテンション種別)で制御するという発想は、KV キャッシュ階層設計のコスト計算に直結する。
papers.summary_en: KV caching reduces LLM serving cost, but the growing KV cache footprint increasingly exceeds GPU and host-memory capacity, so people use SSDs to expand KV cache storage with high I/O bandwidth; however, in production workloads such as multi-round conversation and LLM agents, total KV cache writes significantly exceed SSD capacity, shortening SSD lifetime from years to months. Gating writes by historical access pattern lowers hit rate because different attention types can share the same historical pattern but have different future patterns; the authors' insight is that reducing writes without hurting hit rate requires considering application-level information such as attention type alongside access pattern, leading to Gandalf, the first SSD KV cache offloading system with SSD lifetime awareness, which prioritizes admitting full-attention KV cache into SSD over KV cache from other attention types. Their evaluation shows Gandalf extends SSD lifetime by 7.3x on average with negligible impact on cache hit rate across multiple workload traces and a wide range of hardware capacities, and the design can extend to other flash-based storage such as High Bandwidth Flash (HBF).
papers.why_en: Identifies attention type, not just access-pattern history, as the missing signal for deciding which KV cache blocks are worth writing to SSD, giving a large (7.3x) measured SSD-lifetime improvement with negligible hit-rate cost.

papers.title: Joules-to-GDP: How Much Economic Value Do AI Systems Produce per Unit of Energy?
papers.abstract: An AI system can produce more economically valuable work while delivering less value for the energy it consumes. We therefore ask: How much economic value does an AI system create per unit of energy consumed? We formalize economic value in two ways: (1) net dollar value, the output's dollar value minus AI-system execution cost, and (2) time saving, the expert's completion time minus the AI system's completion time. Dividing each by measured end-to-end energy yields Net Value per Joule (NVJ) and Time Saving per Joule (TSJ), reported in USD/MJ and hours/MJ. We study 220 public GDPval tasks across 44 occupations, serving five open-weight models locally and evaluating four accelerator types. First, the occupation groups where AI systems succeed most often, deliver the greatest dollar value, or save the most time do not necessarily provide the greatest economic return per joule. For example, among the tested tasks, engineering work delivers about 10% more net dollar value per task than software development. Yet software development delivers about 27% more net value per joule. Second, GLM 5.2 delivers the highest average net dollar value, at $72.27 per task using 0.430 MJ, equivalent in energy to about four hours of active laptop use. By contrast, Gemma 4 31B delivers 56% of that net dollar value using just 23% of the energy, achieving approximately 2.5 times the NVJ and 2.8 times the TSJ. Third, across four single-accelerator deployments, Qwen3.6-27B's NVJ varies by a factor of 4.32 and TSJ by 9.27, with B200 leading both. Additionally, one and eight H100s deliver similar net dollar value, but eight reduce completion time by 22% at 3.24 times the energy. Our framework makes output value and expert time saving under an energy budget explicit objectives for improving models, accelerators, and software, while offering a new basis for assessing AI's potential economic effect on occupational work.
papers.ja_title: AI システムが消費エネルギー 1 ジュールあたりに生み出す経済価値を測る Joules-to-GDP
papers.summary: 44 職種・220 タスクの GDPval ベンチマークで 5 つのオープンモデルを 4 種類のアクセラレータ(GPU 等の計算装置)上で実際に動かし、消費エネルギー 1 メガジュールあたりの金額価値(NVJ)と時間節約(TSJ)を測定した。GLM 5.2 は 1 タスクあたり 72.27 ドルの価値を 0.430 メガジュール(ノート PC を約 4 時間使う量に相当)で生んだが、Gemma 4 31B はその 56% の価値をわずか 23% のエネルギーで達成しエネルギー効率は約 2.5〜2.8 倍高かった。Qwen3.6-27B を単一アクセラレータで動かす場合、エネルギー効率はアクセラレータの種類で最大 4.32 倍(価値)・9.27 倍(時間節約)変わり、H100 を 8 枚使う構成は 1 枚構成より完了時間を 22% 短縮する一方で消費エネルギーは 3.24 倍になった。
papers.why: モデルやアクセラレータの選定をコストや速度だけでなく消費電力あたりの経済価値で比較する軸を示し、サービング基盤のハードウェア選定に使える実測値を提供する。
papers.summary_en: The authors ask how much economic value an AI system creates per unit of energy, formalizing value as net dollar value (output value minus execution cost) and time saving (expert completion time minus AI completion time), each divided by measured end-to-end energy to give Net Value per Joule (NVJ) and Time Saving per Joule (TSJ) in USD/MJ and hours/MJ. Studying 220 public GDPval tasks across 44 occupations, serving five open-weight models locally on four accelerator types, they find that the occupation groups where AI succeeds most often, delivers the greatest dollar value, or saves the most time do not necessarily give the greatest return per joule: engineering work delivers about 10% more net dollar value per task than software development, yet software development delivers about 27% more net value per joule. GLM 5.2 delivers the highest average net dollar value ($72.27 per task using 0.430 MJ), while Gemma 4 31B delivers 56% of that value using only 23% of the energy (about 2.5x the NVJ and 2.8x the TSJ), and across four single-accelerator deployments Qwen3.6-27B's NVJ varies by a factor of 4.32 and TSJ by 9.27, with B200 leading both; one and eight H100s deliver similar net dollar value, but eight reduce completion time by 22% at 3.24 times the energy.
papers.why_en: Introduces an explicit per-joule economic-value metric (NVJ/TSJ) and shows with measured numbers that task success rate, dollar value, and energy efficiency are three different axes that can rank occupations, models, and accelerators in opposite orders.

papers.title: Building Presentation Intelligence for High-Quality Slide Generation
papers.abstract: PowerPoint presentations (PPTs) are a dominant medium for communication across diverse domains, yet high-quality PPT generation still depends heavily on labor-intensive human effort. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) for agentic tasks have created both new opportunities and challenges (Chen et al., 2026) for automatic PPT generation. In this work, we present a unified training framework for automatic PPT generation toward presentation intelligence, integrating cross-validated data synthesis, guided teacher enhancement, and verifiable reward optimization. We first construct a cross-validated pipeline for data synthesis, with explicit control over both difficulty and validity. We then develop a teacher-enhancement framework grounded in rules and prior knowledge to substantially strengthen the instructional capacity of teacher models. Building on this, we further improve supervised fine-tuning (SFT) through a mixed-teacher strategy and a lightweight outcome-driven trajectory filtering method. Finally, based on the resulting SFT models, we introduce a suite of verifiable aesthetic metrics together with a GRPO-based reinforcement learning framework to optimize slide-level visual attributes beyond text-only supervision. Experiments show that our enhanced SFT pipeline improves Qwen-3.6-27B and Qwen-3.6-35B-A3B by 7.45 and 9.35 points on PresentBench, respectively, surpassing GLM-5.2 while maintaining strong generalization. Reinforcement learning further improves performance across five aesthetic dimensions, compensating for the limitations of SFT in visual refinement. Overall, the results demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework for high-quality PPT generation.
papers.ja_title: 高品質なスライド自動生成のための学習フレームワーク

papers.title: OpenAttention: One Percent Is Enough with Tail Proxies
papers.abstract: Sparse attention reads only a small subset of the key-value cache, and how to treat the unread tail remains a key challenge. Discarding the tail biases the output, and sampling it as previous approaches do fails at reads of 5% and below, where the tail likely holds heavy hitters the selector missed. Our key observation is that the simplest possible proxy, one token that folds the entire tail into its count-aware mean, already yields lower output error than a sample at every read behind a practical selector. We further show in closed form that at low reads sampling nearly doubles the weight error of discarding while a single proxy stays below it. Building on these findings, we explore approximating the dense attention distribution with a few proxies that target the tail. We propose OpenAttention, a pipeline of clustering, ErrorGate and top-k selection followed by a count-aware mean proxy. To implement clustering and selection both efficiently and effectively, we design training-free Query-Geometry Clustering (QGC) and a Query-Geometry Selector (QGS), which compress the keys while respecting the query directions. Additionally, unlike prior methods that rank clusters by centroid alone, ErrorGate allocates the exact read by the estimated weight error of each cluster. On RULER-32K HARD with Llama-3.1-8B, OpenAttention retains 99% of dense accuracy at a 1% read. It also achieves state-of-the-art accuracy across models, context lengths and datasets. Our customized attention kernel for OpenAttention runs the decode attention stage 10$\times$ faster than dense attention at a 1% read.
papers.ja_title: KV キャッシュの読み込みを 1% に抑えつつ密な注意に匹敵する OpenAttention
papers.summary: スパースアテンション(KV キャッシュの一部だけを読む注意機構)では読まなかった残り(テイル)の扱いが課題で、単純に捨てると出力が偏り、サンプリングも読み込み率 5% 以下では精度が崩れる。OpenAttention はテイル全体を 1 個の代表ベクトルに要約する手法とクラスタリング・選択アルゴリズムを組み合わせ、Llama-3.1-8B の RULER-32K HARD で読み込み率 1% でも密な注意の精度の 99% を維持し、専用カーネルによってデコード時の注意計算を密な注意より 10 倍高速化した。
papers.why: KV キャッシュの読み込み率をさらに切り詰めてもほぼ精度を落とさない具体的な設計(テイルの平均代表ベクトル)を示し、スパースアテンション実装の省メモリ化に直結する。
papers.summary_en: Sparse attention reads only a small subset of the KV cache, and how to treat the unread tail remains a key challenge: discarding it biases the output, while sampling it fails at reads of 5% and below because the tail likely holds heavy hitters the selector missed. The authors observe that a single proxy token, which folds the entire tail into its count-aware mean, already yields lower output error than sampling at every read behind a practical selector, and show in closed form that at low reads sampling nearly doubles the weight error of discarding while a single proxy stays below it; building on this, they propose OpenAttention, a pipeline of training-free Query-Geometry Clustering (QGC) and a Query-Geometry Selector (QGS) that compress keys while respecting query directions, followed by ErrorGate, which allocates the exact read by each cluster's estimated weight error, and top-k selection with a count-aware mean proxy. On RULER-32K HARD with Llama-3.1-8B, OpenAttention retains 99% of dense accuracy at a 1% read, achieves state-of-the-art accuracy across models, context lengths, and datasets, and its customized decode attention kernel runs 10x faster than dense attention at a 1% read.
papers.why_en: Gives a closed-form argument plus empirical evidence that a single mean proxy for the unread KV-cache tail beats sampling at the very low read rates (5% and below) where sparse attention matters most, with a concrete 10x decode kernel speedup at a 1% read.

papers.title: CANNBot-CAKE: Collaborative Agentic Kernel Evolution for Ascend NPU
papers.abstract: Efficient custom operators are essential for modern deep learning workloads, yet developing high-performance kernels for Ascend NPUs remains slow, expert-intensive, and difficult to automate. Although AI agents now approach expert performance on GPU kernel benchmarks, current models remain less capable of generating AscendC kernels for NPUs, potentially reflecting the relative scarcity of relevant training data. We thus present CAKE, a CANN-native system for deployable custom operators that combines adaptive multi-DSL routing, separate Generation and Evolution modes, and reviewed knowledge reuse through CAKE Book and a Self-Evolving Agent. On 53 CANN-Bench v1.1 operators on Ascend 950PR, CAKE's aggregated results achieve $100\%$ case pass rate on the standard set (1,060/1,060) and $98.28\%$ on the hidden set (4,167/4,240), with an overall mean score of 78.63 out of 100 and an average performance speedup of $1.334\times$ over the baseline. Evolution then pushes correct operators further: EngramGateFusion cuts aggregate device time by $46.6\%$ over 20 rounds and roughly halves the mean roofline gap. These results offer a practical path toward closing Ascend's AI-for-kernel capability gap.
papers.ja_title: Ascend NPU 向けカーネルを AI エージェントが自律生成・進化させる CANNBot-CAKE
papers.summary: Ascend NPU(Huawei の AI 専用チップ)向けの高性能カーネルは専門知識が必要で自動化が難しく、GPU 向けと比べて AI エージェントの実装能力も学習データ不足で劣る。CAKE は複数の言語ルーティングと生成・進化の 2 モード、過去知識の再利用を組み合わせたシステムで、53 個の CANN-Bench v1.1 演算子に対して標準セットで合格率 100%、隠しセットで 98.28% を達成し、ベースラインに対して平均 1.334 倍の高速化を実現、進化フェーズでは EngramGateFusion のデバイス時間を 20 ラウンドで 46.6% 削減した。
papers.why: GPU 以外のアクセラレータ(Ascend NPU)向けカーネル生成を自動化する具体的な成功例を示し、ハードウェア多様化が進む中でのカーネル開発の省力化手段になる。
papers.summary_en: Efficient custom operators are essential for deep learning workloads, but developing high-performance kernels for Ascend NPUs remains slow, expert-intensive, and hard to automate; while AI agents now approach expert performance on GPU kernel benchmarks, current models are less capable of generating AscendC kernels, potentially reflecting the relative scarcity of relevant training data. The authors present CAKE, a CANN-native system for deployable custom operators combining adaptive multi-DSL routing, separate Generation and Evolution modes, and reviewed knowledge reuse through a CAKE Book and a Self-Evolving Agent. On 53 CANN-Bench v1.1 operators on Ascend 950PR, CAKE achieves a 100% case pass rate on the standard set (1,060/1,060) and 98.28% on the hidden set (4,167/4,240), with an overall mean score of 78.63 out of 100 and an average performance speedup of 1.334x over the baseline, and its Evolution mode further cuts EngramGateFusion's aggregate device time by 46.6% over 20 rounds, roughly halving the mean roofline gap.
papers.why_en: A concrete, benchmarked attempt to close the AI-for-kernel-generation gap on Ascend NPUs, where current models lag GPU kernel-generation performance, with large measured pass rates and an iterative evolution step that further shrinks the roofline gap.

papers.title: RIFT: KV Cache Compression for Draft Models with Complementary Compressibility Training
papers.abstract: Speculative decoding is a popular decode acceleration method. As such, it is particularly relevant to long-output generation, which requires an increasingly large KV cache. KV cache compression offers a way to constrain costs in long-context drafting. However, compression methods that focus on prefill information can lose relevance as the output length grows. We term this phenomenon decode staleness and show that it degrades draft model accuracy under selection-based KV cache compression. We introduce RIFT, a family of selection-based KV cache compression strategies that balance prefill information and recent generated tokens. We show that refreshing the KV cache selection during token generation significantly improves the drafter's quality at the cost of additional decode latency. To alleviate the refresh costs, we propose an adaptive KV refresh strategy that reduces the number of score calculations while retaining the drafter's quality. We further demonstrate how a compressibility-driven drafter training phase, based on sparse attention masks, can improve the drafter's quality under a compressed KV cache. Combined with compressibility training, RIFT enables Qwen3.5-4B, drafting for Qwen3.5-122B, to retain over 98% of its full-cache acceptance length on 32K-token inputs, 4K-token outputs, and an 8K-token KV cache budget.
papers.ja_title: ドラフトモデルの KV キャッシュ圧縮で投機的デコーディングの劣化を防ぐ RIFT
papers.summary: 投機的デコーディング(小さなドラフトモデルが候補トークンを先読みし、大きな本体モデルが検証して生成を高速化する手法)では、出力が長くなるほどドラフトモデルの KV キャッシュ圧縮の精度が落ちる「デコード陳腐化」が起きる。RIFT は入力部分の情報と直近生成トークンの情報をバランスさせてキャッシュを選び直す方式と、圧縮に強いドラフトモデルを作る訓練法を組み合わせ、Qwen3.5-4B が Qwen3.5-122B のドラフトを務める構成で、32K トークン入力・4K トークン出力・8K トークンのキャッシュ予算でも、圧縮なしの場合の受理長(本体モデルに採用される候補の長さ)の 98% 以上を維持した。
papers.why: 投機的デコーディングの高速化効果を長い出力でも保つための KV キャッシュ管理手法で、長文生成サービングのコスト削減に直接使える。
papers.summary_en: Speculative decoding is a popular decode acceleration method, particularly relevant to long-output generation where the KV cache grows large; KV cache compression constrains costs in long-context drafting, but methods focused on prefill information can lose relevance as output length grows, a phenomenon the authors term decode staleness, which degrades draft model accuracy under selection-based KV cache compression. They introduce RIFT, a family of selection-based KV cache compression strategies that balance prefill information with recently generated tokens, showing that refreshing the KV cache selection during generation significantly improves drafter quality at the cost of additional decode latency, and propose an adaptive KV refresh strategy that reduces the number of score calculations while retaining drafter quality, plus a compressibility-driven drafter training phase based on sparse attention masks. Combined with compressibility training, RIFT enables Qwen3.5-4B, drafting for Qwen3.5-122B, to retain over 98% of its full-cache acceptance length on 32K-token inputs, 4K-token outputs, and an 8K-token KV cache budget.
papers.why_en: Names and addresses 'decode staleness,' a specific failure where prefill-focused KV cache compression degrades a speculative-decoding draft model as output length grows, with a concrete adaptive refresh strategy to control the resulting latency cost.

papers.title: SARIA: Persistence-Aware KV Caching with Coordinated DRAM--SSD Reload for LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Multi-turn LLM agents usually reuse long context prefixes, making key value (KV) caching crucial for reducing prefill latency. SSDs provide a low-cost extension to limited DRAM capacity but introduce two key challenges. Eagerly persisting all KV cache blocks incurs substantial write traffic and rapidly consumes finite SSD endurance. Meanwhile, the small number of SSDs provisioned in typical GPU servers limits aggregate reload bandwidth, making SSD-resident KV cache much slower to retrieve than that in DRAM and inflating prefill latency.
