We present \textsc{Saria} (Selective Admission and Reload for Inference Acceleration), a KV caching system that jointly manages DRAM and SSD by exploiting the session-level temporal locality of LLM agents to reduce SSD writes and accelerate cache reload. On the write path, \textsc{Saria} uses eviction and reuse history to selectively persist KV cache blocks that exhibit reuse opportunities beyond their DRAM residency, avoiding unnecessary writes for KV cache already hosted in DRAM. On the read path, \textsc{Saria} promotes selected SSD-hit KV cache blocks from GPU memory into DRAM after prefill, allowing subsequent reuse within the same session to reduce SSD read traffic while limiting DRAM contention. A transfer coordinator paces DRAM reads while SSD transfers are active, allowing both paths to make progress and efficiently share GPU ingress bandwidth. We implement \textsc{Saria} on LMCache MP and evaluate it using workloads from TraceLab and WEKA, covering both full-attention and hybrid-attention models. The results show that \textsc{Saria} reduces SSD writes by 57.1--58.9\% compared with popular full duplicate caching and the mean time to first token (TTFT) by 42.3--79.7\% over DRAM-only caching.
papers.ja_title: DRAM と SSD を協調させて LLM エージェントの KV キャッシュを管理する SARIA
papers.summary: 複数ターンにわたる LLM エージェントは長い文脈の前半部分を繰り返し使うため KV キャッシュの再利用が重要だが、全部を SSD に書き込むと寿命を消耗し、SSD 台数が少ないサーバではキャッシュの読み出しも遅くなる。SARIA は利用履歴から再利用されそうなキャッシュだけを選んで SSD に書き込み、SSD から読み戻したキャッシュを DRAM に昇格させて次回の再利用を速くする仕組みで、全件をそのまま複製する方式と比べて SSD への書き込みを 57.1〜58.9% 削減し、DRAM のみのキャッシュと比べて応答開始までの時間(TTFT)を 42.3〜79.7% 短縮した。
papers.why: DRAM と SSD の 2 階層キャッシュをセッション単位の局所性に基づいて協調管理する設計は、エージェント向けサービング基盤の KV キャッシュ階層構築の参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Multi-turn LLM agents usually reuse long context prefixes, making KV caching crucial for reducing prefill latency; SSDs extend limited DRAM capacity at low cost but eagerly persisting all KV cache blocks incurs heavy write traffic that rapidly consumes finite SSD endurance, while the small number of SSDs in typical GPU servers limits aggregate reload bandwidth, making SSD-resident KV cache much slower to retrieve than DRAM-resident cache. The authors present Saria, which jointly manages DRAM and SSD by exploiting the session-level temporal locality of LLM agents: on the write path it uses eviction and reuse history to selectively persist only KV cache blocks with reuse opportunities beyond their DRAM residency, and on the read path it promotes selected SSD-hit blocks from GPU memory into DRAM after prefill for later reuse, with a transfer coordinator pacing DRAM reads while SSD transfers are active so both paths share GPU ingress bandwidth. Implemented on LMCache MP and evaluated with TraceLab and WEKA workloads covering full-attention and hybrid-attention models, Saria reduces SSD writes by 57.1-58.9% compared with popular full duplicate caching and cuts mean time to first token by 42.3-79.7% over DRAM-only caching.
papers.why_en: Uses session-level reuse history, rather than treating DRAM and SSD as simply two tiers of the same cache, to selectively decide what is worth writing to SSD and what is worth promoting back to DRAM, directly addressing both SSD endurance and reload-bandwidth limits for agentic workloads.

papers.title: ValuSpec: Plug-and-Play Candidate Valuation before Target Verification for Tree-Based Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract: Tree-based speculative decoding accelerates large language model inference by verifying multiple candidate branches in parallel. However, in practical serving scenarios, similar requests repeatedly induce overlapping candidate branches. While retrieval-based methods mitigate this by reusing historical drafts, the resulting candidate trees often contain many low-quality branches as the candidate tree grows, which reduces verification efficiency and wastes target-side computation. To address this, we propose ValuSpec, a plug-and-play candidate valuation mechanism that filters low-quality branches from a supplied candidate tree before expensive target-side verification. ValuSpec introduces transfer-based supervision to align filtering with the target model's behavior. A filtering threshold is estimated from the target model's greedy trajectories on a calibration split, without any parameter training. The target model then verifies the filtered tree under the output-identical greedy rule, so accepted tokens are guaranteed to match standard autoregressive decoding exactly. Experimental results on HumanEval, GSM8K, Dolly, and SpecBench show that, in our main evaluation, ValuSpec achieves up to 2.38x end-to-end speedup in retrieval-based tree settings. Furthermore, integrating ValuSpec into the EAGLE-3 dynamic tree framework yields up to 2.78x end-to-end speedup without modifying its tree construction strategy, demonstrating that ValuSpec serves as a generally applicable and plug-and-play candidate valuation module.
papers.ja_title: 木構造の投機的デコーディングで候補分岐を事前にふるい落とす ValuSpec
papers.summary: 木構造の投機的デコーディングは複数の候補分岐を並列に検証して高速化するが、似たリクエストが繰り返されると過去の候補を再利用した木に低品質な分岐が増え、検証の無駄が生じる。ValuSpec は本体モデルの挙動に合わせて学習なしで閾値を決める仕組みで低品質な分岐を事前に除去し、HumanEval・GSM8K・Dolly・SpecBench での評価で検索ベースの木構造設定で最大 2.38 倍、EAGLE-3 の動的木構造に組み込むと木の構築方法を変えずに最大 2.78 倍の高速化を達成した。
papers.why: 既存の投機的デコーディング手法に後付けできる軽量なフィルタとして動作する点が実装上扱いやすく、サービング基盤への組み込みコストが低い高速化策になる。
papers.summary_en: Tree-based speculative decoding accelerates LLM inference by verifying multiple candidate branches in parallel, but in practical serving, similar requests repeatedly induce overlapping candidate branches, and while retrieval-based methods reuse historical drafts, the resulting candidate trees accumulate many low-quality branches as they grow, reducing verification efficiency and wasting target-side computation. The authors propose ValuSpec, a plug-and-play candidate valuation mechanism that filters low-quality branches from a supplied candidate tree before expensive target-side verification, using transfer-based supervision to align filtering with the target model's behavior and estimating a filtering threshold from the target model's greedy trajectories on a calibration split without any parameter training; the target model then verifies the filtered tree under an output-identical greedy rule, so accepted tokens are guaranteed to match standard autoregressive decoding exactly. On HumanEval, GSM8K, Dolly, and SpecBench, ValuSpec achieves up to 2.38x end-to-end speedup in retrieval-based tree settings, and integrating it into the EAGLE-3 dynamic tree framework yields up to 2.78x end-to-end speedup without modifying its tree construction strategy, demonstrating it as a generally applicable, plug-and-play module.
papers.why_en: A training-free, calibration-only filtering step that can be dropped into existing tree-based speculative decoding pipelines, including EAGLE-3, while provably preserving output-identical greedy decoding.

papers.title: Drift Says When, Budget Says How Much: Rate-Controlled KV Re-selection for Long-Form Multimodal Generation
papers.abstract: KV cache compression for multimodal LLMs usually selects the visual tokens to keep once, at prefill, and reuses that selection for the whole generation. We show that this one-shot selection is severely limited on long-form generation: on detailed image description, even an oracle that selects with the attention of the uncompressed answer reaches only 0.44-0.52 ROUGE-L agreement with the uncompressed output, because the evidence the model reads moves as the description unfolds. Re-selecting whenever attention drifts out of the kept set is the natural remedy, but we find that a fixed drift threshold fails systematically: drift magnitudes are not comparable across samples, so low-drift samples are almost never refreshed although they benefit the most. We propose Rate-Controlled Refresh (RCR), which lets drift decide when and where to re-select while a per-sample controller regulates how often, combined with a low-rank drift detector, candidate-restricted re-selection, and a decision that stays on the GPU. With one setting for all models and tasks, RCR outperforms the per-step retrieval method InfiniGen by 1.6-3.8 ROUGE-L points on five of six model-task settings with no significant difference on the sixth, while staying within 1.7 points of exact per-step re-selection, with comparable estimated data movement per step and a 4x smaller GPU-resident detector. On DetailCaps, drift-chosen timing beats random timing at the same refresh rate and periodic timing even at a higher rate, by 2.0-5.0 points. On pre-registered video description, where drift is homogeneous across samples, RCR is on par with InfiniGen on Qwen2-VL and exceeds it on Qwen3-VL but no longer beats a fixed threshold at the nearest tested rates, consistent with the diagnosis; object-level evaluation shows that RCR achieves higher object F1 against the uncompressed output than InfiniGen on two of three models.
papers.ja_title: 注意のズレに応じて KV キャッシュの再選択頻度を制御するマルチモーダル生成手法 RCR
papers.summary: マルチモーダル LLM の KV キャッシュ圧縮は生成開始時に画像トークンを 1 回だけ選んで使い回すが、詳細な画像説明のような長文生成では理想的な選び方でも非圧縮出力との一致度が ROUGE-L で 0.44〜0.52 にしか届かず、途中で注意が移動していくことが分かった。RCR は注意のズレで再選択の「いつ・どこ」を決め、サンプルごとの制御器で「どのくらいの頻度か」を調整する方式で、既存の逐次再選択手法 InfiniGen を 6 設定中 5 設定で ROUGE-L 1.6〜3.8 点上回り、完全な逐次再選択との差を 1.7 点以内に抑えつつ GPU 上の検出器を 4 分の 1 サイズにした。
papers.why: KV キャッシュの再選択を固定スケジュールからズレに応じた動的制御に変える設計は、マルチモーダルサービングでの精度とコストの両立に使える。
papers.summary_en: KV cache compression for multimodal LLMs usually selects visual tokens to keep once, at prefill, and reuses that selection for the whole generation, but the authors show this one-shot selection is severely limited on long-form generation: on detailed image description, even an oracle that selects with the attention of the uncompressed answer reaches only 0.44-0.52 ROUGE-L agreement with the uncompressed output, because the evidence the model reads moves as the description unfolds. Re-selecting whenever attention drifts out of the kept set is the natural remedy, but a fixed drift threshold fails systematically because drift magnitudes are not comparable across samples, so low-drift samples are almost never refreshed even though they benefit the most; the authors propose Rate-Controlled Refresh (RCR), which lets drift decide when and where to re-select while a per-sample controller regulates how often, combined with a low-rank drift detector, candidate-restricted re-selection, and a GPU-resident decision. With one fixed setting across all models and tasks, RCR outperforms the per-step retrieval method InfiniGen by 1.6-3.8 ROUGE-L points on five of six model-task settings (no significant difference on the sixth) while staying within 1.7 points of exact per-step re-selection, using a 4x smaller GPU-resident detector; on DetailCaps, drift-chosen timing beats random and periodic timing by 2.0-5.0 points, though on pre-registered video description, where drift is homogeneous across samples, RCR matches InfiniGen on one model, exceeds it on another, but no longer beats a fixed threshold at the nearest tested rates, consistent with the authors' own diagnosis.
papers.why_en: Diagnoses why one-shot KV token selection fails on long-form multimodal generation (an oracle still caps at 0.44-0.52 ROUGE-L agreement) and why a fixed drift threshold under-refreshes exactly the samples that need it most, then reports its own method's limits transparently on a pre-registered video task where the diagnosis predicts it should not help.

papers.title: DIAL: Steerable Language Models with Distilled Instruction-Adherence Levels
papers.abstract: When a user says "Keep it short", how short should the LLM's response be? More generally, users and applications require different levels of instruction adherence, but prompting does not reliably provide fine-grained control over them. We therefore study "steerable language models" that provide fine-grained numerical control over the degree to which models follow general instructions specified in text. However, existing approaches do not jointly offer fine-grained control, efficiency, and scalability across diverse instructions. To address this gap, we introduce DIAL (Distilled Instruction-Adherence Levels) to achieve all three properties. For fine-grained control, we perform classifier-free guidance (CFG) with a frozen LLM to provide training signals for on-policy distillation of instruction adherence at different levels. For efficiency, we design a lightweight steering adapter that uses a classifier over the LLM's hidden states to compute a closed-form steering edit. The classifier adaptively sets the steering magnitude at each token based on the target adherence level, while accounting for the geometry of the LLM's hidden states to preserve response coherence. For scalability, the classifier is text-conditioned, allowing a shared adapter to support new instructions without per-instruction fitting, and training requires only instruction and request text. Evaluation across multiple LLM families shows that DIAL achieves a competitive balance between concept expression and response fluency, with concept scores increasing monotonically across adherence levels. We introduce SteerIF, an instruction-only dataset of 98, 625 concept, persona, verifiable, and descriptive instructions. When trained on SteerIF, DIAL provides fine-grained control over personas and, when combined with prompting, improves verifiable instruction following.
papers.ja_title: 指示への従いやすさの度合いを細かく制御できる言語モデル DIAL

papers.title: RheOPT: Few-Shot Non-Newtonian Flow Prediction via Newtonian Pretraining of RheOFormer
papers.abstract: Despite advances in numerical methods, non-Newtonian flow simulations remain computationally expensive because velocity and stress must be advanced together through rate- and history-dependent constitutive dynamics. Neural-operator surrogates reduce inference cost after training, but their training data require the same expensive simulations they aim to replace, making data-efficient learning essential when only a few non-Newtonian simulations can be afforded. Here, we introduce the Rheological Operator Pretrained Transformer (RheOPT), which pretrains a transformer-based neural operator on inexpensive Newtonian simulations and fine-tunes it on a small number of non-Newtonian samples. Rather than transferring the Newtonian constitutive response itself, RheOPT reuses geometry-conditioned transport structure that remains useful after the stress model changes. We evaluate RheOPT in two geometry-matched settings: a $4{:}1$ contraction channel for Giesekus, Oldroyd-B, and Bingham fluids, and the oscillatory wake behind a triangular obstacle for Oldroyd-B flow. In the contraction, Newtonian pretraining substantially improves few-shot prediction, and a model fine-tuned on four target samples can match or exceed a from-scratch model trained on four times as many. This benefit is reliable under reversible instance normalization (RevIN) but dataset dependent under Global normalization, a difference we trace to the dynamic range of each fluid's velocity and stress fields. In the wake, where relative $L_2$ error alone cannot verify that vortex shedding is recovered, phase-insensitive diagnostics show that pretraining recovers the shedding frequency and wake fluctuation amplitude that are suppressed by the from-scratch model in the few-shot regime. Overall, RheOPT establishes Newtonian simulation as a physically grounded pretraining source for data-efficient non-Newtonian operator learning.
papers.ja_title: ニュートン流体での事前学習を使う非ニュートン流れの少数データ予測 RheOPT

papers.title: Rethinking Sequence Compression with Test-time Regression
papers.abstract: Sequence compression is a fundamental operation and a critical information bottleneck in efficient language and multimodal models, and yet prevailing approaches based on pooling or learned projections remain underperforming. We revisit sequence compression through the lens of test-time regression: input tokens define a regression problem whose fitted coefficients form the compressed representation. Importantly, the regression problem is learned end-to-end via backpropagation, while its coefficients are computed efficiently in closed form during the forward pass. This leads to TTR-Compressor, a general alternative to conventional pooling and projection-based compression. We evaluate TTR-Compressor as the compressor for block-wise sparse attention and the visual token merger for multimodal large language models. On block-wise sparse attention, TTR-Compressor improves RULER performance over attention-based compressors by a large margin. For visual token merging, it consistently outperforms the standard MLP merger and matches its performance with 55.6% fewer visual tokens. These results establish test-time regression as an effective primitive for sequence compression in efficient language and multimodal models.
papers.ja_title: テスト時回帰で系列を圧縮する TTR-Compressor
papers.summary: 効率的な言語・マルチモーダルモデルでは入力系列をまとめて圧縮する処理が重要だが、プーリングや学習済み射影を使う既存手法は性能が伸び悩んでいた。TTR-Compressor は入力トークンを回帰問題として捉え、フォワード計算中に閉じた式で求まる回帰の係数を圧縮表現として使う手法で、ブロック単位のスパースアテンションでは既存のアテンション型圧縮器より RULER の性能を大きく上回り、マルチモーダルモデルの視覚トークン統合では標準的な MLP による統合と同等の性能をトークン数 55.6% 減らして達成した。
papers.why: プーリングや射影に代わる圧縮の基本要素として、スパースアテンションや視覚トークン統合など複数の圧縮用途に転用できる汎用的な手法を示している。
papers.summary_en: Sequence compression is a fundamental operation and critical information bottleneck in efficient language and multimodal models, yet prevailing pooling- or learned-projection-based approaches remain underperforming. The authors revisit sequence compression through test-time regression, where input tokens define a regression problem whose fitted coefficients form the compressed representation, learned end-to-end via backpropagation while the coefficients are computed efficiently in closed form during the forward pass, yielding TTR-Compressor as a general alternative to conventional pooling and projection-based compression. Evaluated as the compressor for block-wise sparse attention, TTR-Compressor improves RULER performance over attention-based compressors by a large margin, and as the visual token merger for multimodal LLMs it consistently outperforms the standard MLP merger and matches its performance using 55.6% fewer visual tokens.
papers.why_en: Reframes sequence compression as a closed-form regression fit at each forward pass rather than a learned pooling or projection, giving a drop-in replacement that improves both sparse-attention compression and multimodal visual token merging.

papers.title: OP-Print: Tracing Membership Imprints in On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation has been widely adopted for alleviating the distribution mismatch of off-policy distillation. Self-distillation further removes the need for an external teacher by using the student's own outputs, enhanced with extra context or demonstrations, as supervision. This teacher-free design makes on-policy self-distillation practical, yet its privacy risks remain largely unexplored. In particular, using two coupled views of the same training example may strengthen its memorization. Motivated by this, we present the first study of membership inference attacks against on-policy self-distillation. We investigate both gray-box and black-box threat models and propose a unified attack framework, named OP-Print. OP-Print builds on our finding that the supervision imprint in on-policy self-distillation is sparse and structured, concentrating on uncertainty-sensitive correction sites rather than across the entire rollout. Exploiting this property, we construct attack signals tailored to the two access levels: in the gray-box setting, OP-Print directly aggregates the privileged teacher-student residual correction along the same rollout; in the black-box setting, it measures restart-based output-basin stability as an observable surrogate for the hidden correction process. Across diverse models and distillation schemes, all baseline attacks remain essentially at random guessing even under gray-box access, whereas OP-Print is broadly validated to be effective in both gray-box and black-box settings.
papers.ja_title: オンポリシー自己蒸留における訓練データの会員性推論攻撃 OP-Print

papers.title: BeNice! Closing Looping's Inference-Memory Gap via KV-Sharing
papers.abstract: Looped architectures scale quality while keeping parameter count fixed by repeatedly passing activations through the same block of layers. During inference, each recurrence generates independent KV-caches, causing memory to grow linearly. To address this challenge, prior work has proposed KV-sharing (i.e., sharing KV-caches across depth), finding that, in some cases, the KV-cache of the final recurrence can be shared with the earlier recurrences without quality loss, a property we denote as KV-shareability. However, the mechanisms underlying KV-shareability remain poorly understood, with even identically trained looped architectures not consistently exhibiting it. In this paper, we study how KV-shareability can be enabled in looped models. We propose a two-stage method: in the first stage, we use stochastic depth during pretraining, which induces contractive residual dynamics that drive representations toward a common limit across recurrences. In the second stage, we propose BeNice!, a post-training method that broadcasts the final recurrence's KV-cache into the first recurrence, training it to produce compatible residuals while preserving the original model's quality. As a result, BeNice! enables KV-shareability while matching standard finetuning's unshared validation perplexity. Using BeNice!, we show that KV-sharing is complementary to alternative KV-compression methods, composing with memory-efficient sequence mixers (e.g., multi-latent attention, Kimi delta attention) and low-precision KV-cache quantization (e.g., fp8, mxfp8, nvfp4). Finally, in simulated low-memory, long-context inference, KV-sharing improves cache hit rates by up to 31.4%, increases throughput by up to 23.6%, and reduces p90 time-to-first-token by up to 83.6%.
papers.ja_title: ループ構造モデルの推論メモリ問題を KV 共有で解消する BeNice!
papers.summary: ループ構造モデル(同じ層のブロックを何度も繰り返し通すことでパラメータ数を増やさずに性能を上げるアーキテクチャ)は、繰り返しごとに別々の KV キャッシュを作るため推論時のメモリが繰り返し回数に比例して増える。BeNice! は事前学習時に確率的な層スキップで各繰り返しの表現を近づけておき、その後の学習で最後の繰り返しの KV キャッシュを最初の繰り返しにも使えるようにする 2 段階の手法で、通常の追加学習と同等の精度を保ったまま KV キャッシュの共有を可能にし、低メモリ・長文脈の想定環境でキャッシュのヒット率を最大 31.4%、スループットを最大 23.6% 向上させ、応答開始までの時間の 90 パーセンタイル値を最大 83.6% 短縮した。
papers.why: ループ構造モデルという新しいアーキテクチャの弱点(推論メモリの線形増大)を解消する具体的な訓練手法で、低精度量子化など他の KV 圧縮技術とも組み合わせられる点が実装上の利点になる。
papers.summary_en: Looped architectures scale quality while keeping parameter count fixed by repeatedly passing activations through the same block of layers, but during inference each recurrence generates an independent KV cache, so memory grows linearly; prior work on KV-sharing across depth found that, in some cases, the final recurrence's KV cache can be shared with earlier recurrences without quality loss, a property the authors call KV-shareability, but the mechanisms behind it remain poorly understood, and even identically trained looped architectures do not consistently exhibit it. The authors propose a two-stage method: first, stochastic depth during pretraining induces contractive residual dynamics that drive representations toward a common limit across recurrences, and second, BeNice!, a post-training method that broadcasts the final recurrence's KV cache into the first recurrence and trains it to produce compatible residuals while preserving the original model's quality, matching standard finetuning's unshared validation perplexity. Using BeNice!, they show KV-sharing composes with memory-efficient sequence mixers (multi-latent attention, Kimi delta attention) and low-precision KV cache quantization (fp8, mxfp8, nvfp4), and in simulated low-memory, long-context inference, KV-sharing improves cache hit rates by up to 31.4%, increases throughput by up to 23.6%, and reduces p90 time-to-first-token by up to 83.6%.
papers.why_en: Turns an inconsistently occurring property, KV-shareability in looped models, into something the authors can reliably induce via a two-stage training recipe, and shows it composes with other memory-saving techniques rather than competing with them.

papers.title: A Fix for Softmax and Cross-Entropy
papers.abstract: Standard implementations of softmax, log-softmax, and cross-entropy have two numerical bugs. The first bug, Softmax Collapse, rounds the target logit's gradient to zero if that one logit is much larger than the others, resulting in gradients that no longer sum to zero. The second bug, Softmax Cancellation, occurs when student logits are close to teacher logits, and produces non-zero gradients even when the student and teacher logits are equal. We present simple implementations of log-softmax, softmax, and cross-entropy that fix both bugs. Our fix eliminates the previously observed "slingshot" phenomenon, speeds up grokking with weight decay, prevents accuracy collapse without weight decay, stops student networks from drifting away from the teacher during distillation, and shows that after memorization, logit growth is bounded by an equilibrium between weight decay and Adam's $ε$ hyperparameter.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: softmax と交差エントロピーの実装に潜む 2 つの数値バグとその修正
papers.summary: 標準的な softmax・log-softmax・交差エントロピーの実装には 2 つの数値計算上のバグがあり、1 つは目的の logit(モデルが出す生の予測値)が他より極端に大きいときに勾配が誤って 0 になる「Softmax Collapse」、もう 1 つは学習対象と教師の logit が一致しているのに勾配が 0 にならない「Softmax Cancellation」である。この論文はこの両方を直す簡潔な実装を示し、既存研究で見られた「スリングショット」現象(学習が突然乱れる挙動)を解消し、重み減衰を使ったグロッキング(突然の汎化)を速め、重み減衰なしでの精度崩壊を防ぎ、蒸留で学習対象のモデルが教師からずれていく問題を止めた。
papers.why: 多くのモデルで共通利用される softmax や交差エントロピーの基礎カーネルにある見落とされたバグを指摘しており、訓練安定性や蒸留の品質に直接影響するため実装者が確認すべき内容である。
papers.summary_en: Standard implementations of softmax, log-softmax, and cross-entropy have two numerical bugs: Softmax Collapse rounds the target logit's gradient to zero when that logit is much larger than the others, leaving gradients that no longer sum to zero, and Softmax Cancellation produces non-zero gradients even when student and teacher logits are equal, when the student logits are close to the teacher's. The authors present simple implementations of log-softmax, softmax, and cross-entropy that fix both bugs, and show the fix eliminates the previously observed 'slingshot' phenomenon, speeds up grokking with weight decay, prevents accuracy collapse without weight decay, stops student networks from drifting away from the teacher during distillation, and shows that after memorization, logit growth is bounded by an equilibrium between weight decay and Adam's epsilon hyperparameter.
papers.why_en: Identifies two silent numerical bugs in implementations as standard and widely used as softmax and cross-entropy, and connects them directly to previously unexplained training phenomena (the slingshot effect, grokking speed, distillation drift), which is a correctness lesson applicable to essentially any training pipeline.

review.note: softmax・log-softmax・cross-entropy という最も基本的な実装でも、target のロジットが他より大きく離れている場合や、生徒と教師のロジットがほぼ一致する場合という境界条件で勾配が黙って壊れることがある。基本演算を実装・レビューするときは、極端な入力(1 つだけ極端に大きい、ほぼ等しい)で勾配が理論値と一致するかを必ず確かめる、という観点。
review.note_en: Even the most standard, widely trusted building blocks (softmax, log-softmax, cross-entropy) can silently produce wrong gradients at edge cases, one logit far larger than the rest, or student and teacher logits nearly equal. A concrete reminder to test core numerical primitives against their edge-case gradient behavior, not just their forward-pass output, when implementing or reviewing them.

papers.title: When and How Does Muon Precondition? The Role of Structured Gradient Noise
papers.abstract: Muon has become a popular optimizer for large language model training, yet its theoretical foundations remain poorly understood. In this work, we study how gradient noise geometry shapes Muon's preconditioning benefits. We first show, theoretically and empirically, that under the classical isotropic noise assumption, Muon offers no acceleration beyond a rescaling of the learning rate. This motivates us to investigate structured noise arising from mini-batch sampling in associative memory with heterogeneous task frequencies. We establish an exact balancing threshold for two tasks and extend the analysis to multiple tasks, revealing how task coverage and gradient reliability jointly shape learning. Our analysis shows that Muon can soften the dependence on task frequency from linear to square-root, helping balance the learning of frequent and rare tasks. We further identify rotation-induced negative transfer in SignSGD that Muon avoids, and explain how momentum reduces sampling noise while tracking changing gradients. Controlled numerical experiments validate these mechanisms, and a preliminary LLM pretraining study illustrates the practical promise of fast-slow momentum.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: Muon オプティマイザがいつ・どう効くのかを勾配ノイズの構造から説明する
papers.summary: LLM 訓練で人気のオプティマイザ Muon の理論的な仕組みは十分に分かっていなかった。この論文は、勾配ノイズが方向に偏りなく均一(等方的)だと仮定した場合 Muon は学習率の調整以上の加速効果を持たないことを理論と実験の両方で示し、代わりにミニバッチ抽出から生じる「構造を持ったノイズ」(連想記憶でタスクの頻度が不均一な場合)を調べることで、Muon が頻出タスクと希少タスクの学習バランスを、頻度への依存度を線形から平方根に緩めることで改善する仕組みを明らかにした。
papers.why: Muon のようなオプティマイザの効果をノイズの統計的性質から説明する理論的な枠組みで、どの訓練設定で Muon が有効かを見積もる手がかりになる。
papers.summary_en: Muon has become a popular optimizer for LLM training, yet its theoretical foundations remain poorly understood; the authors study how gradient noise geometry shapes Muon's preconditioning benefits, first showing theoretically and empirically that under the classical isotropic noise assumption, Muon offers no acceleration beyond a rescaling of the learning rate. This motivates studying structured noise arising from mini-batch sampling in associative memory with heterogeneous task frequencies, where they establish an exact balancing threshold for two tasks, extend the analysis to multiple tasks, and show Muon can soften the dependence on task frequency from linear to square-root, helping balance the learning of frequent and rare tasks; they further identify a rotation-induced negative transfer in SignSGD that Muon avoids, and explain how momentum reduces sampling noise while tracking changing gradients. Controlled numerical experiments validate these mechanisms, and a preliminary LLM pretraining study illustrates the practical promise of fast-slow momentum.
papers.why_en: Pinpoints that Muon's benefit comes specifically from structured, task-frequency-driven gradient noise rather than from gradient noise in general, which under the classical isotropic assumption gives Muon no advantage at all, clarifying when and why to expect Muon to help.

papers.title: Nested Sparsity for Scalable Pretraining and Continual Learning
papers.abstract: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) transformers, the standard backbone for modern large-scale deep learning, employ conditional computation: only a sparse subset of model weights is used in each forward pass. In MoE transformers, this sparsity arises in the MoE operator, which generalizes the multi-layer perceptron in the classical transformer. In this work, we explore an alternative mechanism for conditional computation that analogously generalizes the attention operator. The sparsity induced by this mechanism naturally nests (i.e., hierarchically composes) with the sparsity induced by the MoE operator. We show that a transformer employing this nested sparsity mechanism, which we call Nestor, performs better than a conventional MoE transformer at equal compute and equal sparsity in language model pretraining. We also show that Nestor is well-suited for continual pretraining: it can be adapted to longer contexts more effectively than conventional MoEs, as well as adapt more efficiently to new domains while forgetting less on old domains. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these benefits persist as model size, dataset size, and context length grow. Our results demonstrate the potential of alternative conditional computation mechanisms for deep neural network architectures. Code and checkpoints are available on GitHub at https://github.com/Ma-Lab-Berkeley/Nestor .
papers.ja_title: MoE と入れ子になる新しい条件計算機構 Nestor
papers.summary: 現代の大規模モデルの標準である MoE(Mixture-of-Experts、入力ごとに一部の重みだけを使う仕組み)はフィードフォワード層に条件計算を導入するが、この論文はアテンション層にも似た考え方を適用する機構 Nestor を提案し、MoE のスパース性と自然に入れ子にできる。同じ計算量・同じスパース度で従来の MoE トランスフォーマーより事前学習の性能が高く、長い文脈への適応や新しい分野への追加学習でも既存分野の性能を保ちながら効率的に適応できることを、モデルサイズ・データ量・文脈長を変えて確認した。
papers.why: MoE に続く条件計算の対象をアテンション層にまで広げる新しいアーキテクチャの方向性で、継続事前学習や長文脈対応といった実運用上の課題にも効果が確認されている。
papers.summary_en: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) transformers, the standard backbone for modern large-scale deep learning, use conditional computation where only a sparse subset of weights is used per forward pass, with this sparsity arising in the MoE operator that generalizes the MLP. The authors explore an alternative conditional-computation mechanism that analogously generalizes the attention operator, whose induced sparsity naturally nests with MoE sparsity; they call the resulting transformer Nestor, and show it performs better than a conventional MoE transformer at equal compute and equal sparsity in language model pretraining. Nestor is also well suited to continual pretraining, adapting to longer contexts more effectively than conventional MoEs and adapting more efficiently to new domains while forgetting less on old ones, with these benefits persisting as model size, dataset size, and context length grow.
papers.why_en: Extends conditional computation beyond the now-standard MoE MLP sparsity to the attention operator itself, showing the two sparsity mechanisms nest rather than conflict and that the combination helps specifically with continual pretraining's context-extension and forgetting trade-offs.

papers.title: Rewriting Scaling Laws for Synthetic Data with Compute and Data Constraints
papers.abstract: Synthetic rewrites, where a language model rewrites a natural document e.g. into a target style, are now a standard ingredient of pretraining corpora. However, critical aspects of their use remain poorly understood, such as how much compute should be spent rewriting training data and whether a model trained on rewrites can outperform the rewriter. We study these two questions by proposing a rewriting scaling law that predicts loss from model size, training tokens, the fraction of training tokens that are rewrites, and the number of epochs over the natural data, charging the compute spent generating rewrites. We fit this scaling law in two settings. In the compute-limited setting, natural data is plentiful and rewrites come from a third-party rewriter trained with more compute than our largest run. We find that the estimated optimal rewrite fraction increases with compute, from under $10\%$ at $3\times10^{18}$ FLOPs to $32\%$ at $10^{22}$ FLOPs. Our scaling forecast extrapolates $33\times$ in FLOPs to train a 22B-parameter model, whose final loss is within $1.1\%$ of our prediction. This model achieves a better BPB than its rewriter on several web domains at one-tenth the rewriter's training compute. In the data-limited setting, we assume we only have a fixed seed set of natural data and that our rewriter is a model of the same size as the target, pretrained on that seed set. Again, we find the optimal rewrite fraction increases with the compute budget. We also demonstrate that a model trained on rewrites of its own pretraining data, generated by a rewriter of the same size, beats the best run on natural data alone at every model size up to 3B. Our results show that synthetic rewriting can be studied through the scaling law lens: that optimal methodological choices are predictable and scaling does not necessarily break down beyond the rewriter's capabilities.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 合成リライトデータのための計算量とデータ制約を考慮したスケーリング則
papers.summary: 言語モデルで文書を目的のスタイルに書き換えた「合成リライト」データを事前学習に混ぜる手法が広まっているが、どれだけの計算をリライトに使うべきかは分かっていなかった。この論文はモデルサイズ・訓練トークン数・リライト比率・自然データの周回数からロス(損失)を予測するスケーリング則を提案し、計算量が増えるほど最適なリライト比率も増え(3×10^18 FLOPs で 10% 未満から 10^22 FLOPs で 32% まで)、33 倍の計算量まで外挿して訓練した 22B パラメータモデルの最終ロスは予測の 1.1% 以内に収まり、リライト元のモデルの 10 分の 1 の計算量で複数の Web ドメインでリライト元を上回る性能(BPB)を達成した。
papers.why: 合成データ生成に使う計算量の最適配分を事前に予測できることを示し、事前学習の計算資源配分を設計する際の定量的な指針になる。
papers.summary_en: Synthetic rewrites of natural documents are now a standard pretraining ingredient, but how much compute to spend rewriting, and whether a model trained on rewrites can outperform the rewriter, remained poorly understood. The authors propose a rewriting scaling law predicting loss from model size, training tokens, rewrite fraction, and epochs over natural data, charging the compute spent generating rewrites, and fit it in compute-limited and data-limited settings. The optimal rewrite fraction rises with compute (under 10% at 3x10^18 FLOPs to 32% at 10^22 FLOPs); extrapolating 33x in FLOPs to a 22B-parameter model, the final loss lands within 1.1% of the prediction and the model beats its own rewriter's BPB on several web domains at one-tenth the rewriter's training compute. In the data-limited setting, a model trained on same-size-rewriter rewrites of its own seed data beats the best natural-data-only run at every size up to 3B.
papers.why_en: Shows that compute spent on synthetic rewriting can itself be governed by a predictable scaling law, giving a quantitative basis for allocating pretraining compute between rewriting and raw training.

papers.title: Learning Structured Sparsity for Large Models: Bridging Model Compressibility and Efficient Inference
papers.abstract: Scaling laws continue to reward increases in model scale, while the resulting computational and memory demands drive greater reliance on cloud infrastructure for inference. Yet unreliable network connectivity, communication delays, and privacy requirements can make such reliance impractical, motivating local execution on edge devices. Local deployment requires models to fit within limited memory and execute efficiently with the available computational resources. Recent work has shown that learning sparse-plus-low-rank representations enables elastic compression of a single checkpoint to multiple memory budgets. However, fewer parameters do not necessarily translate into faster inference. Indexing overhead and irregular memory access in unstructured sparse components can offset computational savings. To address this critical deployment barrier, we introduce S-SALAAD, a unified framework that jointly learns the model weights and their low-rank and structured sparse components during training. The framework supports a family of hardware-compatible structured sparsity patterns. It couples this structure learning with budget-aware compression and dedicated CPU and GPU kernels that exploit the learned structure for acceleration, enabling efficient inference from a single checkpoint across memory budgets. Experiments on Llama2 and Qwen3 models, covering both pretraining and distillation, show that S-SALAAD advances the empirical Pareto frontier in perplexity, memory, and inference latency across multiple hardware platforms relative to the evaluated baselines. These results show that structured learning can translate elastic compressibility into reduced memory requirements and lower inference latency, enabling practical deployment of large models on edge devices.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 構造化スパース性でモデル圧縮と推論高速化を両立する S-SALAAD
papers.summary: モデルを小さくしても、非構造的なスパース(不規則にゼロが混じった重み)はインデックス参照の overhead が多く、実際の推論速度向上につながらないことが多い。S-SALAAD は低ランク成分とハードウェアに適した構造化スパース成分を訓練時に一緒に学習し、その構造を活かす専用の CPU/GPU カーネルを組み合わせることで、1 つのモデルチェックポイントから複数のメモリ予算に対応でき、Llama2・Qwen3 で精度・メモリ・推論レイテンシのパレートフロンティア(最良のトレードオフの境界線)を既存手法より改善した。
papers.why: 圧縮してもハードウェアで速くならないという典型的な問題を、構造学習と専用カーネルの両方を同時に設計することで解決しており、エッジデバイス向け推論基盤の設計に直接応用できる。
papers.summary_en: Edge deployment of large models requires fitting within limited memory, but recent sparse-plus-low-rank compression work shows fewer parameters do not necessarily translate into faster inference, since indexing overhead and irregular memory access in unstructured sparse components can offset computational savings. The authors introduce S-SALAAD, a framework that jointly learns model weights together with low-rank and hardware-compatible structured sparse components during training, coupled with budget-aware compression and dedicated CPU/GPU kernels exploiting the learned structure for acceleration from a single checkpoint across memory budgets. On Llama2 and Qwen3, covering pretraining and distillation, S-SALAAD advances the empirical Pareto frontier in perplexity, memory, and inference latency across multiple hardware platforms relative to the evaluated baselines.
papers.why_en: Demonstrates that elastic compressibility and actual hardware speedups require co-designing structured sparsity learning with dedicated kernels, directly informing edge inference deployment design.

papers.title: LazyFlash: Forward-Dense, Backward-Sparse Attention for Accelerated Long-Context Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) process increasingly long sequences, attention becomes a major computational bottleneck. Sparse attention mostly targets inference, yet many methods still train densely or cannot support sparse training, and their added complexity makes sparsity hard to turn into wall-clock speedups, leaving dense attention widely used in practice. This paper introduces LazyFlash, a forward-dense, backward-sparse attention method built on the observation that attention training is dominated by the backward pass. LazyFlash keeps the forward pass exactly dense, so the trained model remains a standard dense model that existing systems such as vLLM can serve without any change. For the backward pass, LazyFlash proposes a gradient-aware block sparsification design that ranks query blocks by their attention-output gradient norms and skips those contributing negligibly to parameter updates, turning the dense backward into a block-sparse one. A gradient-mass budget adapts the amount of skipped computation to each head and training step, while importance sampling preserves the dense gradient in expectation. These designs are implemented inside the tiled FlashAttention backward kernel, where skipped blocks are never loaded or computed, translating gradient sparsity into real wall-clock acceleration. Experiments on long-context text and speech LLMs show that LazyFlash maintains downstream performance while achieving up to 5.7x attention-backward speedup over FlashAttention and 1.7x end-to-end training speedup.
papers.ja_title: 順伝播は密に保ち逆伝播だけスパース化する長文脈学習の高速化 LazyFlash
papers.summary: 長い文脈を扱う LLM の訓練ではアテンション計算がボトルネックになるが、既存のスパースアテンション手法の多くは推論向けで訓練には使えないか複雑すぎて速度向上につながらない。LazyFlash は順伝播(forward)は完全に密なまま保ち、訓練の大半を占める逆伝播(backward)だけを勾配の大きさでクエリブロックを選別してスパース化する手法で、FlashAttention の逆伝播カーネルに直接組み込み、学習済みモデルは vLLM など既存のサービング基盤で変更なく動かせる。長文脈のテキスト・音声 LLM での実験で、下流タスクの性能を保ったまま逆伝播を最大 5.7 倍、学習全体を最大 1.7 倍高速化した。
papers.why: 訓練後のモデルがそのまま既存のサービング基盤で使える(推論側の変更が不要)という制約を守りながら訓練だけを高速化する設計は、実運用への導入障壁が低い高速化策である。
papers.summary_en: Attention is a major bottleneck for long-sequence LLM training, and existing sparse attention methods mostly target inference or are too complex to turn into real wall-clock speedups, so dense attention remains widely used in practice. LazyFlash keeps the forward pass exactly dense -- so the trained model stays a standard dense model that systems like vLLM can serve without change -- and sparsifies only the backward pass via a gradient-aware block sparsification that ranks query blocks by attention-output gradient norms, skips negligible-contribution blocks inside the tiled FlashAttention backward kernel, and uses a gradient-mass budget plus importance sampling to preserve the dense gradient in expectation. On long-context text and speech LLMs, LazyFlash maintains downstream performance while achieving up to 5.7x attention-backward speedup over FlashAttention and 1.7x end-to-end training speedup.
papers.why_en: A training-only speedup that leaves the trained model fully compatible with existing dense serving stacks is a low-friction optimization to adopt in production training pipelines.

papers.title: Can Test-Time Memory Evolution Outperform Test-Time Training for Scientific Discovery?
papers.abstract: Recent \emph{test-time training} (TTT) frameworks have enabled open-weight large language models (LLMs) to outperform inference-only frameworks powered by frontier models on scientific discovery tasks. However, TTT introduces additional computational cost for online weight updates during the discovery process, making computational efficiency an important consideration when scaling to larger models. This motivates us to explore an efficient \emph{test-time adaptation} method for scientific discovery. We introduce \emph{Test-Time Memory Evolution} (TTME), a plug-and-play test-time adaptation method, as an alternative to TTT. TTME continually updates the external memory by distilling the experience to guide subsequent discovery without updating model weights. To have a clean comparison, we evaluate TTME and TTT under the same discovery framework, replacing only the test-time adaptation method. Our evaluation shows that TTME outperforms TTT on all five mathematical tasks, while reducing computational cost by $82.8$-$84.6\%$ in FLOPs and $47.7$-$58.4\%$ in runtime. These results establish TTME as an effective and computationally efficient alternative to TTT in the evaluated discovery settings.
papers.ja_title: 科学的発見タスクでテスト時のメモリ更新は重み更新より効率的か

papers.title: HyScale: Scaling Long-Context Training for Learned Sparse Attention
papers.abstract: We present HyScale, a long-context training system for learned sparse attention. Learned sparse attention is a promising architecture for million-token contexts, widely adopted in production since DeepSeek-V3.2. Selection, however, grows into the training bottleneck. For each query, it scores every previous token whereas sparse attention reads only $k$; worse, current systems materialize a full score table and repeat selection during recomputation. Our key insight is that the output of selection is not an activation, but rather a set of indices. Building on it, HyScale introduces HyTopK and selection replay. HyTopK finds each query's exact top-$k$ on the fly without a score table, while selection replay reuses forward-pass selection in recomputation. Together with holistic system optimizations tackling end-to-end training challenges, HyScale speeds up GLM-5.1 training on 1M-token sequences by 2.07$\times$ over Megatron-LM on 512 H20 GPUs. It also speeds up the CSA layers of DeepSeek-V4-Flash and the QSA layers of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next by 2.01$\times$ and 1.57$\times$ at 1M tokens on 32 H800 GPUs.
papers.ja_title: 100 万トークン級の学習済みスパースアテンションを高速に訓練する HyScale
papers.summary: 学習型スパースアテンション(どのトークンに注意を向けるかをモデル自身が選ぶ方式、DeepSeek-V3.2 以降に実運用で広まった)は、選ぶ処理そのものが訓練のボトルネックになる。HyScale は選択結果を活性化ではなく「インデックス集合」として扱うことに着目し、スコア表を作らずに top-k を直接求める HyTopK と、再計算時に前方計算の選択結果を再利用する selection replay を導入し、GLM-5.1 を 512 枚の H20 GPU で 100 万トークンの系列で訓練する際に Megatron-LM の 2.07 倍の速度を達成、32 枚の H800 GPU でも DeepSeek-V4-Flash の CSA 層と Qwen3.8-Flash-Next の QSA 層を 100 万トークンでそれぞれ 2.01 倍・1.57 倍高速化した。
papers.why: 学習型スパースアテンションという本番採用が進むアーキテクチャの訓練システム側のボトルネックを具体的に解消しており、大規模クラスタでの長文脈訓練の設計に直接活用できる。
papers.summary_en: Learned sparse attention -- widely adopted in production since DeepSeek-V3.2 for million-token contexts -- scores every previous token for selection even though sparse attention reads only k of them, and current systems worsen this by materializing a full score table and repeating selection during recomputation, turning selection into the training bottleneck. HyScale's key insight is that a selection's output is a set of indices rather than an activation, leading to HyTopK (finds each query's exact top-k on the fly without a score table) and selection replay (reuses forward-pass selection during recomputation). Combined with broader system optimizations, HyScale speeds up GLM-5.1 training on 1M-token sequences by 2.07x over Megatron-LM on 512 H20 GPUs, and speeds up the CSA layers of DeepSeek-V4-Flash and QSA layers of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next by 2.01x and 1.57x at 1M tokens on 32 H800 GPUs.
papers.why_en: Targets the training-side bottleneck of an attention architecture already in production inference use, giving concrete system optimizations usable for large-cluster long-context training.

papers.title: DELA: Learning Controllable Edits for Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract: Diffusion language models (DLMs) support bidirectional denoising and iterative refinement, but generation remains largely controlled by token-level masking schedules. This leaves draft-level refinement implicit and limits explicit control over when to insert missing content, delete redundant spans, revisit uncertain regions, or stop editing. We introduce Diffusion Editing Language Adapter (DELA), a plug-in framework that enables controllable draft refinement with a frozen DLM. DELA operates on clean, variable-length drafts using four explicit editing actions: Insert, Delete, Remask, and Stop. The controller determines when and where to edit the draft, while the frozen DLM fills masked regions through denoising, separating high-level edit control from token-level generation. A naive single-phase editor would be computationally expensive because arbitrary interior edits can disrupt prefix stability and limit reliable KV-cache reuse. To address this, DELA uses a two-phase decoding procedure: a fast, append-only drafting phase that supports KV-cache reuse, followed by a global refinement phase that enables targeted non-monotonic edits to the full draft. We train the controller using a staged curriculum that begins with learning local edit priors from synthetic recovery tasks and mined actions that improve draft quality. Subsequent stages refine edit selection through rollout-based outcome preferences and alignment with downstream task feedback. Experiments on mathematical reasoning and code generation show that DELA achieves gains of up to 5.5 percentage points over direct diffusion decoding while keeping the backbone frozen. DELA thus provides a modular approach to explicit draft-level control in diffusion language models.
papers.ja_title: 拡散言語モデルの生成を挿入・削除・再マスクで編集可能にする DELA

papers.title: Head Dimension Matters in Language Models for Long-Context Retrieval
papers.abstract: Multi-head attention retrieves and combines context representations through query--key interactions and value aggregation, with head dimension constraining the per-head representation space. In long-context processing, it remains unclear whether allocating a fixed parameter budget to fewer, wider heads improves information retrieval. In this paper, we investigate how head dimension affects the performance of long-context retrieval tasks. Our empirical studies reveal that pretraining loss and short-context non-retrieval task performance are not affected much by head dimension, while long-context retrieval performance improves with wider heads at fixed model sizes. We find that models with wider heads have a higher proportion of retrieval heads, associating more parameters with retrieval. Our ablation studies also show that the retrieval performance improves with wider heads even when the projection weights in attention modules are frozen during long-context continual pretraining, suggesting that wider heads not only benefit updates in attention modules but lead to more effective adaptation of components such as embeddings and MLPs.
papers.ja_title: 長文脈検索でアテンションのヘッド次元数が性能を左右することを示す研究
papers.summary: マルチヘッドアテンションでは 1 ヘッドあたりの次元数(表現できる空間の広さ)が情報検索の性能を左右しうるが、固定のパラメータ予算を少数で広いヘッドに割り当てるべきかは分かっていなかった。この論文は事前学習時のロスや短い文脈でのタスク性能はヘッド次元の広さにほとんど影響されない一方、長文脈の検索タスクの性能はヘッドを広くするほど向上することを実験で示し、広いヘッドを持つモデルほど検索に使われるヘッドの割合が高く、アテンション層の重みを固定して追加学習しても広いヘッドの方が性能が良いことを確認した。
papers.why: 長文脈対応モデルを設計する際のアーキテクチャ選択(ヘッド数とヘッド次元の配分)に具体的な実験的根拠を与えており、モデル設計の指針として使える。
papers.summary_en: It remained unclear whether, for long-context processing, allocating a fixed parameter budget to fewer, wider attention heads improves information retrieval. The authors find empirically that pretraining loss and short-context non-retrieval performance are not much affected by head dimension, while long-context retrieval performance improves with wider heads at fixed model size, and that models with wider heads have a higher proportion of 'retrieval heads.' Ablations further show retrieval performance improves with wider heads even when attention projection weights are frozen during long-context continual pretraining, suggesting wider heads also help other components such as embeddings and MLPs adapt more effectively.
papers.why_en: Gives concrete empirical evidence for an architecture choice (head count vs. head width) relevant to designing long-context models.

papers.title: Democratizing LLM Training with the Edge: Challenges, Systems, and the Road Ahead
papers.abstract: The growing computational power of modern GPU data centers has let a few industrial giants train and deploy large language models (LLMs) on massive amounts of data. Yet the sheer scale of these models and their training data makes centralized development increasingly hard to sustain, and at the same time shuts out smaller institutions that hold relevant private data but lack comparable infrastructure. In this paper, we organize our positions on distributed LLM training around the pretraining and fine-tuning paradigms, covering federated learning, split learning, and decentralized approaches, and we assess their readiness for geo-distributed settings with heterogeneous hardware and unreliable connectivity. We then present a {\em unified} system architecture built around a cloud-hosted parameter server that coordinates heterogeneous clients over outbound gRPC connections, reusing one communication, compression, and fault-tolerance stack for both pretraining and a family of fine-tuning methods. We validate the design with real geo-distributed experiments on GPT-2 Medium and Llama3-1B pretraining across multiple university sites, showing stable convergence under realistic conditions. Finally, we chart the road ahead, identifying open problems that span frontier model support, elastic fault tolerance, adaptive compression, federated alignment, privacy and trust, incentive design, and system--algorithm co-design, all of which must be addressed to make democratized LLM training a reality.
papers.ja_title: エッジ拠点を使った LLM 分散学習の現状整理と統一アーキテクチャ
papers.summary: 少数の大企業しか大規模 LLM を訓練できない現状に対し、学内など地理的に分散した拠点が持つデータと計算資源を使う分散学習(連合学習・分割学習・非中央集権型)の課題を整理した。クラウド上のパラメータサーバーが複数拠点のクライアントを gRPC で束ね、通信・圧縮・耐故障性の仕組みを事前学習とファインチューニングの両方で共有する設計を提案している。GPT-2 Medium と Llama3-1B を複数大学間で実際に事前学習させ、現実的な通信条件下でも安定して収束することを確認した。
papers.why: 単一データセンター前提の分散学習基盤を、信頼性の低いネットワークや異種ハードウェアが混ざる環境に広げる際の設計指針と、残る課題(弾力的な耐故障性・適応的圧縮など)が整理されている。
papers.summary_en: The sheer scale of LLMs and their training data increasingly excludes smaller institutions that hold relevant private data but lack comparable infrastructure. This position paper organizes federated, split, and decentralized approaches to distributed LLM training around pretraining and fine-tuning, assesses their readiness for geo-distributed settings with heterogeneous hardware and unreliable connectivity, and proposes a unified system architecture built around a cloud-hosted parameter server coordinating heterogeneous clients over outbound gRPC, reusing one communication/compression/fault-tolerance stack for both pretraining and fine-tuning. Real geo-distributed experiments on GPT-2 Medium and Llama3-1B pretraining across multiple university sites show stable convergence under realistic conditions, and the paper charts open problems spanning frontier-model support, elastic fault tolerance, adaptive compression, federated alignment, privacy/trust, incentives, and system-algorithm co-design.
papers.why_en: Lays out a concrete system architecture and real multi-site experiments for distributed training beyond a single data center, plus a roadmap of unsolved problems relevant to anyone designing such infrastructure.

papers.title: Training an MoE LLM in MXFP4: How We Closed the Gap to BF16
papers.abstract: Training large language models (LLMs) in sub-8-bit arithmetic promises substantial gains in memory bandwidth and compute throughput, yet FP4 formats introduce quantization error severe enough to destabilize optimization if left unaddressed. We present ALTO, an open-source training recipe for GPT-OSS-20B, a 20-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts (MoE) model, on the MLPerf Small MoE Training benchmark under the MXFP4 microscaling format. The recipe combines established techniques from Abecassis, Felix et al. [arXiv:2509.25149] (hybrid 1D/2D block quantization, randomized Hadamard transforms, and stochastic rounding) with a simplified weight de-oscillation scheme adapted from TetraJet-v2 [arXiv:2510.27527]. On C4 validation at global batch size 16, MXFP4 + RHT + SR + de-oscillation reaches a validation loss of 3.3350 at 16,128 steps, only 0.007 above the BF16 baseline (3.3283), closing roughly 50% of the gap left by MXFP4 without de-oscillation (3.3418). Measured by steps to reach the MLPerf quality target (validation loss 3.34), de-oscillation cuts the FP4 convergence overhead relative to BF16 from +20.0% to +5.0%. We also report negative end-to-end results from differential gradient estimation, outlier clipping, and macro-block scaling, despite each showing operator-level SNR gains. All experiments use simulated MXFP4 kernels on AMD MI300X hardware and wall-clock speed has not been optimized.
papers.ja_title: 20B MoE モデルを MXFP4(4 bit)で BF16 に迫る精度まで訓練する手法
papers.summary: 8 bit 未満の超低精度での LLM 訓練はメモリ帯域と計算速度を大きく改善できるが、FP4(4 bit 浮動小数点)形式は量子化誤差が大きく学習が不安定になりやすい。著者らは 200 億パラメータの MoE(複数の専門家ネットワークを切り替えるモデル)GPT-OSS-20B を MXFP4 で訓練するレシピ ALTO を提案し、重みの振動を抑える手法を組み合わせることで、検証損失を BF16 基準(3.3283)に対しわずか 0.007 差の 3.3350 まで縮め、量子化による誤差の約 50% を解消した。目標精度に到達するまでの学習ステップ数で見ると、BF16 に対する余分なステップ数を 20.0% から 5.0% まで削減した。
papers.why: MoE モデルを超低精度で訓練する際に実際に効く手法の組み合わせと、効かなかった手法(差分勾配推定・外れ値クリッピングなど)を実測ベースで切り分けており、低精度訓練の実装判断に直接使える。
papers.summary_en: Training LLMs in sub-8-bit arithmetic promises large memory-bandwidth and throughput gains, but FP4 formats introduce quantization error severe enough to destabilize optimization if unaddressed. The authors present ALTO, an open-source MXFP4 training recipe for the 20B-parameter MoE model GPT-OSS-20B on the MLPerf Small MoE Training benchmark, combining hybrid 1D/2D block quantization, randomized Hadamard transforms, and stochastic rounding with a simplified weight de-oscillation scheme. On C4 validation at batch size 16, MXFP4 + RHT + SR + de-oscillation reaches a validation loss of 3.3350 at 16,128 steps, only 0.007 above the BF16 baseline (3.3283), closing roughly 50% of the gap left without de-oscillation, and cutting the FP4 convergence step overhead relative to BF16 from +20.0% to +5.0%; the authors also report negative end-to-end results for differential gradient estimation, outlier clipping, and macro-block scaling despite each showing operator-level SNR gains. All experiments use simulated MXFP4 kernels on AMD MI300X hardware, and wall-clock speed has not been optimized.
papers.why_en: Separates which low-precision techniques actually close the MXFP4-to-BF16 gap for MoE training from those that look good at the operator level but fail end-to-end, directly actionable for low-precision training implementation choices.

papers.title: BiLoCo: Binary Low-Rank Corrections for Post-Training Quantization
papers.abstract: Post-training quantization (PTQ) to FP4 has emerged as a key technique for reducing large language model inference cost, especially on Blackwell GPUs, which offer native FP4 tensor core support. Direct PTQ to FP4, however, still leaves a noticeable accuracy gap. Recent work on SVDQuant mitigates the errors introduced through FP4 quantization for diffusion models by adding high-precision low-rank corrections obtained via SVD. However, this high-precision low-rank correction requires many bits per rank, and it runs on the same tensor cores as the main FP4 GEMM. We introduce BiLoCo, a low-rank correction method whose left and right factors are stored as binary ${\{\pm 1\}}$ sign vectors rather than as BF16 numbers. The signed format uses $16{\times}$ less storage per rank-one component, and since the correction now consists of additions/subtractions, this can be run on CUDA cores concurrently with the FP4 tensor-core GEMM. On 4B--72B LLMs, BiLoCo matches or improves memory-matched SVDQuant for PTQ. We implement BiLoCo on B300 as a fused single kernel, where the FP4 GEMM runs on tensor cores, the bit-packed correction on the CUDA cores of the same launch, and the two are combined in the GEMM epilogue. With batch size $1$, the fused kernel is at most $11\%$ slower than the FP4-only GEMM for every rank up to $512$. At rank $128$, it is at most $20\%$ slower up to batch size $8$.
papers.ja_title: FP4 量子化の誤差を 2 値の低ランク補正でほぼ無料に直す手法 BiLoCo
papers.summary: Blackwell GPU が得意な FP4(4 bit)形式に量子化すると推論コストは下がるが精度が落ちる。従来の SVDQuant は高精度の低ランク補正を追加して誤差を抑えるが、ビット数を多く使い FP4 計算と同じ計算回路(テンソルコア)を使ってしまう。BiLoCo は補正の値を ±1 の 2 値だけで表すことで保存量を 16 倍減らし、FP4 の計算回路とは別の CUDA コアで同時に計算できるようにした。4B から 72B の LLM で SVDQuant と同等以上の精度を保ちながら、B300 GPU 上でバッチサイズ 1 なら FP4 単体の計算に対し最大 11% の速度低下に抑えた。
papers.why: 量子化誤差の補正をメモリ帯域だけでなく計算回路の空き時間に乗せる設計で、FP4 推論カーネルの実装上の「補正のコストをどこに隠すか」という典型的な工夫が具体的に示されている。
papers.summary_en: Post-training quantization to FP4 reduces LLM inference cost on Blackwell GPUs but still leaves a noticeable accuracy gap, and SVDQuant's high-precision low-rank corrections mitigate this at the cost of many bits per rank and sharing the same tensor cores as the main FP4 GEMM. BiLoCo instead stores the low-rank correction's factors as binary {+/-1} sign vectors, using 16x less storage per rank-one component and letting the correction run as additions/subtractions on CUDA cores concurrently with the FP4 tensor-core GEMM. On 4B-72B LLMs, BiLoCo matches or improves memory-matched SVDQuant for PTQ; implemented as a fused single kernel on B300, with the FP4 GEMM on tensor cores and the bit-packed correction on CUDA cores of the same launch combined in the GEMM epilogue, the fused kernel is at most 11% slower than FP4-only GEMM at batch size 1 for ranks up to 512, and at most 20% slower at rank 128 up to batch size 8.
papers.why_en: Shows a concrete 'where to hide the correction cost' kernel-design pattern that moves quantization-error correction off the busy tensor cores onto otherwise idle CUDA cores, directly useful for FP4 inference kernel implementation.

papers.title: MetaDB: Putting File-System Structure Back into Distributed Databases
papers.abstract: Storage systems in production increasingly rely on distributed databases for metadata management, yet our experience at Baidu shows that treating a general-purpose database as a black box leaves substantial performance and efficiency untapped. File-system metadata exhibits directory-tree locality, differentiated consistency requirements, and clustered deletions that general-purpose databases largely ignore. We thus propose MetaDB, a metadata-aware distributed transactional database that serves as the shared metadata layer for Baidu's large-scale storage systems. MetaDB addresses three key mismatches between general-purpose databases and metadata workloads: Data Model Mismatch, Transaction Model Mismatch, and Storage Implementation Mismatch. To bridge these gaps, MetaDB combines (1) tree-topology-induced sharding and execution, (2) semantic-aware off-critical-path processing, and (3) a lifecycle-aware storage engine with in-memory MVCC and locality-aware compaction. MetaDB achieves 2.2x-4.1x the throughput of our previous general-purpose database and halves the number of metadata machines. Deployed in production at Baidu for over five years, MetaDB unifies metadata management across the company's storage fleet and scales to over 1,000 metadata nodes, tens of trillions of metadata records, and exabyte-scale storage in a single cluster.
papers.ja_title: Baidu のファイルシステム向け独自分散データベース MetaDB

papers.title: When Agents Fail: Model or Harness--Who's to Blame?
papers.abstract: LLM agents combine models with execution harnesses, so agentic benchmark performance reflects their joint behavior. We argue that harnesses should therefore be evaluated through their interactions with underlying models. We develop a framework combining five complementary measures: (i) Valid Completion Rate (VCR), how reliably agents finish normally and deliver evaluable results, irrespective of task correctness; (ii) Model-Harness Fit, how well a harness supports task achievement through valid completion for a given model; (iii) Cross-Model Fit, a harness's overall suitability across evaluated models; (iv) Interaction Residuals, pairing-specific execution strengths and weaknesses hidden by component-level summaries; and (v) Token Load, the token demands of agent execution, including failed attempts. We evaluate four general-purpose harnesses (OpenCode, Codex CLI, Pi CLI, and DeepAgents) with four core models, plus two fixed native model-harness systems, on six benchmarks covering context management, tool use, long-context planning, multimodal interaction, and artifact handoff. Including native references and stress conditions, 111 evaluation settings yield 52,168 trajectories. Harness rankings vary across models and benchmarks; task performance and valid completion can favor different pairings, and similar task scores can accompany distinct execution profiles. OpenCode ranks first in cross-model performance, while DeepSeek V4 Flash Preview maintains consistently high Mean VCR across harnesses on the shared four-benchmark panel. These findings support evaluating model-harness interactions, training transferable harness-use capabilities in models, and harness designs adapted to the model and task.
papers.ja_title: エージェントの失敗はモデルのせいか実行環境のせいかを切り分ける評価手法

papers.title: EditJev: System One Routing for Image Editing Models
papers.abstract: Instruction-based image editing models exhibit pronounced sample-specific performance variation: different models can produce substantially different results for the same source image and editing instruction, and the best-performing model often varies across requests. These models also differ substantially in inference latency, making fixed-model deployment inefficient. We therefore study image editing model routing, which dynamically selects an editor from a candidate pool given an input image and editing instruction. We introduce EditJev, a System One routing model that directly predicts sample-level preference scores over candidate image editing models in a single forward pass. A lightweight preference head on a vision-language backbone produces a fixed-dimensional score vector without autoregressive model-name generation or response parsing. To train EditJev, we construct pairwise preferences from offline candidate outputs and optimize a pairwise ranking objective to learn relative model suitability. At inference time, EditJev combines the predicted preference scores with model-level speed scores to balance editing quality and generation latency. Experiments on ImgEdit and GEdit-En show that EditJev improves aggregate quality over the strongest fixed editor, from 4.540 to 4.592 and from 8.194 to 8.255, respectively, while reducing estimated end-to-end latency by 60.8% and 31.7%. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of direct, structured model routing for efficient image editing.
papers.ja_title: 画像編集モデルを指示ごとに自動で選ぶルーティングモデル EditJev

papers.title: InferSlice: A Reference Architecture for SLO-driven LLM Inference over a Telco Wide-Area Network
papers.abstract: LLM inference is increasingly deployed as a core service for enterprise and interactive applications, but sovereignty, compliance, latency and resource-locality requirements can limit the suitability of centralised cloud deployments. Telco operators offer geographically distributed compute and network infrastructure for addressing these constraints. However, existing LLM serving frameworks are designed for tightly coupled data centres and provide limited support for coordinating geographically distributed and heterogeneous resources. We present InferSlice, a reference architecture for Service-Level Objective (SLO)-driven LLM inference over a telco infrastructure, integrating network slicing, GPU partitioning, elastic serving and observability. Led by BT in collaboration with the University of Bristol and NVIDIA, and realised on the JOINER UK national-scale wide-area network (WAN), InferSlice is evaluated on service differentiation across tiers, elastic scale-out, client-edge bandwidth as a bottleneck, and the reach of tensor, pipeline, data parallelism, and prefill/decode disaggregation over the WAN. Our results show that, on a general-purpose telco network, tiers yield distinct latency-throughput regimes, and weight streaming shortens scale-out time. Replication is placement-insensitive but memory-bound; pipeline parallelism tolerates near- and mid-cross-site hops, while tensor parallelism and disaggregation fail beyond a single subnet hop. We share practical insights from operating SLO-driven inference on a telco network, lessons learned and open questions, and hope to encourage further research on distributed and heterogeneous LLM inference systems.
papers.ja_title: 通信事業者の広域網上で SLO を守りながら LLM 推論を提供する参照アーキテクチャ InferSlice
papers.summary: 企業向け LLM 推論はデータの主権や遅延の制約で一つのデータセンターに閉じ込められないことがあるが、既存の推論基盤は同じデータセンター内の密な結合を前提にしている。BT・ブリストル大学・NVIDIA が英国全土の広域ネットワーク JOINER 上で、ネットワークスライシングと GPU 分割、弾力的なサービス拡張を組み合わせた InferSlice を実際に動かして評価した。結果、拠点間を跨ぐテンソル並列や prefill/decode の分離は 1 回のサブネット越え以降で機能しなくなるのに対し、パイプライン並列は近い拠点間ならネットワークの遅延に耐えられることを確認した。
papers.why: 分散並列(テンソル並列・パイプライン並列・prefill/decode 分離)それぞれがネットワーク遅延にどこまで耐えるかを広域網の実機で具体的に示しており、拠点をまたいだ推論基盤を設計する際の並列化方式の選び方の目安になる。
papers.summary_en: Sovereignty, compliance, latency, and resource-locality requirements can make centralized cloud LLM inference unsuitable, but existing serving frameworks assume a tightly coupled data center and give limited support for geographically distributed, heterogeneous telco infrastructure. InferSlice, led by BT with the University of Bristol and NVIDIA and realized on the UK national-scale JOINER wide-area network, is a reference architecture integrating network slicing, GPU partitioning, elastic serving, and observability, evaluated on service differentiation across tiers, elastic scale-out, client-edge bandwidth bottlenecks, and how far tensor parallelism, pipeline parallelism, data parallelism, and prefill/decode disaggregation reach over a WAN. The results show tiers yield distinct latency-throughput regimes and weight streaming shortens scale-out time; replication is placement-insensitive but memory-bound, pipeline parallelism tolerates near- and mid-cross-site hops, while tensor parallelism and disaggregation fail beyond a single subnet hop.
papers.why_en: Gives real wide-area-network measurements of exactly how far each parallelism strategy (tensor, pipeline, disaggregation) can be stretched across sites, a concrete reference point for anyone designing multi-site inference serving.

papers.title: Peregrine: A Language-Agnostic Packet Processing Intermediate Representation with Formal Guarantees
papers.abstract: Many different programmable network devices and domain-specific languages (DSLs) for programming them have been developed in recent years. However, the affiliated compiler infrastructure for each DSL has not kept up, leading to unreliable compilation results and ultimately a poor experience for developers. In response to this fragmented ecosystem, we propose an intermediate representation, Peregrine, to consolidate the common compiler functionalities within this domain into a shared, open-source infrastructure. We designed Peregrine to provide formal guarantees from the beginning, rather than adding them in a later step. The language comes with a formal semantics, along with an equivalence checker written and proven correct in Rocq. Experimental results show that Peregrine is general enough to express multiple applications written in various state-of-the-art network programming languages. The equivalence checker designed in Peregrine can be used for validating the correctness of a range of untrusted compiler passes, as well as for other surprising use cases such as certifying the correctness of packet classification algorithms within a reasonable amount of time.
papers.theme: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.ja_title: ネットワーク機器向けパケット処理言語を統一する中間表現 Peregrine

papers.title: Tile-Based Decompression in Compiled GPU Engines
papers.abstract: Modern GPUs reach record analytical performance only when a query's working set fits within its GPU memory budget, and that budget is under growing pressure: GPUs are partitioned and shared, working sets are outgrowing high-bandwidth memory (HBM), and HBM is a fixed on-device resource whose per-dollar capacity has stagnated across generations. Lightweight compression can relieve this pressure by shrinking both footprint and bandwidth demand, but existing GPU compressed-execution techniques either bind decompression to a specific execution model or materialize decompressed columns in HBM before query execution. We present a compression subsystem for compiled GPU query engines that treats decompression as a first-class physical operator. Compression-specific logic is isolated behind a narrow backend interface, so new GPU-oriented encodings can be added without rewriting downstream operators. We implement the design in Proteus and study where decompressed values should be materialized in the GPU memory hierarchy. Our compiler-integrated shared-memory strategy fuses cooperative tile decompression with tuple-at-a-time query execution inside a single generated GPU kernel, avoiding decompressed-column materialization in HBM. Compared with HeavyDB and Sirius on GPU-resident data, fused on-chip decompression achieves competitive query times while reducing the resident memory footprint by up to 4x and memory-bandwidth consumption by up to 6x.
papers.ja_title: GPU 上のクエリエンジンでタイル単位にデータを展開する圧縮実行方式

papers.title: Frontier-OPD: Discovering the Edge of Agent Capability and Teaching Agents to Go Beyond
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation aligns teacher feedback with a student's current behavior, yet acquiring useful supervision for multi-turn agents requires identifying both where guidance is needed and whether the student can sustain the interaction afterward. We introduce Frontier-OPD, which addresses this problem through the student's learning frontier: decision situations that remain challenging but admit useful autonomous continuation after brief teacher guidance. To operationalize this frontier, Frontier-OPD organizes on-policy experience into a shared-state trajectory graph, where trajectory-balanced aggregation of teacher-student disagreement identifies distinct intervention candidates while preserving the histories needed for replay. Short teacher bridges are then assessed by comparing agreement over the bridge and the ensuing student continuation with an equally long segment of the original trajectory, providing a behavioral proxy for guidance that the current student can build on. Accepted teacher responses augment ordinary distillation data, and fresh rollouts renew the frontier estimate as the policy changes. Experiments on ALFWorld, WebShop, and ScienceWorld report higher mean autonomous performance than the compared distillation baselines across the evaluated student scales and teacher configurations, with ablations indicating complementary effects of candidate selection and guidance filtering. In one ALFWorld timing setting, the additional collection cost is offset by a shorter time to a target success rate.
papers.ja_title: 生徒が自力で続けられる場面を見つけて教師が助言するオンポリシー蒸留 Frontier-OPD

papers.title: NgramRL: Accelerating RL Post-Training for Structured Generation via Rollout-Aware N-gram Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training improves the reasoning capabilities of large language models, but its cost is dominated by autoregressive rollout generation, which can exceed 70% of training time. Existing speculative-decoding methods are poorly suited to this setting: model-based drafters consume scarce GPU memory and may become misaligned as the policy evolves, while existing model-free methods do not explicitly exploit repetition across training epochs. We observe that recent rollouts of the same prompt provide a high-quality, self-updating draft source. Based on this insight, we propose NgramRL, a per-prompt n-gram drafter constructed from bounded recent rollout history. NgramRL requires no auxiliary model, drafter training, or persistent GPU-resident drafter state, while target-model verification preserves the rollout distribution. To hide CPU cache lookup and scheduling, we further introduce an adaptive fan-out prefetcher that predicts likely verification outcomes (j, b), consisting of the accepted draft length j and target-emitted continuation token b. A causal budget allocator concentrates prefetches on high-probability outcomes, while uncovered outcomes fall back to sequential lookup without changing committed tokens. Across two model families and three reasoning and structured-generation workloads, NgramRL commits 3.60-7.77 tokens per target-model forward in the warm-cache regime, up to 1.99x more than SuffixDecoding and 7.0x more than prompt-lookup decoding. On Spider, the prefetcher covers 96.6% of Qwen3-8B outcomes at a candidate budget of 16 and improves measured rollout throughput by 1.38x over synchronous NgramRL, approaching its 1.40x overlap ceiling.
papers.ja_title: 直前のロールアウトを下書きにして RL のトークン生成を高速化する NgramRL
papers.summary: LLM の強化学習による後段訓練(RL post-training)はトークンを 1 つずつ生成する「ロールアウト」が訓練時間の 7 割以上を占めることがある。NgramRL は同じプロンプトの直近の生成結果を下書き(ドラフト)として使う投機的デコーディング(複数トークンをまとめて予測し検証する高速化手法)で、追加モデルや専用のメモリを持たずに済む。warm なキャッシュの条件では 1 回のモデル呼び出しあたり 3.60〜7.77 トークンを確定でき、既存手法の SuffixDecoding より最大 1.99 倍、prompt-lookup decoding より 7.0 倍多い。Spider というタスクでは先読み機能によりロールアウトの実測スループットを同期版の NgramRL の 1.38 倍まで改善した。
papers.why: RL 訓練のコストの大半を占めるロールアウト生成を、訓練エポックをまたいだ繰り返しという RL 特有の性質を使って高速化しており、既存の投機的デコーディング手法が訓練中のポリシー変化に弱いという弱点を回避する設計になっている。
papers.summary_en: RL post-training's cost is dominated by autoregressive rollout generation, which can exceed 70% of training time, yet existing speculative-decoding drafters are poorly suited here: model-based drafters consume scarce GPU memory and can misalign as the policy evolves, and model-free methods do not explicitly exploit cross-epoch repetition. Observing that recent rollouts of the same prompt provide a high-quality, self-updating draft source, the authors propose NgramRL, a per-prompt n-gram drafter built from bounded recent rollout history that needs no auxiliary model, drafter training, or persistent GPU-resident state, while target-model verification preserves the rollout distribution; an adaptive fan-out prefetcher predicting likely verification outcomes and a causal budget allocator hide CPU cache lookup and scheduling latency. Across two model families and three reasoning/structured-generation workloads, NgramRL commits 3.60-7.77 tokens per target-model forward in the warm-cache regime, up to 1.99x more than SuffixDecoding and 7.0x more than prompt-lookup decoding, and on Spider the prefetcher covers 96.6% of Qwen3-8B outcomes at a candidate budget of 16, improving measured rollout throughput by 1.38x over synchronous NgramRL, approaching its 1.40x overlap ceiling.
