papers.why_en: Exploits an RL-specific property -- repetition of the same prompt across training epochs -- to sidestep the policy-drift weakness of conventional speculative decoding drafters, directly speeding up the rollout stage that dominates RL post-training cost.

papers.title: Where Rounding Happens Matters: Rounding-Location Alignment Stabilizes LLM Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning for large language models often uses separate systems for inference and training. Even with identical weights and BF16 tensors, implementation differences can make an intended on-policy update off-policy and destabilize training. Existing remedies align the entire inference and training stacks, change global precision, or modify the learning algorithm. We ask whether aligning selected parts of the execution stack can stabilize BF16 RL while other implementation differences remain. We align training-side rounding locations with inference in three regions---RoPE, SwiGLU, and residual RMSNorm---by retaining selected intermediates in FP32 until their BF16 outputs. Across four Qwen-family models, aligning all three regions prevents the collapse observed under the default BF16 baseline; RoPE-path alignment alone also suffices in the studied runs, despite remaining numerical discrepancies. The interventions keep the inference engine, matrix-multiplication and attention kernels, and learning objective unchanged.
papers.ja_title: 丸め処理の場所を推論側と揃えることで BF16 の RL 訓練を安定させる手法
papers.summary: LLM の強化学習では推論用システムと訓練用システムが別々に動くため、重みが同じ BF16(16 bit の数値形式)でも実装の細かな違いで、意図した「同じポリシーでの更新」が実質的にずれてしまい訓練が崩れることがある。本研究は全体を揃えるのではなく、RoPE・SwiGLU・残差正規化という 3 箇所だけ、訓練側の丸めの場所を推論側に合わせて FP32(より精度の高い形式)を一部保持する方法を試した。Qwen 系の 4 つのモデルで、3 箇所すべてを揃えると BF16 の既定設定で見られていた訓練の崩壊が起きなくなり、RoPE だけを揃える場合でも十分なことが分かった。
papers.why: 推論エンジンや行列演算のカーネルを変えずに、ごく一部の丸め処理だけを揃えれば RL 訓練の不安定さが直るという結果で、学習・推論の数値的なずれが何に効いているかを切り分ける手がかりになる。
papers.summary_en: RL for LLMs typically splits inference and training across separate systems, and even with identical weights and BF16 tensors, implementation differences can make an intended on-policy update off-policy and destabilize training; existing remedies align the whole stack, change global precision, or modify the learning algorithm. The authors instead ask whether aligning only selected parts of the execution stack can stabilize BF16 RL while other implementation differences remain, aligning training-side rounding locations with inference in three regions -- RoPE, SwiGLU, and residual RMSNorm -- by retaining selected intermediates in FP32 until their BF16 outputs. Across four Qwen-family models, aligning all three regions prevents the collapse observed under the default BF16 baseline, and RoPE-path alignment alone also suffices in the studied runs despite remaining numerical discrepancies, all without changing the inference engine, matmul/attention kernels, or the learning objective.
papers.why_en: Shows RL training collapse from train/inference numerical mismatch can be fixed by aligning rounding at just a few specific points rather than the whole stack, a cheap, localized diagnostic for train-inference precision drift.

papers.title: SceneBloom: Agentic Indoor Environment Generation with Realistic and Diverse Layouts for Embodied Learning
papers.abstract: Training generalizable embodied agents requires realistic, varied, and simulation-ready indoor environments. Language-guided methods support semantic planning and object-level reasoning, but precise spatial grounding remains difficult. Visual generative models offer rich priors over plausible arrangements, yet their outputs require geometric reasoning to become physically valid 3D scenes. We introduce SceneBloom, an agentic framework that combines visual layout sampling with contract-guided 3D compilation. A hierarchical sampler uses diffusion priors to generate furniture arrangements within functional zones. A compiler then uses relations extracted from each proposal to guide geometric fitting and local pose correction. Across five room types, SceneBloom attains the highest visual quality and physical stability among the compared methods and is the only method with no detected mesh collisions and out-of-bounds objects. Its layouts are also closer to the distribution of real rooms than those of all compared baselines. Object navigation policies trained in these realistic scenes achieve a higher success rate in held-out real scans than those trained on an equal number of real training scans. Code is available at https://github.com/Tinaliu0123/scenebloom.
papers.ja_title: ロボット学習向けに室内環境を自動生成するエージェント SceneBloom

papers.title: TraceQuery: learning what to recompute from full-denoising trajectory in diffusion language models
papers.abstract: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) enable flexible generation through iterative masked denoising, but incur substantial inference cost because token representations are repeatedly recomputed across denoising steps. Existing cache-based methods reduce this cost by reusing intermediate results across denoising steps and recomputing only a subset of positions at each step, chosen either on a fixed schedule or by heuristic signals of change. Our trajectory experiments instead point to decoding trajectory as the more relevant quantity. Cached generation remains accurate when it stays close to the full-denoising trajectory, with errors concentrated around unmask-order deviations and reduced as longer reference prefixes are recovered. This suggests a more direct principle: limiting representation error helps, but keeping generation on the full-denoising trajectory is a more direct route to accurate decoding. We therefore formulate efficient dLLM inference as trajectory-guided querying. Rather than broadly repairing representation error, we use full-denoising trajectories to supervise which unresolved positions should receive limited fresh computation. Based on this formulation, we introduce TRACEQUERY, a lightweight sparse decoding framework that predicts a small set of near-future trajectory-relevant positions, queries only those candidates, and lets the backbone select which one to commit from their fresh predictions. TRACEQUERY delivers the strongest quality-computation trade-off among cache-based approaches, sustaining high accuracy with substantially fewer fresh token computations, and generalizes across tasks, model variants, and families. Code: https://github.com/fish1928/tracequery.git
papers.ja_title: 拡散型言語モデルの推論を「完全にノイズ除去した軌跡」で導いて高速化する TraceQuery
papers.summary: 拡散型言語モデル(diffusion LLM、マスクされた文章を繰り返し整えて生成するモデル)は生成の各ステップでトークンの表現を何度も計算し直すため推論コストが高い。従来のキャッシュ手法は表現の変化が小さい部分を再利用するが、本研究は「完全にノイズ除去した場合の軌跡」に近いかどうかの方が精度に直結することを実験で確認した。これに基づき TraceQuery は、軌跡から見て近い将来に重要になりそうな少数の位置だけを予測して計算し直す軽量な手法を提案し、同程度の計算量を使う既存のキャッシュ手法より高い精度と計算量のバランスを達成した。
papers.why: 拡散型 LLM のキャッシュ・再計算戦略を「表現誤差」ではなく「生成軌跡のずれ」という観点で設計し直しており、diffusion LLM の推論サービング最適化における判断基準を示している。
papers.summary_en: Diffusion LLMs generate via iterative masked denoising, incurring heavy inference cost from repeatedly recomputing token representations across steps; existing cache-based methods reuse intermediate results and recompute only a subset of positions chosen by a fixed schedule or heuristic change signals. The authors' trajectory experiments instead point to the decoding trajectory itself as the more relevant quantity: cached generation stays accurate when it tracks the full-denoising trajectory closely, with errors concentrated around unmask-order deviations and reduced by recovering longer reference prefixes. Based on this, TraceQuery is a lightweight sparse decoding framework that uses full-denoising trajectories to predict a small set of near-future trajectory-relevant positions, queries only those candidates, and lets the backbone choose which prediction to commit, delivering the strongest quality-computation trade-off among cache-based approaches while generalizing across tasks, model variants, and families.
papers.why_en: Reframes diffusion-LLM cache/recompute strategy around trajectory deviation rather than representation error, offering a different decision criterion for inference serving optimization of diffusion LLMs.

papers.title: Organon : From Evolutionary Search to Recursive Self-Improving Agents for Scientific Discovery
papers.abstract: Scientific discovery does not follow a single fixed methodology: research methods vary across domains and evolve through experimentation as investigations unfold. Although LLM-guided evolutionary search has advanced automated discovery, existing frameworks typically rely on fixed search procedures or restrict adaptation to predefined components, limiting their ability to address diverse research problems and adapt to challenges that emerge at runtime. We introduce Organon, a recursively self-improving agent for scientific discovery. During execution, a single persistent agent analyzes its accumulated experience and autonomously revises its own search strategies, population management, diagnostic tools, memory, and worker coordination. These revisions take effect at runtime, allowing the agent to continuously adapt its approach as research progresses. Importantly, the agent can also diagnose and correct flaws in its own adaptation procedures, enabling recursive improvement of the mechanisms that guide its future self-improvement. We evaluate Organon across 21 computational discovery tasks spanning algorithm design, GPU kernel optimization, mathematical construction, and systems optimization. On ALE-Bench Lite, Organon achieves the best performance among competing search frameworks on all 10 tasks, improving mean held-out performance by 20.5% over EvoX. On KernelBench, it achieves the best results on three of four workloads, with speedups of up to 1.67x over the strongest competing method. Analysis of the search trajectories further reveals how the agent develops task-specific search strategies, builds new diagnostic capabilities, and corrects or reverses its own earlier revisions. We implement Organon using DeepSeek Harness and Cordis's spatiotemporal composability. Code is available at https://github.com/cheikh025/Organon.
papers.ja_title: 研究の進め方自体を自分で書き換える再帰的自己改善エージェント Organon

papers.title: OvisOCR3 Technical Report
papers.abstract: We introduce OvisOCR3, a 0.8B model for a broad range of OCR-related tasks. OvisOCR3 unifies document parsing, general OCR, key information extraction (KIE), document figure captioning, and cross-page table reconstruction in a single model. We train the model on real and synthetic data through continued pretraining and use domain-balanced mid-training to balance supervision across tasks with different data volumes and response lengths. Multi-teacher on-policy distillation transfers expertise from five domain-specific 4B teachers into the shared model, followed by mixed-task reinforcement learning with domain-specific rewards. We compare OvisOCR3 with general-purpose vision-language models and specialized OCR models on public and in-house benchmarks covering all five task families. In these comparisons, it achieves an overall score of 96.74 on OmniDocBench v1.6 and the highest overall scores on PureDocBench, Real5-OmniDocBench, and MDPBench. On OCRBench v2, it ranks first, scoring 65.9 and 61.3 on the English and Chinese splits, respectively. It also outperforms the baselines on OCRBench and all four KIE benchmarks. On DocFigCapBench, it achieves the highest localization F1 and a caption score close to that of Qwen3.8-Max. For cross-page tables, it leads in Relation F1 on CrossTabBench and truncated-table TEDS on MPDocBench-Parse. These results demonstrate that a compact 0.8B model can achieve strong performance across diverse OCR-related tasks. OvisOCR3 is available at https://huggingface.co/ATH-MaaS/OvisOCR3.
papers.ja_title: 文書解析から表構造復元までを 1 つでまとめる 0.8B の OCR モデル OvisOCR3

papers.title: Modeling Liquid-Cooled Data Centers in EnergyPlus
papers.abstract: As AI workloads accelerate data center transition toward high-density racks with direct-to-chip (DTC) liquid cooling, existing simulation tools remain limited in evaluating whole-building and multi-year efficiency. To bridge this gap, we develop a native EnergyPlus object, ElectricEquipment:ITE:LiquidCooled, that models DTC liquid cooling for chilled-water and warm-water architectures as plant-loop components. It couples facility-water loops, rack-side secondary loops, coolant distribution units, and chip-junction temperatures within a single solver. Validation against an independent Modelica implementation across 21 operating conditions, including two full-year runs compared at one-minute resolution, yields loop-temperature RMSE at or below 0.021 K, well within the 0.1 K acceptance threshold. Our case study demonstrates that warm-water liquid cooling reduces annual PUE from 1.43 to 1.25, eliminates on-site water use, and cuts total facility energy by 37.9% relative to an air-cooled baseline. By embedding liquid-cooling logic into EnergyPlus, our work provides whole-building, long-term energy modeling for high-density AI infrastructure within an open-source framework.
papers.ja_title: AI データセンターの液冷設備をビル全体のシミュレータ EnergyPlus で再現する手法

papers.title: AOS-Bench: Can LLM Agents Manage Dynamic Workloads?
papers.abstract: Coding agents are moving from handling one request at a time to serving as persistent assistants to which users hand a stream of work: a build, a data-processing job and a bug fix may all be pending on the same machine at once. Such an agent must decide when to take on new tasks, how to delegate and overlap them, and how to stay within the machine's CPU and memory. Existing benchmarks cannot measure this, because they evaluate each task in isolation. We introduce AOS-Bench, which evaluates an agent system as a workload manager: verified tasks arrive over time and must be delivered under shared CPU and memory limits, and the same tasks run one at a time serve as a per-system reference. Across five model--harness pairs, isolated task success does not carry over evenly. On heavy workloads every system loses 13 to 23 points. On medium workloads, systems span 11 points in isolated success but 26 points in stream success, and two systems 0.6 points apart in isolation deliver 54\% and 68\% of the same tasks. Execution-policy interventions trace much of this gap to task intake: serial dispatch leaves 73\% of heavy-workload tasks unclaimed. Yet more elaborate management does not necessarily help. A fixed concurrency of two comes within four points of the best agent-managed policy on both medium and heavy workloads, and under every policy median CPU use stays below 30\% of the provisioned cores while tasks wait. These results identify workload management as a distinct capability for agents, and AOS-Bench as a way to measure it.
papers.ja_title: 複数のタスクを同時に抱えたときのエージェントの資源管理力を測るベンチマーク AOS-Bench

papers.title: Vision Token Pruning via Query-Vision Interaction Decomposition
papers.abstract: Large vision-language models (VLMs), which process both visual inputs and text queries, incur high inference costs due to the large number of visual tokens, making visual token pruning a natural approach for improving efficiency. Recent work has leveraged query information to guide token selection, often through heuristics derived from attention patterns or token dynamics. However, these approaches do not explicitly exploit the underlying structure of query-vision interactions. We address this gap by observing that the query-vision interaction matrix, naturally induced by the query and key projections already present in transformer attention, is effectively low-rank, with a small number of dominant latent interaction modes capturing query-relevant semantics. Motivated by this observation, we propose Query-Vision Decomposition (QViD), a novel training-free query-aware visual token pruning method that exploits this structure. Extensive experiments on both image and video understanding benchmarks show that QViD consistently improves performance under matched token budgets, with the largest gains appearing under aggressive compression regimes.
papers.ja_title: 問い合わせとの関係が低次元にまとまることを使った視覚言語モデルの画像トークン削減 QViD
papers.summary: 画像と文章を両方扱う視覚言語モデル(VLM)は画像トークンの数が多く推論コストが高いため、重要度の低い画像トークンを削る「トークン剪定」が使われる。本研究は、質問文と画像トークンの関連度を表す行列が実際には少数の支配的なパターンに要約できる(低ランクである)ことを見つけ、この構造を利用した学習不要の剪定手法 QViD を提案した。画像・動画の理解ベンチマークで、同じトークン数の予算の下で既存手法より高い性能を示し、削減率を強くするほど効果の差が大きくなった。
papers.why: 画像トークン剪定をヒューリスティックな注目度ではなく、質問と画像の関係行列の数学的な構造(低ランク性)から導いており、VLM 推論の軽量化手法を選ぶ際の理論的な裏付けになる。
papers.summary_en: Vision-language models incur high inference cost from large numbers of visual tokens, making query-aware visual token pruning attractive, but prior work guides token selection through heuristics from attention patterns or token dynamics without explicitly exploiting the structure of query-vision interactions. The authors observe that the query-vision interaction matrix induced by existing query/key projections is effectively low-rank, with a small number of dominant latent interaction modes capturing query-relevant semantics, and propose QViD, a training-free, query-aware pruning method built on this structure. On image and video understanding benchmarks, QViD consistently improves performance under matched token budgets, with the largest gains under aggressive compression.
papers.why_en: Grounds visual token pruning in the mathematical low-rank structure of the query-vision interaction rather than attention heuristics, giving a theoretical basis for choosing a VLM inference lightening method.

papers.title: CCAaaS: An Orchestration Platform for High-Velocity Design, Development, and Deployment of Data Center Transports at Meta
papers.abstract: Today, data center networks run multiple congestion control algorithms (CCAs), each tailored to distinct traffic characteristics, from latency-sensitive intra-region RPCs to high-throughput cross-region AI workloads. The rapid evolution of AI training and inference further accelerates this trend by continually introducing new traffic characteristics that demand new CCAs. This paper introduces CCA-as-a-Service (CCAaaS), our eBPF-based ecosystem for the rapid design, deployment, and operation of production-grade CCAs at hyperscale. We present (1) a modular BPF-TCP framework and general lessons for designing modular CCAs; (2) a deployment and orchestration layer that provides disruption-free CCA updates, along with best practices for managing a zoo of CCAs at scale; and (3) a lightweight observability tool for CCAs and a blueprint for scaling CCA observability. CCAaaS manages over 97% of our server-to-server traffic using three active eBPF-based CCAs; two of the five CCAs we have built have since been deprecated. We show that our eBPF-centric approach to CCAs development delivers the same application-level performance (retransmissions, bandwidth, and tail latency) as their native in-kernel counterparts, and that our custom CCAs add negligible CPU and memory cost over their eBPF baselines. In terms of realized benefits, the CCA built with CCAaaS significantly improved network, and application metrics, for example, one of our CCAs reduced P99 latency for cross-region services by up to 20X.
topics: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.theme: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.ja_title: Meta のデータセンター内輸送制御を eBPF でサービス化する CCAaaS
papers.summary: データセンターのネットワークでは、低遅延が必要な社内通信と AI の訓練・推論で出る大量データ転送など、トラフィックの性質に応じて異なる輻輳制御アルゴリズム(CCA、送信速度を調整する仕組み)を使い分ける必要がある。Meta は eBPF(カーネルを再起動せずに機能を差し替えられる技術)を使って CCA を素早く開発・展開・運用できる基盤 CCAaaS を構築し、サーバー間通信の 97% 以上を 3 種類の eBPF ベース CCA で運用している。独自に作った CCA の一つは、拠点間サービスの P99 レイテンシ(99 パーセンタイルの遅延)を最大 20 倍改善し、カーネル内蔵の実装と比べても CPU やメモリの追加コストはごく小さかった。
papers.why: AI の訓練・推論トラフィックが増える中でネットワークの輻輳制御を迅速に差し替える仕組みの実例で、データセンター規模で輻輳制御を運用する際の設計とコストの実測値が得られる。
papers.summary_en: Data center networks run multiple congestion control algorithms (CCAs) tailored to different traffic -- from latency-sensitive intra-region RPCs to high-throughput cross-region AI workloads -- and the rapid evolution of AI training/inference keeps introducing traffic patterns that demand new CCAs. Meta's CCAaaS is an eBPF-based ecosystem for rapidly designing, deploying, and operating production-grade CCAs at hyperscale, comprising a modular BPF-TCP framework, a disruption-free deployment/orchestration layer with best practices for managing a zoo of CCAs, and a lightweight CCA observability tool. CCAaaS manages over 97% of Meta's server-to-server traffic using three active eBPF-based CCAs (two of the five built have since been deprecated), matches native in-kernel application-level performance (retransmissions, bandwidth, tail latency) with negligible added CPU/memory cost, and one of its CCAs reduced cross-region P99 latency by up to 20x.
papers.why_en: A production example of rapidly iterating on network congestion control to match growing AI-driven traffic, with concrete hyperscale operating experience and measured costs/benefits of the eBPF-centric approach.

papers.title: All-in-One: A Composable Attack on LLM Transformations
papers.abstract: Quantization, pruning, and model merging are popular transformations applied to deployment-ready LLMs to improve efficiency and downstream performance. Recent work has shown that these transformations can introduce a security threat: an adversary can train a model that passes safety checks in its pre-transformed state, only turning malicious once it is transformed for deployment. However, prior attacks target one specific transformation (e.g., quantization) and generally rely on transformation-specific techniques, making them difficult to combine in practice. In this work, we introduce a simple, composable attack framework that targets multiple transformations simultaneously and triggers when any one of them is applied by a user. Our key insight is that the effect of each transformation can be approximated as a perturbation to the model weights, allowing us to jointly train the model with a benign loss on the original model and a malicious loss on each simulated transformed model. These perturbations are simple enough to simulate at every training iteration across diverse transformations, making them practically combinable within a single training objective, enabling a unified attack. Through extensive experiments across attack scenarios, model families, and a wide range of deployment-time model transformations, we show that our attack achieves high success rates. This demonstrates that model transformations may be utilized to trigger significantly different behavior from the original model and reinforces the associated security concerns by demonstrating that a single attack can jointly target diverse transformations.
papers.ja_title: 量子化・枝刈り・モデル統合をまとめて狙う複合的な攻撃手法

papers.title: Nemo: Efficient Caching with Index Pushdown for Disaggregated OLTP Databases
papers.abstract: Storage-disaggregated databases decouple compute from storage, improving elasticity but suffering from network bottlenecks. Most cloud databases use page-based B+trees and buffer pools. Under disaggregation, each index traversal incurs serial network round-trips. Page-granularity transfers and caching also amplify network traffic and lower cache efficiency. Pushing down the full index to storage and caching only hot records at compute is appealing, but an efficient design must (1) provide a holistic record cache that accelerates both point and range queries, (2) mitigate the negative search penalty of confirming non-existence via remote probes, and (3) enforce phantom protection despite the index being encapsulated by the storage service. We introduce Nemo, a holistic index-and-buffer design optimized for storage-disaggregated OLTP with index pushdown. Nemo employs a tree-structured record buffer that unifies caching and buffering and accelerates both point and range queries. It further reduces the negative search penalty by caching negative search results. Nemo provides phantom protection that requires no knowledge of the storage-side data layout and is robust against large key domains, varying data skew, and partition schemes. Experiments show that Nemo outperforms page-based B+Tree and the state-of-the-art 2-Tree by up to 11.42x and 2.97x on positive point queries, and achieves up to 4.76x speedup on negative searches over a hash-indexed record cache. For phantom protection, Nemo outperforms PCL by up to 1.55x even under a dense key domain. Moreover, Nemo maintains stable performance while PCL degrades sharply as the key domain grows large and sparse.
papers.ja_title: ストレージ分離型 OLTP データベース向けのインデックス押し下げキャッシュ Nemo

papers.title: When Does Pre-Trained Capacity Help Causal Learning? From Scalar Prediction to Counterfactual Post-Training
papers.abstract: How does pre-trained model capacity relate to performance after adaptation for causal tasks? We study two systems built on the Qwen 2.5 family: CausalLLM, which estimates scalar potential outcomes with treatment-specific heads, and CausalGen, which generates treatment-conditioned text or code using soft prefixes and factual supervised fine-tuning (SFT), counterfactual SFT, and preference alignment. Increasing backbone size from 0.5B to 1.5B yields mixed scalar-estimation results on IHDP, but improves CodeGen pass@1 from 0.267 to 0.575 and treatment-effect score from 0.231 to 0.515 after the complete generative pipeline. Within 0.5B CausalLLM, narrative inputs reduce mean sqrt(PEHE) from 1.842 to 1.780, a 3.4% improvement over tabular inputs; the 5.8% improvement over a no-LLM baseline combines changes in representation and input format. These descriptive comparisons motivate a distinction between available and convertible capacity. They do not isolate the contribution of post-training: the two systems differ in dataset, architecture, output modality, and supervision, and intermediate-stage evaluations are unavailable. With only two small backbones and three replications, the results support a hypothesis about capacity--adaptation alignment rather than a general scaling law or a demonstrated causal mechanism.

papers.title: Information-Theoretic Scaling Laws for Generative Diffusion Training
papers.abstract: Diffusion models trained on increasingly large datasets sampled from the same data distribution will converge to the same learned distribution. However, in practice, a model trained on finite data depends on the particular training dataset; this dependence is reflected in properties of the model's outputs, such as memorization and sample quality. To understand this dependence through an information-theoretic lens, we study \textit{model information}, a computationally tractable measure of how much samples from the trained model depend on the particular training dataset. We explore its scaling behavior as model size and training dataset size vary. Specifically, we uncover two qualitatively distinct scaling regimes: (1) a nonlinear model information regime marking the transition from pure memorization to imperfect generalization, and (2) a generalization regime characterized by linear scaling of the model information and progressively improved generalization and sample quality. We then posit an information-theoretically principled scaling law to quantify these two regimes, and show that this law yields induced scaling laws for memorization and sample quality. We finally demonstrate that these induced scaling laws extrapolate well outside the fit's domain. Our results demonstrate information-theoretic principles for memorization and sample quality scaling laws in diffusion models. Our code is publicly available on \href{https://github.com/DruvPai/diffusion_info_theory_scaling_law}{GitHub}.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 拡散モデルの記憶と汎化を情報量の指標でスケーリング則として説明する研究
papers.summary: 同じデータ分布から十分大きいデータで訓練した拡散モデルは同じ分布に収束するはずだが、実際には有限のデータで訓練したモデルの出力は訓練データそのものに依存し、記憶(訓練データをそのまま覚えてしまう現象)や生成品質に表れる。本研究は、生成結果が特定の訓練データにどれだけ依存するかを測る「モデル情報量」という指標を定義し、モデルサイズと訓練データ量を変えたときの変化を調べた。その結果、単純な記憶から汎化への移行を示す非線形な領域と、モデル情報量が線形に増えながら汎化と生成品質が改善していく領域という 2 つの異なる段階を見つけ、この関係をスケーリング則として定式化すると、記憶や生成品質についても当てはめた範囲の外側までよく当てはまることを示した。
papers.why: モデルサイズとデータ量をどう配分すれば記憶(学習データの漏えいリスク)と生成品質がどう変わるかを予測する枠組みで、拡散モデルの訓練計算資源の配分を決める際の指標として使える。
papers.summary_en: Diffusion models trained on increasingly large data sampled from the same distribution should converge to the same learned distribution, but in practice a model trained on finite data depends on its particular training set, a dependence reflected in memorization and sample quality. The authors study 'model information,' a computationally tractable measure of how much a trained model's samples depend on the particular training set, and its scaling with model size and dataset size, uncovering two qualitatively distinct regimes: a nonlinear regime marking the transition from pure memorization to imperfect generalization, and a generalization regime with linear scaling of model information alongside progressively improved generalization and sample quality. They posit an information-theoretically principled scaling law for these regimes, derive induced scaling laws for memorization and sample quality, and show these extrapolate well outside the fit's domain.
papers.why_en: Offers a framework for predicting how memorization (a data-leakage risk) and generation quality trade off as model size and data size are scaled, usable as a metric for allocating diffusion-model training compute.

papers.title: MOSHO: A Native Discrete Shark-Inspired Metaheuristic for Hardware-Aware Neural Architecture Search
papers.abstract: Hardware-aware neural architecture search (NAS) requires jointly optimizing predictive accuracy and device-specific latency over discrete search spaces. While multi-objective swarm optimizers show promise, continuous formulations such as the Multi-Objective White Shark Optimizer (MOWSO) can suffer from quantization noise when rounded to integer-encoded architecture vectors. To address this limitation, we propose MOSHO (Multi-Objective Shark Hunting Optimization), a native discrete metaheuristic that replaces continuous motion equations with discrete architecture-editing operators. MOSHO integrates adaptive operator scheduling, energy-regulated restarts, and deferred crowding-distance truncation to enhance exploration and search efficiency. On the merged NAS-Bench-201/HW-NAS-Bench benchmark across 18 contexts, MOSHO achieves a median normalized hypervolume of 0.9987 and IGD+ of 0.0064, yielding Pareto fronts competitive with NSGA-II while reducing search runtime by 96.4% (0.64 s vs. 17.72 s). These results demonstrate that tailored discrete search mechanisms can enable swarm optimizers to achieve high-quality multi-objective solution quality with substantially lower search cost in hardware-aware NAS.
papers.ja_title: サメの狩り行動を模した離散最適化によるハードウェア考慮型ニューラルアーキテクチャ探索 MOSHO

papers.title: How To Build A Modern Diffusion Language Model
papers.abstract: The frontier of large language model (LLM) performance has advanced rapidly in recent years, fueled by scaling laws for pretraining on large text corpora. However, mainstream LLMs have fundamental limitations: they generate text autoregressively, producing outputs sequentially from left to right one token at a time. This sequential process leaves parallel GPU hardware underutilized during inference--a bottleneck that has grown acute as progress shifts toward scaling post-training and inference-time compute--and commits irreversibly to each token without the ability to revise earlier mistakes. Discrete diffusion models address these limitations by generating tokens in parallel, starting from a noisy or masked sequence and iteratively refining the entire output over a series of denoising steps. This parallel generative process enables speeds of thousands of tokens per second, provides a new axis of inference-time compute scaling, and supports built-in error correction and controllable generation. Over the past two years, discrete diffusion has scaled to billions of parameters across biological sequence modeling and natural language, with open-weights and commercial releases from leading labs. This article provides a survey of key ideas in discrete diffusion and a high-level introduction to how modern diffusion LLMs are built, covering their foundations, core algorithmic and architectural building blocks, applications in biology and language, and implications for future LLM scaling laws.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 現代の拡散型言語モデルの作り方を整理したサーベイ
papers.summary: 主流の LLM は文章を 1 トークンずつ左から順番に生成するため、並列処理が得意な GPU を十分に使い切れず、一度出したトークンの間違いを後から直せないという弱点がある。離散拡散モデル(discrete diffusion)は、マスクされた文章全体を繰り返し整えることで複数トークンを同時に生成でき、1 秒あたり数千トークンという速度や、生成の途中で誤りを直せる性質を実現できる。本稿は過去 2 年で数十億パラメータ規模まで広がった拡散型言語モデルの基礎・アーキテクチャ・応用・今後のスケーリング則への影響を整理したサーベイである。
papers.why: 自己回帰型とは異なる並列生成アーキテクチャの設計要素を一通り把握できるため、推論の並列度やスケーリング則が大きく変わりうる次世代アーキテクチャの選択肢を検討する際の整理に使える。
papers.summary_en: Mainstream autoregressive LLMs generate left-to-right one token at a time, leaving parallel GPU hardware underutilized during inference -- a bottleneck growing more acute as progress shifts to scaling post-training and inference-time compute -- and committing irreversibly to each token without revision. Discrete diffusion models instead generate tokens in parallel by iteratively refining a noisy or masked sequence, enabling thousands of tokens per second, a new axis of inference-time compute scaling, and built-in error correction and controllable generation; over the past two years discrete diffusion has scaled to billions of parameters across biological sequences and natural language, with open-weight and commercial releases from leading labs. This article surveys the foundations, core algorithmic/architectural building blocks, biology and language applications, and implications for future LLM scaling laws.
papers.why_en: Provides a comprehensive overview of the architectural building blocks of an alternative, parallel-generation architecture, useful for assessing a next-generation option whose inference parallelism and scaling laws differ substantially from autoregressive models.

papers.title: An Empirical Study of Reinforcement Learning Scaling Laws
papers.abstract: The discovery of scaling laws enables prediction of the performance, the optimal resource allocation strategy, and the best hyperparameter configuration of a large-scale training job based on inexpensive experiments at smaller scales. Guided by these empirical scaling laws, the deep learning community has achieved great success in training large (self-)supervised models on Internet-scale datasets. In contrast, despite its potential and wide application, reinforcement learning (RL) has yet to find a guiding principle for predictable scaling. In this work, we conduct an empirical study of RL scaling laws of an actor-critic algorithm in two procedurally generated environments, Starpilot and Craftax. We discover empirical scaling laws with strong predictive performance in both environments. The discovered scaling laws accurately predict the aforementioned three quantities for larger-scale training jobs up to two orders of magnitude in total training compute. In particular, we employ a variant of Elo scores for the single-agent RL paradigm as an alternative performance metric than the commonly used mean episode return. Our results show that the Elo score is a much more predictable metric than the mean episode return, making it a better choice for fitting scaling laws. By applying our discovered scaling laws to increase training compute, we establish a new state of the art in the challenging Craftax environment. Beneath the surface of the global scaling trend, we also observe a non-monotonic scaling pattern of the compute-optimal model size in Craftax. We connect this observation to a pathology known as Ray interference.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 強化学習のスケーリング則を実験で確かめた研究
papers.summary: 教師あり学習ではスケーリング則(モデルサイズや計算量を増やすと性能がどう伸びるか)を使って小規模な実験から大規模訓練の性能や最適な資源配分を予測できるが、強化学習にはまだそうした指針がなかった。本研究は Starpilot と Craftax という 2 つのゲーム環境で actor-critic 法のスケーリング則を実験的に求め、最大で学習計算量を 2 桁(100 倍)変えた範囲まで性能・最適資源配分・最適なハイパーパラメータを正確に予測できることを示した。また、よく使われる平均エピソード報酬よりも Elo スコア(対戦相手との強さを表す指標)の方が予測しやすい指標であることを見つけ、これを使って Craftax で新しい最高性能を達成した。
papers.why: 強化学習でも教師あり学習と同様に小規模実験から大規模訓練の資源配分を予測できる可能性を示しており、RL 訓練の計算資源をどこに割り振るかという判断に使える具体的な指標(Elo スコア)を提案している。
papers.summary_en: Scaling laws let the deep-learning community predict performance, optimal resource allocation, and best hyperparameters for large supervised/self-supervised training from cheap small-scale experiments, but RL has lacked a comparable guiding principle despite its potential and wide application. The authors empirically study RL scaling laws for an actor-critic algorithm in two procedurally generated environments, Starpilot and Craftax, discovering laws with strong predictive performance that accurately forecast the three quantities above for training jobs up to two orders of magnitude larger in total compute. They also show that a variant of Elo scores is a far more predictable alternative to the commonly used mean episode return for fitting scaling laws, and by applying the discovered laws to scale up compute they set a new state of the art on Craftax, while also observing -- and connecting to the Ray interference pathology -- a non-monotonic scaling pattern in Craftax's compute-optimal model size.
papers.why_en: Shows RL training compute allocation may be predictable from small-scale experiments much like supervised learning, and proposes a concrete, more scaling-law-friendly metric (Elo score) to use instead of mean episode return.

papers.title: Learning When to Collaborate: Selective Multi-Agent Medical Reasoning via Uncertainty-Aware Routing
papers.abstract: Multi-agent systems have emerged as a promising paradigm for multimodal medical reasoning, but existing methods rely on two assumptions that hinder practical deployment: (i) always-active dense collaboration among multiple agents, and (ii) dependence on large cloud-based models that raise privacy and efficiency concerns. In this paper, we challenge both assumptions and propose SMART-Med, a fully local multi-agent method that treats collaboration as a learnable decision rather than a default behavior. Our key insight is that not every medical query requires costly multi-agent deliberation: many can be reliably solved by a single well-trained agent, while only uncertain cases benefit from expert collaboration. Based on this insight, SMART-Med introduces an uncertainty-driven routing mechanism that adaptively decides when to answer directly and when to recruit a small subset of expert agents, effectively converting dense multi-agent reasoning into selective, query-adaptive coordination. To make this routing reliable, we curate a new multimodal medical dataset MedVR-3K with high-quality reasoning traces and a difficulty hierarchy, and then fine-tune local agents using GRPO with two complementary rewards: a certainty-aware accuracy reward and a vision-language reward model for correctness and reasoning quality respectively. Experiments on four medical visual question answering benchmarks show that SMART-Med achieves competitive performance compared to existing MAS approaches while substantially reducing inference cost (reducing inference time by more than 3.8x and token usage by 72%). Moreover, after fine-tuning on MedVR-3K, SMART-Med yields an average improvement of 6.7% across Slake, PathVQA, VQA-RAD, and PMC-VQA.
papers.ja_title: 必要なときだけ複数の医療エージェントを協調させる不確実性ベースのルーティング SMART-Med

papers.title: RAQ-MLA: Role-Aware Quantization for Multi-Head Latent Attention Caches
papers.abstract: Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA) has been adopted by recent frontier large language models. Instead of per-head keys and values, MLA caches a compressed KV latent that is up-projected into keys and values at decode time, together with a narrow positional key that carries position information into the attention score. Existing KV-cache quantization methods are designed around the keys and values of standard attention and do not account for what MLA actually caches, which costs accuracy at low bit widths. We analyze the MLA cache both in activation distribution and in how quantization error propagates to the attention output, and show that the two cached tensors play different roles: the latent mainly supplies the values, whereas the positional key dominates the attention score. We therefore propose RAQ-MLA (Role-Aware Quantization for Multi-Head Latent Attention Caches), which fits an invertible transform to each cached tensor against the error that tensor delivers to the attention output: attention-weighted value error for the latent and score perturbation for the positional key. Without training, RAQ-MLA quantizes the full MLA cache to about 2.5 bits per element, a 6.5x increase in theoretical KV-cache capacity, while remaining nearly lossless on reasoning and coding tasks across four MLA models.
papers.ja_title: Multi-Head Latent Attention の KV キャッシュを役割ごとに分けて量子化する RAQ-MLA
papers.summary: 最新の LLM が採用する Multi-Head Latent Attention(MLA)は、通常の注意機構とは異なり、圧縮された潜在表現と位置情報を持つ別のキーを KV キャッシュ(過去の計算結果を覚えておく領域)に保存する。既存の KV キャッシュ量子化手法は通常の注意機構向けに作られているため、MLA のキャッシュに使うと低いビット数で精度が落ちてしまう。本研究は、潜在表現は主に値(value)を、位置情報付きキーは注意の重みを決める役割を担うという違いに着目し、それぞれの役割に応じた変換を適用する RAQ-MLA を提案し、追加学習なしで MLA のキャッシュを 1 要素あたり約 2.5 bit(理論上の容量は 6.5 倍)まで圧縮しても、推論とコーディングのタスクでほぼ精度を落とさなかった。
papers.why: MLA を採用する最新モデル特有のキャッシュ構造に合わせて量子化を設計し直しており、KV キャッシュの省メモリ化を検討する際に「通常の注意機構用の手法をそのまま流用できない」という具体的な落とし穴と解決策を示している。
papers.summary_en: Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA), adopted by recent frontier LLMs, caches a compressed KV latent (up-projected into keys/values at decode time) together with a narrow positional key carrying position information into the attention score, but existing KV-cache quantization methods are designed around standard attention's keys/values and don't account for what MLA actually caches, costing accuracy at low bit widths. Analyzing both activation distribution and how quantization error propagates to the attention output, the authors find the latent mainly supplies values while the positional key dominates the attention score, and propose RAQ-MLA, which fits an invertible transform to each cached tensor against the error it actually delivers to the attention output (attention-weighted value error for the latent, score perturbation for the positional key). Without any training, RAQ-MLA quantizes the full MLA cache to about 2.5 bits per element -- a 6.5x increase in theoretical KV-cache capacity -- while remaining nearly lossless on reasoning and coding tasks across four MLA models.
papers.why_en: Redesigns KV-cache quantization around the specific role split inside MLA's cache rather than reusing standard-attention quantization methods, exposing a concrete pitfall and fix for memory-saving work on newer MLA-based models.

papers.title: Speeding up Log-Sum-Exp: Kernel Fusion at the Memory Wall, Integer Arithmetic at the Compute Wall
papers.abstract: While the Log-Sum-Exp (LSE) function is a foundational numerical primitive for stable log-domain computation in modern machine learning, its fast and efficient computation on generic platforms (\ie, CPUs and GPUs) has been underexplored, potentially creating execution bottlenecks for large workloads. On GPU, the de facto implementation $\texttt{torch.logsumexp}$ dispatches a chain of nine sub-kernels per call, incurring redundant High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) traffic and launch overhead. On CPU, exp and log operations are hardware-hungry, limiting the computing efficiency. To address these bottlenecks, we propose two drop-in kernels to significantly accelerate LSE computation on both GPUs and CPUs: FuseLSE, a single-pass fused kernel that evaluates LSE's exp and log functions on the GPU's Special Function Unit (SFU); and IntLSE, which further replaces the LSE computation with approximated integer arithmetic for CPU computation. Our experiments, validated by benchmarks across workload sizes and hardware platforms, show that both kernels are ${\sim}10-11\times$ faster than PyTorch at small workloads and ${\sim}6\times$ faster on larger ones on GPUs, where the speed-up is attributed to reduced launch overhead and HBM traffic. On CPU, where no SFU is available, LSE computation dominates the cost, allowing IntLSE to gain ${\sim}3-6\times$ execution speed over FuseLSE.
papers.ja_title: Log-Sum-Exp 計算を GPU のカーネル融合と CPU の整数演算で高速化する手法
papers.summary: Log-Sum-Exp(LSE)は機械学習の数値計算を安定させるための基本的な演算だが、PyTorch の標準実装は GPU 上で 9 個のサブカーネルを連続して呼び出すため、メモリ帯域(HBM、GPU の主記憶との転送量)の無駄や起動オーバーヘッドが大きい。本研究は GPU 向けに 1 回のカーネル呼び出しで済ませる FuseLSE と、CPU 向けに整数演算で近似する IntLSE という 2 つの代替カーネルを提案した。実験では、小規模な処理で PyTorch より約 10〜11 倍、大規模な処理でも約 6 倍高速化し、CPU では専用の演算回路がない分 IntLSE が FuseLSE よりさらに 3〜6 倍速かった。
papers.why: 一見小さな演算であっても標準実装の非効率(サブカーネルの多さ、メモリ転送)が大きな速度低下を招くことを示しており、カーネル融合や低精度・整数近似が効く具体例として他の数値演算の高速化にも応用できる。
papers.summary_en: The Log-Sum-Exp (LSE) function is a foundational primitive for stable log-domain computation in ML, yet its fast computation on generic CPU/GPU platforms has been underexplored; on GPU, PyTorch's de facto torch.logsumexp dispatches a chain of nine sub-kernels per call, incurring redundant HBM traffic and launch overhead, while on CPU exp/log operations are hardware-hungry and limit efficiency. The authors propose two drop-in kernels: FuseLSE, a single-pass fused GPU kernel that evaluates LSE's exp and log on the GPU's Special Function Unit, and IntLSE, which further replaces LSE computation with approximated integer arithmetic for CPU. Benchmarked across workload sizes and hardware platforms, both kernels are about 10-11x faster than PyTorch at small workloads and about 6x faster at larger ones on GPU (from reduced launch overhead and HBM traffic), while on CPU, where no Special Function Unit exists and LSE computation dominates cost, IntLSE gains about 3-6x execution speed over FuseLSE.
papers.why_en: Demonstrates that even a seemingly minor numerical primitive can suffer large overhead from an unfused, multi-kernel standard implementation, a concrete example of where kernel fusion and integer approximation pay off.

papers.title: A Distribution-Matching Perspective on LLM Training Algorithms
papers.abstract: In this work, we propose a unified framework for training algorithms across different stages of modern large language model development, based on the perspective of distribution matching. We show that a broad class of language model training algorithms can be interpreted as minimizing a certain divergence between the current model and a target distribution, and that characterizing the properties of this target distribution provides substantial insight into the behavior of the corresponding training algorithms. By analyzing specific forms of the target distribution, we establish that On-Policy Distillation (OPD) enjoys an advantage over classical Knowledge Distillation (KD) when the current model distribution is close to the target distribution, while exhibiting a disadvantage when the two distributions are far apart. Furthermore, when the target distribution itself depends on the model being optimized, we show that the accumulation of estimation variance can induce a deterministic degradation of the target distribution. These results provide a theoretical explanation, at least in part, for the long-term behavior of existing Reinforcement Learning (RL) algorithms. With this intuition we further designed Conditional KL (CKL) regularization for mitigating the degradation of the target distribution. CKL can effectively preserve mode diversity while relaxing the constraint imposed by classical KL regularization on reward improvements. We believe this theoretical perspective can bring some new understanding of language model training algorithms and provide useful guidance for future research.
papers.ja_title: LLM の訓練アルゴリズムを「分布を一致させる」という観点で統一的に説明する理論研究

papers.title: Software Engineering LLMs: Why We Need Them and How Software Engineering Helps Build Them
papers.abstract: Software engineering (SE) expertise can shape how coding large language models (LLMs) are trained and which engineering capabilities they acquire. We examine this role through an industrial case study of capability-focused training for a 92B-parameter coding LLM serving more than 100,000 developers. We demonstrate how established SE knowledge can guide the selection of engineering capabilities, the construction of verifiable training data, and the evaluation of model improvements. To target repository-level refactoring, we developed RefactorForge, a pipeline that combines refactoring knowledge, established SE tools, and verification techniques to construct training data. Across 306 Python repositories, RefactorForge generated 5,704 executable tasks and retained 4,572 verified teacher trajectories totaling 72.51 million tokens. Incremental supervised fine-tuning on these trajectories, accounting for 0.46% of the preceding coding mixture's tokens, improved RefactorBench performance by 18.00 percentage points and SWE-Bench ProMax performance by 7.06 points. Under OpenCode, these improvements extended to SWE issue resolution, with gains of 4.97 points on SWE-Bench Verified and 1.23 points on SWE-Bench Pro. Improvements also persisted across other coding-agent harnesses, while greenfield repository generation showed mixed results. We report lessons from constructing capability-focused training data and evaluating its effects across engineering workloads. Building on this industrial experience, we propose a research agenda for expanding SE's role in transforming coding LLMs into SE LLMs: incorporating SE knowledge into model training, applying engineering methods to model development and maintenance, and systematically defining the engineering capabilities these models should acquire.
papers.ja_title: コーディング LLM にソフトウェアエンジニアリングの知識を組み込む訓練手法

papers.title: Self-Evolution Reasoner: Continuous Optimization via Policy-Intrinsic Exploration and Exploitation
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) enables large language models (LLMs) to continuously self-improve their reasoning capabilities. Compared to RLVR's scalar rewards, recent self-supervised on-policy distillation methods leverage denser supervision signals. However, both paradigms suffer from exploration bottlenecks, struggling to escape local optima when the policy fails to sample valid solutions. Relying on external demonstrations can bypass this issue; however, the off-policy nature hinders genuine self-improvement and the mismatched-distribution reasoning can not be fully exploited. In this work, we propose Self-Evolution Policy Optimization (SEPO), a framework that drives continuous reasoning capability evolution via guided exploration and in-distribution exploitation. Specifically, SEPO utilizes labels to elicit correct reasoning from the policy, unlocking the exploration potential. By treating current policy conditioned on this in-distribution reasoning as a self-teacher, SEPO distills the newly discovered solution back into the policy. Through this iterative cycle of policy-intrinsic exploration and exploitation, SEPO achieves robust and continuous capability evolution. Across scientific, tool-use, and complex logical reasoning domains, SEPO consistently achieves the best performance under identical training time or steps, demonstrating superior efficiency and convergence ceilings. Notably, SEPO maintains stable improvements even in scenarios where baselines severely underperform or fail entirely, such as on complex tasks or with small-scale models. Our code is available at https://github.com/Eric8932/SEPO.
papers.ja_title: 方針内の探索と活用で推論能力を継続的に自己進化させる強化学習手法

papers.title: Rethinking Retrieval in the Long-Context Era: Training-Free Semantic Trees for Adaptive Context Construction
papers.abstract: Long-context language models can increasingly process entire documents, making full-context prompting a practical alternative to passage retrieval. However, greater capacity determines how much information a model can receive, but not which information best supports a query. This distinction motivates rethinking retrieval: when the full document already fits, can selecting and organizing its evidence improve answering? The challenge is to retain supporting facts and relations while keeping the context focused on the question. To reconcile these goals, we introduce \ours, a training-free framework that uses semantic abstraction to guide selection while retaining original text for answering. \ours constructs a reusable semantic hierarchy from the full document in a single generation, linking node descriptions to source spans. Given a query, structural--semantic scoring and fine-grained lexical attribution nominate shared source nodes; their union with ancestor context preserves structural relations and complete local text. Across four frontier answer models, \ours improves average QA-F1 by 1.72 points over full-context prompting on three LongBench tasks, surpassing the evaluated baselines on the four-model average while reducing answer-context length by 58.55\%. Our code is available at the $\href{https://anonymous.4open.science/r/treefuse-ECFE}{repository}$.
papers.ja_title: 長文脈時代における学習不要の意味木構築による文脈選択手法

papers.title: Last-Iterate Stationarity of Muon with Finitely Many Newton-Schulz Iterations
papers.abstract: Muon has achieved strong empirical performance in large-scale language-model training, motivating a better theoretical understanding of its practical implementation. Unlike the idealized polar-factor update, practical Muon uses a fixed number of quintic Newton--Schulz iterations. Existing analyses mainly establish average- or best-iterate stationarity guarantees, leaving last-iterate convergence less understood. We study last-iterate gradient convergence of practical finite-step Muon on smooth, lower-bounded nonconvex objectives. For deterministic gradients, we show that without input stabilization, Muon can cycle even on a smooth convex quadratic. With positive stabilization, we establish last-iterate gradient convergence for any fixed momentum coefficient below one and a sufficiently small constant learning rate, together with square-summability of gradients. For stochastic gradients, we first show that persistent bounded, unbiased noise can prevent convergence with fixed learning rates and momentum, even with positive stabilization. We then establish almost-sure and mean-square last-iterate gradient convergence by combining decreasing learning rates with increasing momentum under bounded-variance stochastic gradients. Finally, we construct a smooth counterexample showing that neither convergence theorem guarantees a pointwise polynomial rate. We further establish density-one convergence rates, guaranteeing polynomial gradient decay for all but a vanishing fraction of iterations.

papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 有限回のニュートン・シュルツ反復を使う Muon の最終反復収束理論
papers.summary: 大規模言語モデルの学習で使われる最適化手法 Muon は、理想的な計算の代わりに有限回の近似計算(ニュートン・シュルツ法)を使うが、その収束の仕組みはよく分かっていなかった。この研究は、入力を適切に安定化させ、学習率と慣性項(モメンタム)を適切に設定すれば、最後の更新がきちんと勾配(傾き)ゼロに近づくことを理論的に証明した。安定化がないと滑らかな凸関数でも振動が止まらないことも示した。
papers.why: Muon は実運用で広く使われている最適化手法であり、その収束保証の条件(学習率・モメンタムの設定範囲)を理論的に裏付けたことで、大規模学習のハイパーパラメータ設計に指針を与える。
papers.summary_en: Muon, the optimizer behind strong empirical large-scale LLM training results, uses a fixed number of quintic Newton-Schulz iterations in practice rather than the idealized polar-factor update, and existing analyses mainly give average- or best-iterate stationarity guarantees, leaving last-iterate convergence less understood. For deterministic gradients, the authors show that without input stabilization Muon can cycle even on a smooth convex quadratic, while with positive stabilization they establish last-iterate gradient convergence for any fixed momentum coefficient below one and a sufficiently small constant learning rate, together with square-summability of gradients. For stochastic gradients, persistent bounded unbiased noise can prevent convergence with fixed learning rate and momentum even with stabilization, but combining decreasing learning rates with increasing momentum under bounded-variance noise yields almost-sure and mean-square last-iterate convergence; they also construct a counterexample showing neither theorem guarantees a pointwise polynomial rate, though they establish density-one polynomial gradient decay for all but a vanishing fraction of iterations.
papers.why_en: Provides a theoretical account of exactly which stabilization, learning-rate, and momentum conditions are needed for Muon's practical finite-step implementation to actually converge, grounding hyperparameter choices for an optimizer already used in large-scale training.

papers.title: MultiEvoSkill: Structure-Aware Multi-Agent Skill Evolution for Generalizable Skill Artifacts
papers.abstract: Skill documents are becoming the default adaptation surface for frozen large language model (LLM) agents, but current skill generators face two key limitations. First, humans and different LLMs differ in how they organize procedural knowledge and approach task solving. Skills authored from a human or single-model perspective may therefore fail to align with the reasoning behaviors of other backbones, limiting cross-model generalization. Second, sequential skill descriptions inadequately represent procedures with parallel branches and explicit dependencies, while existing skill optimizers primarily operate on prose and lack explicit support for graph-structured skill evolution. We introduce MultiEvoSkill, a skill-optimization framework comprising three core components: 1) Skill compiler casts the skill as a typed graph with tailored operators, producing a compact, informative representation with explicit procedural topology; 2) Heterogeneous agent system proposes revision advices using collective intelligence, where minimal and informative issues are identified based on multiple sets of experiences. 3) Structure-aware debate and evolution mechanism organizes candidate edits into a heterogeneous graph, resolves them under dependency and importance constraints, and distills the collective proposal into the artifact. Multi-dimensional gating ensures the information gain and topological correctness of each evolution. Optimal skills are then obtained when the system converges at a consistent state. Various experiments and ablations against SOTA methods validate the effectiveness and generalization of MultiEvoSkill.
papers.ja_title: 構造を意識した複数エージェントによるスキル文書の進化手法

papers.title: ScaleRLT: Exact Log-Probabilities and Fast Deferred Rollouts for Reinforcement Learning on Looped Transformers
papers.abstract: Looped language models such as Ouro reuse one block of layers several times per token. A rollout engine can batch the deeper loops of several response positions and run them only when a deep readout is due. This deferred schedule is fast, but the learner of an on-policy RL algorithm recomputes the sampled tokens' log-probabilities with a dense pass, and the two computations differ in floating point: in FP32 at 4096 tokens about 18% of the sampled tokens miss a $10^{-5}$ same-weight gate, and with bf16 weights nearly every token does. We use a hybrid learner log-probability, $\ell=\ell_{\mathrm{dense}}+\mathrm{sg}(\ell_{\mathrm{sched}}-\ell_{\mathrm{dense}})$, where $\mathrm{sg}$ denotes stop-gradient. Its value is a no-grad replay through the rollout's own schedule, and its gradient is the dense learner's. The replay reproduces the rollout bit for bit in all 167 FP32 and 28 bf16 real-weight cells we ran on three platforms, including rollouts whose batch shrinks at stop tokens, and the gradient has the same FP32 error as other dense implementations in all 102 pre-registered comparisons from 96 to 4096 tokens; the full GRPO loss of a training step matches a float64 reference to $3.1\times10^{-4}$. On one GPU, deferral raises rollout throughput by $1.47$ to $1.56\times$, and by $1.18$ to $1.54\times$ once every step runs from CUDA graphs, bit for bit. In a two-node GRPO loop, one-wave KV admission and CUDA graphs shorten an update by $2.71\times$ with the gate bitwise at every update, and four nodes keep the update time within 2% at the same per-GPU load. In 100-update runs held-out GSM8K accuracy rose from 23% to 82% with the mixed-depth readout that deferral relies on and from 34% to 90% with the native readout, which reached a higher accuracy in less time. For looped models beyond one node we analyse a ring mapping of layers to GPUs and measure its communication paths.
papers.ja_title: ループ型 Transformer の強化学習を高速化する ScaleRLT の厳密な対数確率計算
papers.summary: 同じ層のブロックを何度も繰り返し使う「ループ型」言語モデルは、生成を高速化するために深い繰り返しをまとめて遅延実行できるが、その結果を学習側が再計算すると数値がわずかにずれてしまう問題があった。ScaleRLT はこのずれを勾配計算と値計算で分けて扱う手法を提案し、167 回の浮動小数点検証すべてでビット単位の一致を確認した。GPU 1 台で生成速度を 1.47〜1.56 倍に、2 台構成の強化学習更新を 2.71 倍短縮し、4 台に増やしても更新時間の増加は 2% 以内に収まった。
papers.why: ループ型モデルという新しいアーキテクチャに対する強化学習の分散実行基盤を、数値の厳密性を保ったまま高速化する具体的な実装パターンを示している。
papers.summary_en: Looped language models such as Ouro reuse one block of layers several times per token, and a rollout engine can batch deeper loops across response positions and run them only when a deep readout is due -- a deferred schedule that is fast but creates a floating-point mismatch with the learner's dense recomputation of sampled tokens' log-probabilities (in FP32 at 4096 tokens about 18% of sampled tokens miss a 1e-5 same-weight gate, and with bf16 weights nearly every token does). The authors use a hybrid learner log-probability whose value is a no-grad replay through the rollout's own schedule and whose gradient is the dense learner's, reproducing the rollout bit-for-bit across all 167 FP32 and 28 bf16 real-weight cells on three platforms, with the gradient matching other dense implementations' FP32 error in all 102 pre-registered comparisons and the full GRPO loss matching a float64 reference to 3.1e-4. On one GPU, deferral raises rollout throughput by 1.47-1.56x (1.18-1.54x once every step runs from CUDA graphs, bit-for-bit); in a two-node GRPO loop, one-wave KV admission and CUDA graphs shorten an update by 2.71x with the gate bitwise at every update, and four nodes keep update time within 2% at the same per-GPU load; in 100-update runs, held-out GSM8K accuracy rose from 23% to 82% with the mixed-depth readout deferral relies on, and from 34% to 90% with the native readout, which reached higher accuracy in less time.
papers.why_en: Gives a concrete, numerically exact recipe for reconciling a fast deferred rollout schedule with an on-policy RL learner's dense recomputation for a new looped-transformer architecture, with distributed scaling measurements up to four nodes.

papers.title: Prefix Keys and Values Matter Late: RIPE Caching for Self-Speculative Decoding in Looped Language Models
papers.abstract: A looped language model runs one block of layers $R$ times per token, so its key-value (KV) cache holds $R$ planes per recurrent layer, and self-speculative decoding (draft with a few loops, verify with all $R$) reads them all. We find that prefix keys and values matter late: at equal perturbation size, loops 25-32 are $e^{15.0}$ (Huginn-0125) and $e^{12.8}$ (Raven-Llama) times more sensitive than loops 2-9, and the planes approach the last one geometrically, at 0.88 and 0.81 per loop. Whether the deepest plane alone suffices then depends on how ripe the late planes are: on Raven, storing only it is indistinguishable from a bf16-to-fp32 change; on Huginn, 1% of positions carry 74% of its error. We turn this into RIPE, which stores the deepest plane everywhere except a window of recent positions kept at full depth. On Huginn, a 64-position window removes 89% of the tail positions at 11.9% of the full cache's memory (1024-token context), and any window at least as long as the draft block makes batched verification block-independent by construction. Nine pre-registered GPU batches back these results. Simple models of acceptance, decoding cost and memory, two of them checked on held-out measurements, account for the measured self-speculative speed-ups ($2.09\times$ with the full cache, $2.58\times$ with the deepest plane) and decompose the $2.24\times$ fixed-memory throughput gain of one shared plane.
papers.ja_title: ループ型言語モデルの自己投機的デコーディング向け KV キャッシュ圧縮 RIPE
papers.summary: ループ型言語モデルは 1 トークンにつき同じ層を何度も繰り返すため、KV キャッシュ(過去の計算結果を覚えておく領域)が繰り返し回数分だけ膨らんでしまう。この研究は、浅い繰り返し層のキャッシュは古くても影響が小さいが、深い層ほど後になって重要になることを発見し、直近の位置だけ全階層を保持し残りは最後の層だけ保存する RIPE という方式を提案した。64 位置分の窓を使うと、精度劣化の 89% を取り除きながらメモリ使用量をフルキャッシュの 11.9% に抑え、生成速度を最大 2.58 倍に高速化した。
papers.why: ループ型アーキテクチャという新しい構造に対して KV キャッシュの何を削ってよいかを実測で明らかにし、既存の KV キャッシュ圧縮技術をどう適応させるかの指針になる。
papers.summary_en: A looped language model runs one block of layers R times per token, so its KV cache holds R planes per recurrent layer, and self-speculative decoding (draft with a few loops, verify with all R) must read all of them. The authors find prefix keys and values 'matter late': at equal perturbation size, loops 25-32 are e^15.0 (Huginn-0125) and e^12.8 (Raven-Llama) times more sensitive than loops 2-9, with planes approaching the last one geometrically (0.88 and 0.81 per loop); whether storing only the deepest plane suffices then depends on how 'ripe' late planes are -- on Raven it is indistinguishable from a bf16-to-fp32 change, while on Huginn 1% of positions carry 74% of its error. RIPE stores the deepest plane everywhere except a window of recent positions kept at full depth; on Huginn, a 64-position window removes 89% of the tail positions' error at 11.9% of the full cache's memory (1024-token context), and any window at least as long as the draft block makes batched verification block-independent by construction. Across nine pre-registered GPU batches, simple acceptance/cost/memory models (two checked on held-out measurements) account for the measured self-speculative speed-ups (2.09x with the full cache, 2.58x with the deepest plane) and decompose the 2.24x fixed-memory throughput gain of one shared plane.
papers.why_en: Identifies exactly what can be dropped from a looped transformer's multi-plane KV cache without hurting accuracy, directly informing how to adapt existing KV-cache compression ideas to this emerging architecture.

papers.title: Ambiguous Fits: The Rashomon Effect and Challenges in Scaling Law Estimation
papers.abstract: Estimating neural scaling laws involves an end-to-end pipeline: designing a scaling recipe, training models across scales, evaluating models on a target metric, and deploying an algorithm to fit a scaling law to the resulting data. This final fitting stage is often treated as routine: standard procedures minimize a non-convex fitting loss using local optimization from a grid of initializations, and return the best solution found. Yet such heuristic searches can fail in two distinct ways: they offer no guarantee of returning a nearly optimal solution, and they obscure whether fundamentally different parameter choices fit the data nearly as well. Indeed, we show that standard scaling law fitting is subject to a Rashomon effect (Breiman, 2001): the sublevel sets of near-minimizers correspond to broad parameter regions whose extrapolations diverge substantially at scale. We resolve these issues with a deterministic branch-and-bound algorithm that guarantees nearly optimal fitting loss and exhaustively maps the near-minimizers to the implied range of scaling curves.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: スケーリング則のあてはめに潜む「別解が多数ある」問題と解決アルゴリズム
papers.summary: モデルサイズと性能の関係を表すスケーリング則は、通常いくつかの初期値から最適化して一番良い当てはめを選ぶが、この研究はほぼ同じ当てはまりの良さを持つ全く異なるパラメータの組が多数存在し、それぞれ将来予測(大規模にしたときの性能)が大きく食い違うことを示した。これを「羅生門効果」と呼び、確実に最適な当てはめを見つけ、近い当てはめすべてが示す予測の幅を網羅的に求める決定的な分枝限定法を提案した。
papers.why: スケーリング則から将来の性能を予測して投資判断をする際、当てはめ方法そのものが信頼できる予測を返しているかを検証する手段を与える。
papers.summary_en: Estimating neural scaling laws is usually treated as routine at the fitting stage: standard procedures minimize a non-convex fitting loss via local optimization from a grid of initializations and return the best solution found, offering no guarantee of near-optimality and obscuring whether fundamentally different parameter choices fit the data nearly as well. The authors show standard scaling-law fitting is subject to a Rashomon effect: the sublevel sets of near-minimizers correspond to broad parameter regions whose extrapolations diverge substantially at scale. They resolve this with a deterministic branch-and-bound algorithm that guarantees nearly optimal fitting loss and exhaustively maps the near-minimizers to the implied range of scaling curves.
papers.why_en: Warns that a standard scaling-law fit can mask many near-equally-good fits that extrapolate very differently, giving a method to check whether a scaling-law forecast is actually trustworthy.

review.note: スケーリング則の当てはめは、グリッド初期値からの局所最適化で『一番良い解』を返すだけでは不十分で、同程度に当てはまる別パラメータ群が将来予測を大きく違えることがある、という測り方そのものの落とし穴を示す観点。
review.note_en: Shows that standard scaling-law fitting via local optimization from a grid of initializations can hide many near-equally-good fits whose large-scale extrapolations disagree substantially, a pitfall in how the fit itself is validated.

papers.title: TRIAGE: Efficient Vision-Language-Action Inference Needs Both Reuse and Pruning
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are increasingly used for robot manipulation because they map camera images and a language instruction directly to actions. Robots that cannot be tethered to a workstation, such as mobile manipulators and humanoids, must run them on onboard embedded boards, where the prefill latency of the language backbone grows with the hundreds of visual tokens processed at every control step. To meet real-time limits, training-free accelerators recompute only a subset of the visual tokens and skip the rest, either by pruning them or by reusing their cached key-value (KV) states. The two options save nearly the same computation, yet existing methods apply only one of them to every skipped token. Through a token-level diagnostic, we show that which option keeps the action closer to full recomputation depends on the token's drift, the change in its shallow-layer value since its cache was computed. On both backbones tested, reusing tokens below a drift threshold was no worse than pruning them, whereas beyond it, reuse yields up to 4.4x the action error of pruning; the same diagnostic calibrates this threshold per backbone. Building on this finding, we propose TRIAGE, which deems a cache valid when its drift is below this threshold and it is not too old. TRIAGE recomputes a fixed budget of tokens, prioritizing important tokens with invalid caches, reuses every other token with a valid cache, and prunes the rest; prune-only and reuse-only methods are the two extremes of this partition. Because the budget fixes the number of recomputed tokens, it directly sets the prefill latency. On LIBERO and SimplerEnv, TRIAGE stays within 3 pp of full recomputation in average success rate while cutting prefill latency on a Jetson AGX Orin by up to 48%, and with only 7% of visual tokens recomputed, it beats the strongest baseline by 24.4 pp on LIBERO-Object.
papers.ja_title: 視覚言語行動モデルの推論を再利用と刈り込みの両方で最適化する TRIAGE
papers.summary: ロボットを動かす視覚言語行動モデル(カメラ画像と指示から行動を直接出すモデル)は搭載基板上で動くことが多く、画像トークンの量に比例して計算が重くなる。この研究は、各トークンのキャッシュ(計算結果の保存)をそのまま使い回すか、捨てて計算し直すかを、浅い層での値の変化量(ドリフト)で判断する基準を見つけ、その基準に基づいて予算を固定して割り振る TRIAGE 手法を提案した。LIBERO と SimplerEnv の実験で、成功率を全計算時の 3 ポイント差以内に保ちながら Jetson AGX Orin 上の計算時間を最大 48% 削減し、画像トークンの 7% だけ計算し直す設定では最も強い既存手法を 24.4 ポイント上回った。
papers.why: KV キャッシュの再利用と刈り込みをどちらか一方でなく動的に選択する発想は、LLM サービングのキャッシュ管理にも転用できる考え方である。
papers.summary_en: Vision-language-action (VLA) models for robot manipulation must often run on embedded boards, where the language backbone's prefill latency grows with the hundreds of visual tokens processed at every control step, and training-free accelerators save computation by either pruning skipped visual tokens or reusing their cached KV states, applying only one option to every skipped token even though the two save nearly the same computation. Through a token-level diagnostic, the authors show which option keeps the action closer to full recomputation depends on the token's drift (the change in its shallow-layer value since caching): on both tested backbones, reusing tokens below a drift threshold was no worse than pruning them, but beyond it reuse yields up to 4.4x the action error of pruning, with the same diagnostic calibrating the threshold per backbone. TRIAGE recomputes a fixed token budget -- prioritizing important tokens with invalid caches, reusing every valid-cache token below the drift/age threshold, and pruning the rest -- and on LIBERO and SimplerEnv stays within 3 pp of full recomputation in average success rate while cutting prefill latency on a Jetson AGX Orin by up to 48%, beating the strongest baseline by 24.4 pp on LIBERO-Object when recomputing only 7% of visual tokens.
papers.why_en: Shows cache reuse and pruning are not interchangeable but should be chosen per-token by a measured drift signal, an idea directly transferable to KV-cache management in general LLM serving.

papers.title: MOFjson: An Explicit Topological Representation of Metal-Organic Frameworks for Language Models
papers.abstract: Language models for metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) rely on formats that separate atomic geometry from structural topology, forcing models to choose between unstructured coordinate lists and non-spatial string identifiers[1]. We present MOFjson, the first representation separating structural data into a raw atomic layer with explicit bond shift vectors and a derived layer exposing secondary building units (metal nodes and organic linkers) and network topology. Additionally, we introduce a benchmark with crystal-derived ground truth across four question categories. Across four models, MOFjson beats all three baselines in every category: 100% vs. 18-47% on reaching a block's nearest periodic copy, 96% vs. 71% on crystal system characterisation, and 60% vs. 48% on metal node and organic linker coordination. Ablating shift labels drops accuracy to 12.7%, proving models read the periodic graph rather than the surface format. MOFjson gives language models structure to read rather than reconstruct, establishing a foundation for agentic tool workflows and constrained MOF generation.

papers.title: Rethinking Verification in Agent Harnesses
papers.abstract: Agent harnesses enable large language models to act through tools, observe the results, and iteratively work toward a task goal. Verification checks and revises agents' work to improve output quality. Yet there is limited guidance on how harnesses should organize this effort. We study verification as an axis of test-time scaling by examining when to intervene, who checks the work, and how checking leads to revision. Our framework spans four layers of the agent lifecycle: initial instructions, mid-turn reminders, completion gates, and independent review. We compare 17 designs across seven frontier coding models on Terminal-Bench (TB) and SWE-bench Verified (SWE), and introduce VisualBench for expert evaluation of visual and interactive artifacts. Initial instructions and execution-time reminders yield modest, model-dependent average gains on the coding benchmarks, without substantially increasing average output token use. Completion gates can yield larger gains but may substantially increase cost. Independent review by a critic offers a more favorable accuracy-cost tradeoff, improving average accuracy by 5.9-9.5 percentage points on TB and 3.9-6.6 on SWE at 1.13-1.25 and 1.00-1.04 times baseline cost, respectively. On VisualBench, independent review achieves net preferences of 13.2-23.8 points over the baseline across its four designs, exceeding the evaluated L0-L2 designs. Additional review rounds or independent critics further improve average TB accuracy by up to 3.5 percentage points. Together, these results provide empirical guidance for verification design in agent harnesses and support independent review as a practical axis of test-time scaling.

papers.title: Dream to Assist: Intent-Conditioned World Models for Shared Vehicle Control
papers.abstract: Assistive agents in shared-control settings face a dual challenge: acting proactively to align with the human's intentions while remaining legible enough for the human to comprehend and fluently respond in real time. We present Dream2Assist, a model-based reinforcement learning framework for tightly-coupled shared decision making that addresses both sides of this challenge. Our approach extends a recurrent state-space world model with intent inference, enabling an assistive policy trained via fictitious co-play to anticipate and support discrete human objectives without overriding human agency. Beyond the computational framework, we describe the full deployment pipeline needed to translate a world-model-based policy into a safe, human-centered system in a resource-efficient way. Crucially, we address the sim-to-real-human gap via policy down-selection and reward restructuring within an iterative human-machine interface design. We validate the framework through three human-subjects studies and a preliminary on-vehicle deployment spanning two qualitatively distinct domains: high-speed racing (N=30) and urban driving with richer intent structure (N=10). Our results demonstrate that intent conditioning yields measurable improvements in torque alignment and collision rate. We surface key design insights and practices for deploying learning-based assistive agents in safety-critical, real-time human-robot teaming.
