papers.title: VLA-HWBench: Where the Time Goes When VLA Models Run on Edge Hardware
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models increasingly run on edge devices aboard robots, where inference latency constrains closed-loop robot control. However, it remains unclear how to design VLA models, their inference software and edge hardware so that robots can run VLA inference in real time. Most VLA models report only task success, while prior studies cover limited action-generation strategies, divide inference into at most three stages, and lack comparisons of inference optimizations on the same models. Therefore, we introduce VLA-HWBench, a benchmark that measures 18 open VLA models on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor and AMD Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 395, with a seven-stage inference breakdown. Our study reveals three insights. First, action-generation strategy matters more than model size. It dominates 14 of 19 Jetson configurations, latency varies by $82\times$ on Jetson and $157\times$ on AMD, and parameter count explains at most 15% of latency variance. Models that generate long action chunks in a few flow-matching steps keep up with control, whereas token-by-token decoding does not. Second, kernel fusion with 4-bit weights helps most, running $π_{0.5}$ and GR00T N1.7 2.6-2.9$\times$ faster than PyTorch with torch.compile, but it exists for only these two models and only on the Jetson. Optimization also moves the time to the stages it shortens least, as CPU preprocessing grows from 12% to 39% of the GR00T N1.7 call. Third, after optimization, memory bandwidth limits only the stages that process few tokens on the Jetson, such as the denoising steps, whereas software limits all other stages, from unfused kernels to serial preprocessing on the host CPU. Overall, low-latency edge VLAs should use few action-generation iterations, inference software should extend kernel fusion and low-bit weights to more models and platforms, and edge hardware needs high memory bandwidth and a fast host CPU.
papers.ja_title: エッジ機器上で動く視覚言語行動モデルの推論時間がどこで消えるかを計測する VLA-HWBench
papers.summary: ロボットに搭載する視覚言語行動モデルは、応答の速さがロボットの制御周期を左右するが、どこで時間がかかっているかを詳しく調べた研究は少なかった。VLA-HWBench は 18 個の公開モデルを Jetson AGX Thor と AMD Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 395 上で測定し、推論を 7 段階に分解した。モデルの大きさよりも行動を生成する方式の違いの方が遅さを左右し(最大 157 倍の差)、カーネル融合と 4 ビット量子化を組み合わせると PyTorch の通常実行より 2.6〜2.9 倍速くなるが、この最適化が使えるのは測定した 18 モデルのうち 2 モデルだけだった。
papers.why: カーネル融合や低ビット量子化が実際にどのモデル・どの段階に効くかを、メモリ帯域とソフトウェアのどちらが制約になっているかまで分解して示しており、エッジ推論の最適化箇所を見極める材料になる。
papers.summary_en: VLA models increasingly run on edge devices where inference latency constrains closed-loop robot control, yet it remains unclear how to design the models, inference software, and edge hardware for real-time operation, and prior studies cover limited action-generation strategies, divide inference into at most three stages, and lack cross-optimization comparisons on the same models. VLA-HWBench measures 18 open VLA models on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor and AMD Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 395 with a seven-stage inference breakdown, finding: (1) action-generation strategy matters more than model size, dominating 14 of 19 Jetson configurations, with latency varying 82x on Jetson and 157x on AMD while parameter count explains at most 15% of latency variance, and models generating long action chunks in few flow-matching steps keeping pace with control while token-by-token decoding does not; (2) kernel fusion with 4-bit weights helps most, running pi_0.5 and GR00T N1.7 2.6-2.9x faster than PyTorch with torch.compile, but exists for only these two models and only on Jetson, and shifts bottleneck time -- CPU preprocessing grows from 12% to 39% of the GR00T N1.7 call; (3) after optimization, memory bandwidth limits only token-sparse stages like denoising on Jetson, while software limits everything else, from unfused kernels to serial host-CPU preprocessing.
papers.why_en: Decomposes exactly where edge VLA inference time goes across 18 models and two hardware platforms, pinpointing which bottlenecks are memory-bandwidth-bound versus software-bound and thus actionable through different fixes.

papers.title: The Physical Cost of Context: Quality-Constrained Resource Accounting for Coding Agents
papers.abstract: Coding agents resend a growing context on every model call, and context policies are usually judged by the prompt tokens they save. Executed work also depends on call count and prefix reuse: a caching runtime prefills only the tokens after the longest cached prefix. A shorter prompt can therefore cost more if it rewrites cached history. Our quality-gated protocol splits executed prefill into logical prompt minus reused prefix and measures KV residency, time, and energy. On 450 localization cases derived from SWE-rebench V2, preloading ten retrieved blocks (Eager) and adding anchored history compaction (Compact) both pass a five-point non-inferiority gate. In a separate 900-cell study, Eager cuts model calls by 35.7% and the GPU-energy proxy by 33.2% against on-demand search (Grep); Compact saves nothing further. Enabling prefix caching leaves Eager's prompt volume similar (+8.3%; its 95% CI spans zero) but cuts its uncached prefill by 67.7%. Deleting history can turn a token saving into extra work. With mini-SWE-agent on 100 SWE-bench Verified instances, keeping only the last five observations (Mask-5) cuts Eager's prompt volume by 33.3% but loses 135.9k reusable tokens per task. Uncached prefill rises by 608.5%, the energy proxy by 125.6%, and the policy misses the quality gate. Policies thus save physical work by shortening the trajectory and can multiply it by editing reusable history.
papers.ja_title: コーディングエージェントの文脈管理をキャッシュ再利用まで含めて評価する手法
papers.summary: コーディングを行う AI エージェントは呼び出しごとに文脈(プロンプト)を送り直すが、文脈を短くする工夫は「送るトークン数」だけで評価されがちで、実際に GPU が計算し直す量(キャッシュが効かない部分)は見落とされていた。この研究は、過去の履歴をあらかじめ読み込む方式(Eager)がオンデマンド検索に比べモデル呼び出し回数を 35.7%、GPU 消費電力の目安を 33.2% 削減する一方、履歴を一部消す方式(Mask-5)はプロンプトを 33.3% 短くしても再利用できるトークンを失い、計算し直す量が 608.5% 増えて消費電力の目安も 125.6% 増えることを示した。
papers.why: プロンプト長の削減が必ずしも実際の計算量削減にならないことを定量的に示し、プレフィックスキャッシュ(共通する先頭部分の再利用)を前提にした文脈管理の設計指針を与える。
papers.summary_en: Coding agents resend a growing context on every model call, and context policies are usually judged only by the prompt tokens they save, even though executed work also depends on call count and prefix reuse -- a caching runtime prefills only the tokens after the longest cached prefix, so a shorter prompt can cost more if it rewrites cached history. The authors' quality-gated protocol splits executed prefill into logical prompt minus reused prefix and measures KV residency, time, and energy; on 450 localization cases from SWE-rebench V2, preloading ten retrieved blocks (Eager) and anchored history compaction (Compact) both pass a five-point non-inferiority gate, and in a separate 900-cell study Eager cuts model calls by 35.7% and the GPU-energy proxy by 33.2% against on-demand search (Grep), with Compact saving nothing further; enabling prefix caching leaves Eager's prompt volume similar (+8.3%, 95% CI spans zero) but cuts its uncached prefill by 67.7%. With mini-SWE-agent on 100 SWE-bench Verified instances, keeping only the last five observations (Mask-5) cuts Eager's prompt volume by 33.3% but loses 135.9k reusable tokens per task, raising uncached prefill by 608.5% and the energy proxy by 125.6%, missing the quality gate.
papers.why_en: Demonstrates quantitatively that shortening a prompt does not necessarily reduce the physical compute actually executed once prefix caching is accounted for, and can even multiply it, a measurement framework directly applicable to agent context-management design.

review.note: プロンプトのトークン数だけで文脈管理策を評価すると見誤る。プレフィックスキャッシュの再利用まで含めた実行時間・エネルギーで測り直すと、トークン削減策が逆に計算量を増やす例がある、という評価指標の選び方の観点。
review.note_en: Shows that judging context-management policies by prompt token count alone can mislead; measuring actual executed prefill, time, and energy under prefix caching reveals that a token-shortening policy can increase real compute, a metric-selection pitfall for agent benchmarking.

papers.title: The Right Fact, the Wrong Decision: SciValidityBench for Scientific Agent Memory
papers.abstract: Most agent-memory benchmarks frame long-term memory as retrieval: can an agent recover the relevant record from a long and evolving history? Scientific agents face a stricter problem: a correctly remembered fact may still be invalid to use. The same reported test result can support confirmation when the outcome and stopping rule were fixed in advance, yet only exploration when the outcome was selected from twenty inspected results. We call this scientific use validity: whether remembered evidence is eligible to influence a decision under the state governing its interpretation. We introduce SciValidityBench, an executable benchmark factory with 64 TaskSpecs spanning five validity modules and six scientific domains. TaskSpecs couple generated experimental histories with scientific-state definitions, programmatic decision oracles, controlled interventions, and automatic scoring. The SciStateForge compiler-reader framework turns distributed histories into explicit decision-governing state. Counterfactual pairs and targeted corruption-repair controls then test whether models use those dependencies and localize failures. Across four model families, compiled scientific state improves valid decision-making by 9.2-18.8 percentage points over a generic Event Graph. Retrieval alone does not reproduce this cross-family gain, while content-identical flat and typed views show that the improvement comes from exposing governing state rather than a particular graph serialization. SciValidityBench thus shifts memory evaluation from finding the right fact to deciding whether that fact should control the decision.
papers.ja_title: 科学エージェントの記憶が事実の正しさだけでなく使用の妥当性も問う SciValidityBench

papers.title: Transporting Quantiles to Codebook: Scalable Vector Quantization without Codebook Collapse
papers.abstract: Effective discrete representation learning with VQ-VAE serves as a fundamental component of modern autoregressive generative models. However, it is widely known to suffer from codebook collapse and inefficient code utilization. To address this issue, we propose FlowVQ, a simple yet effective alternative to standard vector quantization by formulating neural quantization as a joint modeling and clustering process. Specifically, we learn the latent space using a lightweight flow matching model alongside training, corresponding to a probability flow ODE that transports an often fixed well-behaved source distribution while preserving probability mass. Based on this, we define the codebook C_1 by transporting even-quantile partitioned prior codes C_0 from the source space through the learned flow, and obtaining the Voronoi centroids under the induced distribution, leading to a structured discretization. We evaluated on image tokenization and generation, as well as on two tasks requiring high-precision tokenization, demonstrating scalability and improved expressivity of the codebook with full utilization.
papers.ja_title: 分位点をコードブックへ輸送しコードブック崩壊を防ぐベクトル量子化 FlowVQ

papers.title: HiLO: Towards Product-Level Graceful Degradation with a Quality-Aware, Load-Aware Control Framework
papers.abstract: Graceful degradation is a key mechanism employed by large-scale systems to handle overload conditions. Its importance has grown further as GPU-intensive LLM inference introduces persistent capacity constraints that cannot be addressed through provisioning alone. Common degradation approaches rely on service-level mechanisms such as load shedding and circuit breakers, or on feature-level switches (some manually controlled) to preserve availability and quality. While effective at protecting services, such approaches lead to untestable product states and thereby unpredictable product quality. We present HiLO (High Load Optimizer), an automated product-level degradation system designed to handle graceful degradation at scale. HiLO maps observed load to a product state lattice: a small set of pre-validated product states, partially ordered by degradation severity. Dependencies are resolved at design time enabling deterministic and continuous control without requiring runtime dependency discovery. The same abstraction applies unchanged across heterogeneous services, including GPU-intensive deep models, LLMs and their serving layers. At Microsoft, HiLO is deployed in Bing (serving over a billion monthly active users), where it manages on average two traffic surges per week across all datacenters, bounding OneDCG (relevance) drop to under 0.5 points (the operational target) even under sustained load exceeding 2$\times$ baseline peak. HiLO complements existing service-level protections with product-level coordination and makes product quality measurable, testable and predictable.
papers.ja_title: Bing で稼働する LLM サービス過負荷時の製品レベル段階的縮退システム HiLO
papers.summary: GPU を大量に使う LLM 推論は、サーバーを増やすだけでは需要の急増に対応しきれず、過負荷になると品質やサービスを落として維持する「段階的縮退」が必要になる。Microsoft が Bing(月間利用者 10 億人超)で運用する HiLO は、負荷の大きさを事前に検証済みの少数の「製品状態」の並びに対応づけ、依存関係を設計時に解決しておくことで実行時に試行錯誤せず済む仕組みを作った。平常時のピークの 2 倍を超える負荷が続いても、検索結果の関連度の低下を目標値である 0.5 ポイント未満に抑えながら、週に平均 2 回の急増を全データセンターで処理している。
papers.why: 大規模 LLM サービングにおける過負荷対策を、個別のサービス遮断器ではなく製品全体で一貫した段階的縮退として設計する実運用例であり、サービング基盤のキャパシティ管理に直接役立つ。
papers.summary_en: Graceful degradation is a key mechanism for handling overload, and its importance has grown as GPU-intensive LLM inference introduces persistent capacity constraints that provisioning alone cannot fix; common approaches rely on service-level load shedding/circuit breakers or feature-level (sometimes manual) switches that protect availability but leave product quality untestable and unpredictable. HiLO (High Load Optimizer) is an automated product-level degradation system that maps observed load to a product state lattice -- a small set of pre-validated product states partially ordered by degradation severity -- resolving dependencies at design time for deterministic, continuous control without runtime dependency discovery, applying unchanged across heterogeneous services including GPU-intensive deep models, LLMs, and their serving layers. At Microsoft, HiLO is deployed in Bing (over a billion monthly active users), managing on average two traffic surges per week across all datacenters and bounding the OneDCG (relevance) drop to under 0.5 points -- the operational target -- even under sustained load exceeding 2x baseline peak.
papers.why_en: A production system for coordinating overload degradation at the whole-product level rather than per-service, making LLM-serving capacity management testable and predictable at hyperscale.

papers.title: ThinkBit: Search Codewords, Recalibrate Scales, Select by Reasoning
papers.abstract: Reasoning language models generate thousands of tokens per answer, and generation speed is limited by memory bandwidth, so storing weights in two bits instead of bfloat16 can potentially make inference 8$\times$ cheaper. Two-bit methods are usually judged by perplexity and multiple-choice question-answering accuracy, both of which say little about whether a model can still reason through more difficult problems. We present ThinkBit, a strictly scalar two-bit framework built to preserve reasoning, in which every weight is an integer codeword times a bfloat16 scale shared by a group of weights. We first use a sensitivity metric to assign each layer a ternary, 2-bit, or 3-bit tier to allocate bitwidths optimally among layers. This is followed by a layerwise Gumbel-softmax-based scalar quantization algorithm that searches for optimal codewords block by block. Since a layerwise scheme does not capture how quantized layers interact with each other, we recalibrate scales, with the codewords frozen, using a knowledge-distillation-based loss against the teacher model. We then perform a short quantization-aware training (QAT) stage that lets the model mimic the base model's distribution by reassigning codewords. Finally, a paired reasoning test on training problems selects the final checkpoint between the recalibration stage and the QAT stage. On Qwen3-1.7B at matched size, our recalibrated checkpoint scores 46.7 on MATH-500 against 30.0 for EfficientQAT trained on the same data, and 73.0 after QAT on reasoning traces; at 0.52 GB it is smaller than every published 2-bit GGUF of the model yet more accurate on MATH-500. We show that this framework scales and up to 14B, a 3.74 GB model scores 94.8 on MATH-500, against 97.5 for the 29.5 GB bfloat16 model.
papers.ja_title: 推論能力を保ったまま重みを 2 ビットに圧縮する ThinkBit
papers.summary: 長い思考過程を生成する推論向け言語モデルは生成速度がメモリ帯域で決まるため、重みを 16 ビットから 2 ビットに落とせれば理論上 8 倍安く推論できるが、従来の 2 ビット量子化の評価は難しい推論問題への強さを測れていなかった。ThinkBit は層ごとに最適なビット数を割り当て、符号語を層単位で探索したあとに教師モデルとの比較で再調整し、最後に短い量子化考慮学習を行う。Qwen3-1.7B で同じサイズの既存手法(EfficientQAT)の MATH-500 スコア 30.0 に対し 46.7、追加学習後は 73.0 まで達し、14B モデルでは 3.74GB の量子化モデルが 29.5GB の元モデルの 97.5 点に対して 94.8 点を記録した。
papers.why: 低ビット量子化が単純な正解率だけでなく難しい推論能力をどこまで保てるかを具体的な数値で示し、推論コストを 8 倍近く下げる量子化手法の実装レシピを提供する。
papers.summary_en: Reasoning language models generate thousands of tokens per answer with generation speed limited by memory bandwidth, so storing weights in two bits instead of bfloat16 could make inference up to 8x cheaper, but two-bit methods are usually judged by perplexity and multiple-choice accuracy, which say little about whether a model can still reason through harder problems. ThinkBit is a strictly scalar two-bit framework in which every weight is an integer codeword times a shared bfloat16 scale: a sensitivity metric first assigns each layer a ternary/2-bit/3-bit tier, then a layerwise Gumbel-softmax scalar quantization searches for optimal codewords block by block, then scales are recalibrated (codewords frozen) against a knowledge-distillation loss from the teacher, then a short quantization-aware training stage lets the model mimic the base model's distribution, and finally a paired reasoning test on training problems selects the checkpoint between recalibration and QAT. On Qwen3-1.7B at matched size, the recalibrated checkpoint scores 46.7 on MATH-500 against 30.0 for EfficientQAT on the same data, and 73.0 after QAT, at 0.52 GB smaller than every published 2-bit GGUF of the model yet more accurate on MATH-500; scaling to 14B, a 3.74 GB model scores 94.8 on MATH-500 against 97.5 for the 29.5 GB bfloat16 model.
papers.why_en: Shows that two-bit quantization's reasoning-preservation quality depends heavily on recipe choices beyond perplexity/accuracy proxies, and provides an implementation recipe that keeps most reasoning ability while approaching an 8x inference cost reduction.

papers.title: GUIFlow: Temporal Redundancy-Aware Incremental Inference for GUI Agents
papers.abstract: GUI agents built on vision-language models interact with continuously evolving interfaces, yet conventional inference repeatedly recomputes representations of largely overlapping observations and histories. This mismatch makes multi-step interaction costly, while changes in context, interface content, and action arguments prevent straightforward cache reuse. We introduce GUIFlow, a framework for full-pipeline incremental inference in multi-image GUI interaction. Our central insight is that advancing a decision need not require rebuilding all supporting representations: each interaction step can instead selectively update computational states maintained across the trajectory. To support new decisions as the context evolves, GUIFlow adapts how past computation is reused: historical KV states are position-aligned and injected into the current context; change signals guide selective updates of current-observation states in the vision encoder and language model; and earlier action responses serve as speculative drafts verified by the target model. Together, these mechanisms enable cross-step reuse throughout visual encoding, prefill, and decoding without additional training, a separate draft model, or changes to the model-visible inputs and action interface. Experiments demonstrate up to 3.39x geometric-mean speedup across offline multi-image benchmarks and up to 3.49x in online, closed-loop interaction on OSWorld, while maintaining task performance broadly comparable to the dense baseline.
papers.ja_title: GUI エージェントの時間方向の重複を利用した段階的推論 GUIFlow
papers.summary: 画面を操作する GUI エージェントは、ほとんど変化のない画面と履歴を毎回全部計算し直しており無駄が多い。GUIFlow は過去の KV キャッシュ(計算結果の保存)を位置をそろえて再利用し、画面の変化した部分だけ選んで更新し、過去の行動を投機的な下書きとして検証に使うことで、学習や別モデルの追加なしに計算を再利用する。複数画像を使うオフラインの評価で最大 3.39 倍、OSWorld でのオンライン操作で最大 3.49 倍の速度向上を、タスクの成功率をほぼ落とさずに達成した。
papers.why: KV キャッシュの再利用と投機的デコーディングをマルチステップの視覚言語エージェントに拡張する実装で、同種の技術を LLM サービング以外の繰り返し呼び出しにも適用できることを示す。
papers.summary_en: GUI agents built on vision-language models interact with continuously evolving interfaces, yet conventional inference repeatedly recomputes representations of largely overlapping observations and histories, making multi-step interaction costly while changes in context, interface content, and action arguments prevent straightforward cache reuse. GUIFlow's central insight is that advancing a decision need not require rebuilding all supporting representations: historical KV states are position-aligned and injected into the current context, change signals guide selective updates of current-observation states in the vision encoder and language model, and earlier action responses serve as speculative drafts verified by the target model, together enabling cross-step reuse throughout visual encoding, prefill, and decoding without additional training, a separate draft model, or changes to model-visible inputs or the action interface. Experiments show up to 3.39x geometric-mean speedup across offline multi-image benchmarks and up to 3.49x in online closed-loop interaction on OSWorld, while maintaining task performance broadly comparable to the dense baseline.
papers.why_en: Extends KV-cache reuse and speculative decoding to multi-step, multi-image vision-language agent interaction, showing these LLM-serving techniques generalize beyond single-turn text generation to repeated agentic calls.

papers.title: Attention under Bounded Key-Query Similarity: Space Complexity and Transformer Anisotropy
papers.abstract: A growing body of work on KV-cache compression aims to reduce the memory requirements of autoregressive generation. These methods compress the stored context while approximately preserving attention computation, enabling generation with reduced memory consumption. Almost tight theoretical results on the worst case space complexity of attention have recently been obtained, but they are achieved by instances where queries can be perfectly aligned with keys. This directly contradicts the observed anisotropy of the key/query geometry in real transformers. In particular, it has been shown empirically that key/query cosine similarities are small even for most correlated pairs, i.e., near-perfect alignment of queries with keys does not happen in practice. In this paper, we study the space complexity of attention approximation under the assumption that key/query cosine similarities belong to a small interval around zero, i.e., a query cannot align too much with any key. We give a nearly space optimal algorithm and a corresponding space lower bound. Surprisingly, the distribution of key/query cosine similarities in our lower bound exhibits the anisotropy property empirically established and studied in the literature. Additionally, we show that the simple uniform sampling algorithm is nearly optimal for a typical range of parameters, supporting its surprising effectiveness on real datasets.
papers.ja_title: キーとクエリの類似度が小さい現実の Transformer における注意機構の空間計算量理論
papers.summary: KV キャッシュ圧縮(過去の計算結果の保存領域を削る技術)の理論限界はこれまで、クエリとキーが完全に一致できる極端な場合で示されてきたが、実際の Transformer ではキーとクエリの類似度(コサイン類似度)は小さいことが知られている。この研究は、類似度がゼロ付近の小さな範囲に収まるという現実的な仮定のもとで、ほぼ最適な注意機構の近似アルゴリズムと、それに対応する空間計算量の下限を示した。さらに、単純な一様サンプリング法が典型的なパラメータ範囲でほぼ最適であることも示し、実データで一様サンプリングがうまく働く理由を理論的に説明した。
papers.why: KV キャッシュ圧縮で使われる単純なサンプリング手法がなぜ実際にうまく機能するのかを理論的に裏付け、圧縮アルゴリズムの設計に根拠を与える。
papers.summary_en: Recent near-tight theoretical results on the worst-case space complexity of KV-cache compression are achieved by instances where queries can be perfectly aligned with keys, directly contradicting the empirically observed anisotropy of key/query geometry in real transformers, where key/query cosine similarities are small even for the most correlated pairs. The authors instead study the space complexity of attention approximation under the assumption that key/query cosine similarities lie in a small interval around zero, giving a nearly space-optimal algorithm and a corresponding lower bound; surprisingly, the lower bound's key/query cosine-similarity distribution exhibits the anisotropy property established empirically in the literature. They also show that simple uniform sampling is nearly optimal for a typical range of parameters, supporting its surprisingly strong effectiveness observed on real datasets.
papers.why_en: Provides a theoretical justification, under a realistic anisotropy assumption rather than a worst-case alignment assumption, for why simple uniform sampling works surprisingly well for KV-cache compression in practice.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning Done Right for Explicit Confidence Targets
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can produce plausible but incorrect answers when they are uncertain, which can mislead users and undermine model reliability. Training models to abstain with reinforcement learning is a natural approach, but most existing methods use a fixed error penalty and therefore cannot adapt their behavior to different confidence requirements at inference time. We study \emph{explicit confidence targets}, where a user specifies a target \(p\) in the prompt and the model directly chooses whether to answer or abstain, with the goal of achieving an accuracy of at least \(p\) among answered questions. However, learning to respond to different confidence targets with a single model has proven difficult, and prior attempts have failed to distinguish different targets. We show that this failure comes from two problems: the reward signal that distinguishes different values of $p$ is often lost during optimization, while the original error penalty grows without bound as $p$ approaches one. We propose RLEC (\textbf{R}einforcement \textbf{L}earning with \textbf{E}xplicit \textbf{C}onfidence Targets), which preserves the learning signal needed to distinguish confidence targets, introduces a stable reward family that keeps the desired answer condition unchanged, and uses reward scheduling to balance effective learning and training stability. Together, these designs enable the first successful training of a single LLM for explicit confidence target control. Extensive experiments across diverse benchmarks and model scales show that RLEC largely preserves general capabilities and achieves competitive calibration performance. RLEC also supports fine-grained target control without an external decision system or threshold calibration after training. By making explicit confidence targets part of the trained policy, RLEC opens a new and more direct path toward behavioral calibration.

papers.title: UTA: Universal Training Adaptive Learning Rate Decay
papers.abstract: Learning rate decay (LRD) is critical for training high-performance models, yet most designs remain empirically driven. Although the Universal Budget Aware (UBA) LRD offers a theoretical framework, its reliance on SGD dynamics limits its applicability to modern Adam-type optimizers and leaves its key `optimization difficulty parameter' opaque. To bridge this gap, we propose the Universal Training Adaptive (UTA) LRD. Unlike UBA's fixed offline trajectory anchored solely to iterations, UTA treats LRD as a closed-loop shape-and-scale problem. By continuous-time formulation, UTA is training-state adaptive with segment-wise optimal shape. This adaptivity links external iterations with internal training states, enabling a near-optimal path in both progression shape and learning rate (LR) scale, a property unattainable by other LRDs, including UBA. Empirically, we demonstrate consistent improvements across language models (LLaMA 60M to 1B) and vision models (ResNet50, ViT-B) on ImageNet with plug-and-play ease and negligible overhead. Extensive ablation studies further confirm UTA's robustness across dimensions, including peak LR, final decay ratio, its parameter $\varphi_0$, component efficacy and generalization to fine-tuning scenarios, underscoring its practical implementability.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 学習状態に適応する学習率減衰スケジュール UTA
papers.summary: 学習率をどう下げていくか(学習率減衰)は、これまで経験則に頼ることが多く、理論に基づく既存手法(UBA)も確率的勾配降下法(SGD)向けに作られていて Adam 系の最適化手法には使いにくかった。UTA は学習の進み具合そのものに応じて区間ごとに最適な減衰の形と大きさを決める閉ループの方式を提案した。LLaMA(60M〜1B)や ResNet50、ViT-B などの言語・画像モデルで、追加の計算負荷をほとんど増やさずに一貫した性能改善を確認した。
papers.why: 学習率スケジュールは大規模事前学習の計算コストに直結する設定であり、Adam 系最適化手法でも使える適応的な減衰則は実運用の学習レシピに直接取り込める。
papers.summary_en: Learning rate decay (LRD) design has mostly been empirical, and the existing theoretical framework UBA is tied to SGD dynamics and leaves its core 'optimization difficulty parameter' opaque. The authors propose UTA, which treats LRD as a closed-loop, continuous-time shape-and-scale problem that adapts to the training state rather than following a fixed offline trajectory anchored to iterations alone. They report consistent improvements on language models (LLaMA 60M-1B) and vision models (ResNet50, ViT-B on ImageNet) with plug-and-play ease and negligible overhead, and ablations confirming robustness across peak LR, decay ratio, the parameter phi_0, and fine-tuning scenarios.
papers.why_en: Learning rate schedules directly affect the compute cost of large-scale pretraining, and an adaptive decay rule that also works with Adam-type optimizers (not just SGD) can be dropped into existing training recipes with practical implementability.

papers.title: TUON: A Tensor-Aware Optimizer Utilizing Tensor-SVD and Polarization for Large Language Model Pretraining
papers.abstract: Large scale language model~(LLM) pretraining is increasingly bottlenecked by optimizer efficiency, driving optimizer design from vector-aware methods such as AdamW to matrix-aware methods. Matrix-aware optimizers such as Muon exploit matrix structure but treat layers independently, neglecting cross-layer correlations. Tensor-aware optimizers are therefore needed, yet existing ones rely on a matricization-based tensor algebra and remain restricted to shallow stacking and specific modules. In this paper, we propose \textbf{TUON}, a novel optimizer built on a transform-based tensor algebra derived from the Tensor-SVD (T-SVD). Unlike methods that polarize a globally unfolded matrix, TUON mixes layers via a unitary transform $\boldsymbol{Q}$ and then polarizes each transformed slice, and inverts the transform to recover the update. This mix-then-separate strategy captures cross-layer correlations while preserving per-layer diversity, avoiding the structural dimension imbalance and cross-layer misalignment of unfolding. Thus it successfully scales to more layers and diverse modules beyond QKV. Theoretically, we prove that TUON performs steepest descent under a $\boldsymbol{Q}$-transformed tensor spectral norm, and identify its update as the tensor polar factor of the T-SVD. We further establish transform non-redundancy, norm and smoothness comparisons with Muon and TEON, and a convergence guarantee. Empirically, TUON improves consistently over Muon and TEON on GPT-124M/350M and Qwen-0.6B/4B, with ablations confirming the transformation mechanism, cross-layer structure beyond two-layer stacking, adaptability beyond QKV, and robustness to the polarization method.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: テンソル特異値分解を使う大規模言語モデル事前学習向け最適化手法 TUON
papers.summary: 大規模言語モデルの事前学習は最適化手法(オプティマイザ)の効率が性能を左右するようになっており、AdamW から行列構造を利用する Muon のような手法へと進化してきたが、Muon は層ごとに独立して扱うため層をまたいだ相関を見ていなかった。TUON はテンソル特異値分解(T-SVD)に基づき、層をまとめて変換してから各層ごとに調整し元に戻すという手順で層間の相関を捉えつつ層ごとの個性も保つ。GPT-124M/350M や Qwen-0.6B/4B で Muon や既存のテンソル対応手法(TEON)より一貫して性能が改善した。
papers.why: Muon 系の行列対応オプティマイザをさらに層間の相関まで扱えるよう拡張しており、より大規模な層構成や QKV 以外のモジュールにも適用できる最適化手法の選択肢を広げる。
papers.summary_en: Matrix-aware optimizers such as Muon improve on AdamW for LLM pretraining but treat layers independently, neglecting cross-layer correlations; existing tensor-aware optimizers rely on matricization-based tensor algebra and remain restricted to shallow stacking and specific modules. The authors propose TUON, built on a transform-based tensor algebra derived from Tensor-SVD, which mixes layers via a unitary transform, polarizes each transformed slice, then inverts the transform, and they prove it performs steepest descent under a transformed tensor spectral norm with a convergence guarantee. On GPT-124M/350M and Qwen-0.6B/4B, TUON improves consistently over Muon and TEON, with ablations confirming the transformation mechanism, cross-layer structure beyond two-layer stacking, adaptability beyond QKV, and robustness to the polarization method.
papers.why_en: Extends Muon-style matrix optimizers to capture cross-layer correlations and scales to more layers and diverse modules beyond QKV, widening the set of optimizer choices for large-scale pretraining.

papers.title: Accelerating SO(2)-Equivariant Materials Models through Low-Precision Emulation
papers.abstract: Rotationally equivariant architectures improve the physical fidelity of machine-learned (ML) universal materials models based on graph neural networks (GNNs). However, their scalability is limited by the use of non-trivial, high-precision tensor operations during both training and inference. Adopting the reduced-precision formats of matrix multiplication units (MMUs), e.g., FP8 instead of FP32, provides massive increases in throughput, up to 30x (60x) on NVIDIA Hopper (Blackwell) GPUs, but may lead to drastic loss of accuracy. Here, we introduce tailored 'emulated' low-precision operations under the integer Ozaki scheme to accelerate the 'SO(2)-equivariant' processing layers of GNNs, which dominate the runtime of (1) many state-of-the-art ML interatomic potentials (MLIPs) and (2) most universal ML Hamiltonian (MLH) models. Our framework, FlashSO(2), outperforms TF32, the most accurate native low-precision MMU format, in throughput, accuracy, and memory footprint at once. At the SO(2) layer level, it reaches 40x (7x) the throughput of MALOQ's (UMA's) reference implementation, an MLH (MLIP) model, sustaining up to 236 (232) effective Tflop/s on an NVIDIA GH200, 3.5x the FP32 peak. At the model level, FlashSO(2) helps train MALOQ 3.9x faster than its pure-FP32 version while reducing peak memory by 58% at no loss in accuracy. In molecular dynamics simulations with UMA, the speedup factor is 3.3x, and the peak memory is reduced by 51%. FlashSO(2) thus pushes the speed-accuracy Pareto frontier of equivariant materials models beyond the native low-precision formats and substantially lowers the resources required to exploit their scaling laws.

papers.title: Context Is Not Free: Carbon-Aware LLM Routing for Multi-Turn LLM Web Services across Geo-Distributed Data Centers
papers.abstract: The sustainability of the Web has drawn growing attention, as large language model (LLM)-based web services leave a substantial carbon footprint. These services typically run in geo-distributed data centers whose grid carbon intensity varies across regions and over time, so routing each query to a cleaner region or a smaller model can reduce emissions. A conversation, however, is a stateful web session: each turn reuses the key--value (KV) cache of its history, which resides only where earlier turns were served. Serving a turn on another deployment requires recomputing this history, whose carbon cost grows with the conversation and can outweigh the saving of the move. Existing carbon-aware LLM routers treat a conversation's queries as independent and ignore this cost. We present CarbonRouter, an online framework that jointly selects the model, GPU type, and region for each query to minimize carbon emissions. CarbonRouter introduces a cache-aware carbon cost model, which charges history recomputation to every candidate deployment using cached-token counts from the serving backends, and uses a lightweight gate that keeps a session on its cached deployment when it would likely move back at the next turn and rebuild its history again. We evaluate CarbonRouter in trace-driven experiments on two real-world conversation datasets with five LLMs, three GPU types, and four regions, where it achieves the lowest carbon of all policies. CarbonRouter reduces CO$_2$ by 16.1\% on average relative to FairCarbon, a state-of-the-art carbon-aware router with the same action space, while also improving predicted answer quality and estimated latency. Moreover, the saving rises further to 23.1\% for sessions longer than 30 turns.
papers.ja_title: KV キャッシュの移動コストを考慮したカーボン配慮型 LLM ルーティング CarbonRouter
papers.summary: LLM サービスは地理的に分散したデータセンターで動いており、電力の二酸化炭素排出量は地域や時間帯で変わるため、問い合わせをよりクリーンな地域や小さいモデルに振り分けると排出量を減らせる。しかし会話は前のやり取りの KV キャッシュ(計算結果の保存)が置かれた場所でしか安く続けられず、別の場所に移すと履歴を計算し直すコストがかかる。CarbonRouter はこの計算し直しコストをキャッシュされたトークン数から計算に入れてモデル・GPU 種類・地域を選び、同じ選択肢を使う既存手法(FairCarbon)に比べ二酸化炭素排出量を平均 16.1%、30 ターンを超える長い会話では 23.1% 削減した。
papers.why: KV キャッシュの再利用コストをルーティング判断に組み込む設計は、省エネだけでなく複数地域・複数モデルに分散した LLM サービング全般のルーティング基盤の参考になる。
papers.summary_en: LLM web services run across geo-distributed data centers with time- and region-varying grid carbon intensity, but routing a multi-turn conversation to a cleaner region requires recomputing its KV-cache history, whose carbon cost grows with the conversation and can outweigh the savings of the move; existing carbon-aware routers treat a conversation's queries as independent and ignore this. The authors present CarbonRouter, an online framework that jointly selects model, GPU type, and region per query using a cache-aware carbon cost model that charges history recomputation to every candidate deployment from cached-token counts, plus a lightweight gate that keeps a session on its cached deployment when it would likely move back next turn. In trace-driven experiments on two real conversation datasets with five LLMs, three GPU types, and four regions, it achieves the lowest carbon of all evaluated policies, reducing CO2 by 16.1% on average versus FairCarbon (rising to 23.1% for sessions longer than 30 turns) while also improving predicted answer quality and estimated latency.
papers.why_en: Folding KV-cache reuse cost into routing decisions is relevant beyond carbon-awareness, as a template for any routing policy spanning multiple regions, GPU types, or model deployments.

papers.title: Thermal-Headroom Routing for Efficient Robot Perception in Extreme Heat
papers.abstract: Adaptive robot perception systems must balance detector accuracy, inference latency, and energy consumption, particularly when high ambient temperatures cause processors to thermally throttle. We propose Thermal-Headroom Routing (THR), a lightweight model-selection policy that forecasts processor temperature using a closed-form RC thermal model and excludes detector configurations predicted to cross a throttling threshold. We evaluate THR with four YOLO11 configurations across seven real-world perception traces, eight ambient temperatures, and 20 randomized seeds, comparing it with latency-aware routing, fixed-threshold thermostats, duty caps, and a matched-compute-budget control. At ambient temperatures of 45-55 degrees C and a tight inference deadline, THR eliminates throttling in simulation, reduces deadline misses by 3.9-7.5 percentage points, and reduces energy per on-time frame by approximately 12-13% relative to a latency-belief router. A separate experiment using deadline-paced, nonoverlapping frame execution yields miss-rate reductions of 6.2-9.5 percentage points. A tuned thermostat or duty cap can match THR at a fixed operating point; predictive routing is most useful when ambient conditions or calibrated thermal parameters differ from those used to tune static policies. Measurements on an Apple M5 support the single-node heating approximation but do not validate hardware throttling. The results characterize the conditions under which thermal forecasting improves the efficiency and timeliness of resource-constrained robot perception.

papers.title: InterQ-RL: Interaction-Aware Correction of Execution Mismatch in Quantized Agentic RL
papers.abstract: Multi-turn agent reinforcement learning (RL) relies on long closed-loop rollouts, making generation and KV-cache costs a major bottleneck. Quantized rollout reduces these costs, but its low-precision executor also serves as the behavior policy and can induce execution mismatch with the learner. Existing quantized-RL methods are designed primarily for single-turn generation. They align the learner forward with quantized rollout or correct the current-token rollout-learner ratio, without modeling the policy history that produces each agent state. Even after quantization alignment, residual rollout-learner mismatch accumulates along the state-reaching policy history, so a current action may look locally aligned despite a mismatched history. We introduce InterQ-RL (Interaction-aware Quantized Reinforcement Learning) to correct this post-alignment mismatch. It applies bounded execution-prefix correction over the state-reaching policy history, allocates correction strength across action segments by effective support under a fixed displacement budget, and requires no additional model forward pass. We evaluate dense and mixture-of-experts (MoE) backbones from 4B to 30B on ALFWorld, WebShop, and ScienceWorld, with all quantized arms sharing the same rollout with 8-bit weights, activations, and KV cache (W8A8-KV8). Across four environment-backbone settings, InterQ-RL achieves the strongest quantized endpoint result, matching BF16 to within 0.7 points and exceeding it in two settings. It matches or exceeds the learning speed of alignment alone while avoiding its late performance regression.
papers.ja_title: 量子化したエージェント強化学習の実行ずれを補正する InterQ-RL
papers.summary: 複数ターンにわたりツールを使うエージェントの強化学習では、長い往復のやり取りの生成と KV キャッシュのコストが大きな負担になり、量子化(低精度化)で軽くすると、低精度の実行役(ロールアウト)が学習役とずれてしまう問題があった。InterQ-RL は、現在の 1 手だけでなく状態に至るまでの過去の方針履歴全体に対して補正をかける方式を提案した。4B から 30B の密なモデルと専門家混合(MoE)モデルを使った実験で、8 ビットの重み・活性・KV キャッシュという量子化構成のもとで、16 ビット精度の性能に 0.7 ポイント差まで迫り、2 つの設定ではそれを上回った。
papers.why: 強化学習の実行基盤を量子化して軽くする際に生じる実行ずれの蓄積という問題に、学習全体の履歴を見て補正する具体的な手法を示しており、RL 訓練基盤の低コスト化に直結する。
papers.summary_en: Quantized rollout reduces generation and KV-cache cost in multi-turn agentic RL, but the low-precision executor also serves as the behavior policy, and existing quantized-RL methods align the learner with quantized rollout or correct only the current-token ratio, without modeling the policy history that produced each state; residual rollout-learner mismatch therefore accumulates along that history even after alignment. InterQ-RL applies bounded execution-prefix correction over the state-reaching policy history, allocating correction strength across action segments by effective support under a fixed displacement budget, with no additional forward pass. Evaluated on dense and MoE backbones from 4B to 30B on ALFWorld, WebShop, and ScienceWorld under W8A8-KV8 quantization, it achieves the strongest quantized endpoint result across four environment-backbone settings, matching BF16 within 0.7 points (exceeding it in two settings) and sustaining single-rollout training at 35B where tested critic-free baselines deteriorate after initial gains.
papers.why_en: Addresses the accumulated mismatch between quantized rollout and the learner across long multi-turn interactions, a concrete fix for a bottleneck in making agentic RL training cheaper.

papers.title: CRIM: Composable and Reusable Item Memory for Efficient Personalized Retrieval
papers.abstract: Large language models incur substantial training and inference costs in personalized search and recommendation, as growing interaction histories lengthen request inputs and repeatedly expose the same item text to the model. We propose \textbf{C}omposable and \textbf{R}eusable \textbf{I}tem \textbf{M}emory (CRIM), a framework that separates item-level semantic encoding from request-level history modeling. A small set of learnable summary tokens compresses each item into compact continuous memories, while segment-level readout tokens (REC tokens) introduce predictive supervision within the interaction history. These memories are independent of users and queries and can therefore be reused across requests. At inference time, CRIM composes cached memories in interaction order and incorporates an optional query to produce a personalized retrieval representation, reducing repeated item-text encoding while retaining request-dependent contextual modeling. We further introduce a joint training mechanism that combines cached memories with sampled live re-encoding. Re-encoding only a few history items per request allows the retrieval objective to jointly optimize the item and request encoders at limited computational cost, while periodic cache refreshes maintain consistency. Extensive evaluation and cost analysis on MovieLens-1M, Qilin, and our new LazSeq dataset show that CRIM achieves state-of-the-art retrieval performance with substantially lower inference costs at the same backbone scale, while limiting item re-encoding during joint training. We will publicly release our code and dataset.
papers.ja_title: 個人化検索のための再利用可能なアイテム記憶を作る CRIM
papers.summary: 個人向け検索や推薦で大規模言語モデルを使うと、利用者ごとの履歴が長くなるほど同じ商品やアイテムの説明文を何度も読み直すコストが増えていく。CRIM はアイテムごとの意味表現を少数の要約トークンに圧縮して利用者やクエリと独立に再利用できる形にし、推論時にはキャッシュされたこの表現を履歴の順番でつなぎ合わせて個人化した表現を作る。MovieLens-1M や Qilin などのデータセットで、同じ規模の土台モデルのもとで推論コストを大きく下げながら最高水準の検索性能を達成した。
papers.why: アイテム表現をキャッシュして再利用するという考え方は、LLM サービングにおけるプレフィックスキャッシュや KV キャッシュの発想を検索・推薦の文脈に応用したものとして参考になる。
papers.summary_en: LLM-based personalized search and recommendation incur substantial training and inference cost because growing interaction histories lengthen request inputs and repeatedly expose the same item text to the model. CRIM separates item-level semantic encoding from request-level history modeling: a small set of learnable summary tokens compresses each item into compact, user- and query-independent continuous memories, segment-level REC tokens add predictive supervision within the interaction history, and a joint training mechanism mixes cached memories with sampled live re-encoding (re-encoding only a few history items per request) with periodic cache refreshes. On MovieLens-1M, Qilin, and a new LazSeq dataset, CRIM achieves state-of-the-art retrieval performance with substantially lower inference cost at the same backbone scale, while limiting item re-encoding during joint training.
papers.why_en: Caching and reusing item-level representations across requests mirrors prefix/KV-cache ideas from LLM serving, applied to the retrieval and recommendation setting.

papers.title: One Megakernel is Not Enough: Predicting Where to Cut for Streaming Inference
papers.abstract: We address a fundamental question: How far should kernel fusion extend and which boundaries are worth preserving? Unlike the general convention of using one monolith megakernel at lower batch sizes or supporting only a selective model component as megakernel and rest of the model as conventional graph, we show that the best configuration is a composition of multiple megakernels with no overlapping conventional graph component, or a fully conventional graph. We present a framework that selects megakernel regions in a streaming inference model from conventional-graph profiles and standalone kernel benchmarks, without running any candidate design end to end. It simulates each candidate's tile and event graphs to predict time to first output and selects the measured best design in all 13 combinations of model and batch size we tested. Across NH-TTS, Qwen3-TTS and Llama-1B, the best composition ranges from two to four megakernels to fully conventional execution and none is a single megakernel. We introduce four model categories (megakernel-stable/ receding/ advancing/ averse) that capture how a model's best megakernel composition changes with batch size. Using NH-TTS model on H100 NVL GPU, we demonstrate that preserving three specialized megakernels can improve both latency and throughput despite introducing additional kernel boundaries. At batch size 32, this design delivers 21.4% lower mean batch-p95 time to first audio (TTFA) and 28% higher throughput than the evaluated monolith megakernel. Against conventional TensorRT graph execution, it reduces engine-level mean batch TTFA p95 by 4.05x and increases throughput by 19.7%.
papers.ja_title: ストリーミング推論でどこまでカーネルを融合すべきかを予測する手法
papers.summary: GPU 上の推論を速くするカーネル融合(複数の計算を 1 つのまとまりにまとめる技術)は、1 つの巨大なカーネル(メガカーネル)にまとめるのが一般的だが、この研究はモデルとバッチサイズごとに最適な構成が複数のメガカーネルの組み合わせや通常のグラフ実行である場合が多いことを示した。候補を実際に動かさずにタイルとイベントの動きを模擬して予測する仕組みを作り、テストした 13 通りのモデル・バッチサイズの組み合わせすべてで実測の最良構成を選び当てた。NH-TTS モデルで 3 つの専用メガカーネルを残す構成は、バッチサイズ 32 で単一メガカーネルより音声出力までの時間(p95)を 21.4% 短縮し、スループットを 28% 向上させた。
papers.why: 「カーネル融合は多いほど良い」という前提を実測で否定し、どこで融合境界を残すべきかを事前に予測する設計手法を示しており、推論エンジン開発の意思決定に直接使える。
papers.summary_en: Contrary to the common convention of fusing a streaming inference model into one monolithic megakernel at lower batch sizes (or fusing only a selective component), the authors show the best configuration is often a composition of several megakernels with no overlapping conventional-graph component, or a fully conventional graph. They present a framework that predicts where to place megakernel boundaries from conventional-graph profiles and standalone kernel benchmarks, simulating each candidate's tile and event graphs without running any candidate end to end, and across all 13 tested model/batch-size combinations it selects the measured-best design; on NH-TTS, Qwen3-TTS, and Llama-1B, the best composition ranges from two to four megakernels to fully conventional execution, and none is a single megakernel. On NH-TTS on an H100 NVL GPU, preserving three specialized megakernels gives 21.4% lower mean batch-p95 time-to-first-audio and 28% higher throughput than the evaluated monolith megakernel at batch size 32, and 4.05x lower engine-level p95 TTFA plus 19.7% higher throughput versus conventional TensorRT graph execution.
papers.why_en: Empirically overturns the assumption that more kernel fusion is always better and offers a prediction method for where to preserve kernel boundaries, directly useful for inference engine design decisions.

papers.title: S3AC: Stabilized, Selective, and Scalable Actor-Critic for LLM Reasoning
papers.abstract: Critic-free methods are widely used in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) for long chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, avoiding difficult and costly critic training. Common alternatives lack token-level credit assignment and typically rely on grouped rollouts to estimate prompt-specific baselines. A critic can address both limitations, but long-CoT critic training is hindered by insufficient coverage of trajectories with diverse lengths and early gradients dominated by the newly initialized value head. We introduce S3AC (Stabilized, Selective, and Scalable Actor-Critic) for LLM reasoning, built around a practical critic-training recipe. The trained critic provides token-specific advantages and prompt-specific baselines. Using the prompt-level baseline to estimate difficulty, we propose Difficulty-Aware Prompt Sampling (DAPS). DAPS combines this estimate with outcome history to select prompts before generation, reducing rollout waste without offline difficulty initialization. S3AC improves group-rollout performance across dense and mixture-of-experts models from 1.5B to 397B parameters, outperforming a modern GRPO variant (GRPO-X). At 35B, it sustains single-rollout training while tested critic-free baselines deteriorate after initial gains.
papers.ja_title: LLM 推論の強化学習向け安定・選択的・拡張可能なアクタークリティック S3AC
papers.summary: 検証可能な報酬を使う強化学習(RLVR)で長い思考過程を学習させる際、価値関数(クリティック)を使わない手法はトークン単位の評価ができず、グループ単位の比較に頼っているが、クリティックを学習させるには長さの異なる軌跡を十分カバーする工夫が必要だった。S3AC は実用的なクリティック学習手順を核に、クリティックが出すプロンプトごとの難易度推定を使って生成前に有望なプロンプトを選ぶ Difficulty-Aware Prompt Sampling を導入した。1.5B から 397B パラメータの密な・専門家混合(MoE)モデルで既存手法(GRPO-X)を上回り、35B では他のクリティック不要の手法が途中で性能が落ちる中、単一軌跡だけの学習でも性能を維持した。
papers.why: 大規模な強化学習後訓練でクリティックを安定して学習させる実用的な手順と、無駄な生成を減らすプロンプト選択の仕組みを示し、RL 後訓練基盤のスケーラビリティに関わる。
papers.summary_en: Critic-free RLVR methods for long chain-of-thought reasoning avoid costly critic training but lack token-level credit assignment and typically rely on grouped rollouts for prompt-specific baselines; training a critic to fix this is itself hindered by insufficient coverage of trajectories with diverse lengths and early gradients dominated by a newly initialized value head. S3AC introduces a practical critic-training recipe that gives token-specific advantages and prompt-specific baselines, and uses the prompt-level baseline to estimate difficulty for Difficulty-Aware Prompt Sampling (DAPS), which combines this estimate with outcome history to select prompts before generation and reduce rollout waste without offline difficulty initialization. Across dense and MoE models from 1.5B to 397B parameters, S3AC improves group-rollout performance over a modern GRPO variant (GRPO-X), and at 35B it sustains single-rollout training while tested critic-free baselines deteriorate after initial gains.
papers.why_en: Gives a practical recipe for stabilizing critic training at scale and a difficulty-aware prompt-sampling method to reduce rollout waste, both relevant to the scalability of RL post-training infrastructure.

papers.title: Quantitative Generalization Bounds for Multi-Layer Transformers: A Few Long Strings can Beat Many Short Ones
papers.abstract: Transformer-based language models exhibit an astonishing capacity to generalize to longer and more difficult problem instances than those seen in training. However, theoretical understanding of this phenomenon still lags behind. Unlike most machine learning models, the generalisation abilities of transformers inherently require considering two axes. On one hand, one must examine in-distribution statistical generalisation, which concerns the ability of a model to broaden a function from training samples to novel samples of the same distribution. On the other hand, given the sequential nature of language data, one must also consider length generalisation, which reflects whether a model trained on inputs of a given length can extrapolate to longer ones. These two notions have mostly been studied separately, leaving open how they interact. In this work, we give a joint treatment of both axes for fixed-precision transformers. We give generalisation guarantees in terms of the parameter sizes of the involved models, as well as the quantization space and the alphabet size that supply the sequences. Finally, we illustrate how the requirements in the sample count and training length trade off. In particular, we find that increasing training length can be exponentially more efficient than increasing the sample size. Experiments support predictions of the theory.
papers.ja_title: 多層 Transformer の統計的一般化と長さ一般化を同時に扱う理論的な汎化保証

papers.title: Auto-Research Arena: Benchmarking and Advancing Auto-Research in Language Modeling
papers.abstract: As autonomous research systems become more capable, benchmarks must both evaluate their performance and support meaningful research progress. We introduce Auto-Research Arena, a multi-target benchmark for evaluating autonomous research systems and discovering ideas in language modeling. Arena supports diverse research objectives within a shared experimental environment by separating admissibility from improvement: model quality and resource constraints determine whether a result qualifies, while the selected target measures progress among admissible results. We instantiate Arena in language model pretraining with nine targets spanning model, data, training, and inference efficiency, and evaluate seven research harnesses using two foundation models. Arena clearly differentiates existing harnesses across research objectives, with several sophisticated methods outperformed by our simple sequential search baseline, indicating substantial headroom in current auto-research systems. Beyond evaluation, Arena reveals a substantially broader frontier of model and system ideas aligned with active research directions. Reusing these discoveries in a new quality-driven search yields lower training loss under matched data and FLOPs and lower held-out BPB at the same model size. Together, Arena provides a common framework for benchmarking autonomous research and expanding its scope in language modeling. The code is available at https://github.com/Auto-Research-Arena/auto-research-arena
papers.ja_title: 自律研究システムを比較するベンチマーク Auto-Research Arena

papers.title: Distributed LLM Inference via Communication-Efficient Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract: Distributed speculative decoding has emerged as a promising approach for device--server collaborative large language model (LLM) inference, but its decoding speedup is often limited by the vocabulary-scale communication overhead. In existing distributed speculative decoding methods, exact rejection sampling requires transmitting full token distributions over the LLM vocabulary between the device and the server, which becomes costly in bandwidth-constrained environments. To address this issue, we propose DISCO, a communication-efficient framework for distributed speculative decoding, that eliminates vocabulary-scale distribution transfer while preserving the exact target distribution. DISCO achieves this by introducing a server-side replica of the draft small language model (SLM), which enables the server to locally obtain the draft-side distribution required for rejection sampling. As a result, DISCO exchanges only drafted token indices and scalar probability values between the device and the server. Experimental results on multiple datasets show that DISCO consistently achieves higher decoding speedup than existing distributed speculative decoding methods, particularly under stringent bandwidth constraints.
papers.ja_title: 語彙サイズの通信を避ける分散投機的デコード DISCO
papers.summary: 端末とサーバーで協力して LLM を動かす投機的デコード(小さいモデルで下書きを作り大きいモデルが検証する高速化手法)は、下書きと本番モデルの確率分布を語彙全体ぶん送受信する必要があり、通信が細い回線では速度が出ない。DISCO はサーバー側にも下書き用の小さいモデルの複製を置き、トークンの番号と確率の数値だけをやり取りすることで、語彙全体の分布を送らずに済ませる。複数のデータセットでの実験で、特に通信帯域が厳しい条件において既存の分散投機的デコード手法より高い高速化を一貫して達成した。
papers.why: 端末-サーバー分離推論で通信量がボトルネックになる場面に直接効く設計で、帯域制約下のエッジ推論基盤を作る際の実装の参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Distributed speculative decoding for device-server collaborative LLM inference is often bottlenecked by vocabulary-scale communication overhead, since exact rejection sampling requires transmitting full token distributions over the LLM vocabulary between device and server. DISCO eliminates this by introducing a server-side replica of the draft small language model, which lets the server locally obtain the draft-side distribution needed for rejection sampling, so only drafted token indices and scalar probability values need to be exchanged, while the exact target distribution is preserved. Experimental results on multiple datasets show DISCO consistently achieves higher decoding speedup than existing distributed speculative decoding methods, particularly under stringent bandwidth constraints.
papers.why_en: Directly targets the communication bottleneck in device-server disaggregated speculative decoding, a concrete design for bandwidth-constrained edge inference.

papers.title: h1: A Taste of the Bitter Lesson in Automated Theorem Proving
papers.abstract: While progress in informal mathematics has come largely from scaling the chain-of-thought and agentic reasoning of frontier language models, formal theorem proving has increasingly relied on human-designed workflows around these models, such as planning, decomposition, and orchestrating specialized provers. This raises a bitter-lesson question: can a simple agentic loop that scales test-time compute match these workflows? The answer matters as formal verification must scale to keep up with frontier models producing research mathematics, yet new workflows rarely settle it, as their gains are often confounded with stronger models or more compute. We study this question with h1, a simple harness that gives a model an efficient interface to Lean 4 and keeps it working through verifier feedback and self-reflection, without imposing a decomposition or search structure. h1 reaches state-of-the-art results on PutnamBench, FATE-X, and FormalConjectures100-Solved, settles eight open problems in FormalConjectures, and, at matched models, matches or outperforms specialized workflows such as Goedel-Architect and AlphaProof Nexus, surprisingly showing that a single attempt (pass@1) can often scale to solve open problems. Through ablations and matched-model comparisons with Claude Code and AxProverBase, we find that simplicity alone is not enough: an efficient Lean interface largely determines cost and solve rate. We thus recommend that future work evaluate frontier models with efficient execution feedback before prescribing workflows, at the risk of bitter lessons.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 定理証明におけるシンプルな探索の強さを示す h1

papers.title: Let the Gate Decide: Per-Lookup Precision for Quantized Conditional Memory in LLMs
papers.abstract: Conditional memory layers, such as DeepSeek's Engram, attach large hashed n-gram tables to a language model, and removing them from DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash costs 36.8 PopQA points. Low-bit quantization loses long-tail facts first, and the standard remedy, giving more bits to frequently accessed rows, backfires: refining lookups by access frequency is worse than refining them at random. We trace this to the gate that scales each retrieved row. A lookup's quantization error is weighted by its gate, which is small for frequent n-grams, large for the rare n-grams of long-tail entities, and computable from a 1-bit code. GateRQ therefore stores each row as a ladder of 1-bit residual codes, keeps level 1 in GPU memory to compute the gate, and reads deeper levels only for the lookups the gate ranks highest. Without retraining, GateRQ cuts GPU table memory by 7.8x on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, which raises vLLM throughput by 11%-31% over FP8 tables, while losing about 1 PopQA point at 1.50 bits read per lookup and 0.2 points at 2.10 bits across two models.
papers.ja_title: ゲートの値で読み出し精度を変える条件付きメモリの量子化 GateRQ
papers.summary: DeepSeek の Engram のような巨大なハッシュ表(n-gram ごとに知識を格納する表)を LLM から外すと精度が 36.8 ポイント落ちるほど重要だが、低ビット量子化(数値を少ないビット数で表現してメモリを減らす手法)をすると珍しい知識ほど先に失われ、よく使われる行に多くビットを割く従来のやり方は逆効果だった。原因は各行をスケーリングする「ゲート」の値にあり、GateRQ はゲートが大きい(=珍しい知識の)行だけ深いビットまで読む仕組みにした。再学習なしで DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash の表メモリを 7.8 倍削減し、FP8 表と比べて vLLM のスループットを 11〜31% 向上させつつ、1 ルックアップあたり 1.50 ビットで精度低下は約 1 ポイントに留めた。
papers.why: 巨大な条件付きメモリ表を持つモデルのサービング効率化に直結し、量子化の割り当てを頻度でなく重要度の代理指標で決める発想が他の疎構造にも応用できる。
papers.summary_en: Conditional memory layers such as DeepSeek's Engram attach large hashed n-gram tables to a language model, and removing them from DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash costs 36.8 PopQA points; low-bit quantization loses long-tail facts first, and the standard remedy of giving more bits to frequently accessed rows backfires, since refining lookups by access frequency is worse than refining them at random. The authors trace this to the gate that scales each retrieved row, which is small for frequent n-grams, large for rare long-tail entities, and computable from a 1-bit code; GateRQ therefore stores each row as a ladder of 1-bit residual codes, keeps level 1 in GPU memory to compute the gate, and reads deeper levels only for the lookups the gate ranks highest. Without retraining, GateRQ cuts GPU table memory by 7.8x on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, raising vLLM throughput by 11%-31% over FP8 tables, while losing about 1 PopQA point at 1.50 bits read per lookup and 0.2 points at 2.10 bits across two models.
papers.why_en: Directly improves serving efficiency for models with huge conditional-memory tables, and allocating quantization depth by a gate-based importance proxy rather than access frequency is an idea that may transfer to other sparse structures.

papers.title: OmniBrain-0: A Unified Agentic Model for Embodied Intelligence
papers.abstract: General-purpose embodied intelligence requires robots to coordinate diverse skills over long horizons, track task progress, and recover from failures. Specialist policies alone do not ensure task-level reliability, while powerful multimodal agents rely on costly reasoning and external experience that compact models struggle to reproduce. We introduce OmniBrain-0, a lightweight unified embodied agent that coordinates manipulation and navigation through a shared high-level decision model, integrating task understanding, planning, progress tracking, and feedback-driven recovery. Our progressive training framework combines embodied pretraining, domain-specialized agent distillation, and multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD). It distills powerful teachers' interaction experience into manipulation and navigation experts, then consolidates their decision capabilities into OmniBrain-0. Unification therefore occurs within the learned decision model rather than only at the tool interface. We further introduce Rubric-Guided Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI), a data flywheel in which a Meta-Agent turns execution evidence into refined rubrics, step-level reminders, and verified trajectories for domain-expert updates before their reconsolidation into OmniBrain-0 through MOPD. We evaluate OmniBrain-0 on LIBERO-Pro, LIBERO-Plus, RoboCasa365, RoboTwin 2.0, and R2R-CE Val-Unseen, as well as multiple real-world manipulation tasks. OmniBrain-0 combines strong cross-domain task performance with substantially lower inference and execution overhead than its closed-source teacher, demonstrating efficient transfer and consolidation of embodied capabilities into a compact unified agent.
papers.ja_title: 操作とナビゲーションを統合するロボット向けエージェント OmniBrain-0

papers.title: How Much Does the Hint Matter? Scope Conditions for Hindsight Self-Distillation in Financial Reasoning
papers.abstract: Financial institutions operating under data-residency constraints are restricted to open-weight models small enough to locally host, which trail frontier systems on multi-step quantitative reasoning. On-policy distillation narrows such gaps by supervising a student on its own rollouts, but traditional OPD requires a strong external teacher, and on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) conditions on a full reference solution. We ask how much of that signal is necessary. We present Fin-SD, a localized hindsight self-distillation recipe for multi-step reasoning. Given a problem the student fails, the student itself identifies the first incorrect reasoning step and writes a short critique of that step. We truncate the student's trajectory immediately before the error (aiming to obtain a correct prefix), condition a frozen copy of the student on the same prefix plus the hint, and distill that hint-conditioned teacher into the student over a short rollout under reverse KL. No external model contributes a gradient. We apply Fin-SD to GPT-OSS-20B on a custom multi-step financial reasoning benchmark that requires deriving formula inputs from realistic scenarios via accounting conventions. We find: (i) replacing the critique with a generic-feedback control matches Fin-SD's entire 3.03 pp accuracy gain over the base model on the FinanceReasoning Hard subset, suggesting the gain comes from where supervision is applied, not hint content; (ii) the model writing the hint does not need to be stronger than the model receiving it: hints from same-family GPT-OSS-120B, at roughly 6x the parameters, yield no materially greater benefits than self-written hints; and (iii) Fin-SD matches on-policy self-distillation from full reference solutions on accuracy while generating 9.5% fewer tokens. With Fin-SD, general reasoning on MMLU-Pro and a fourteen-metric compliance audit on FinTrust show no material regression.
papers.ja_title: 金融推論における事後ヒント自己蒸留の効果が成立する条件 Fin-SD

papers.title: Physical structure as an organizing principle for universal Hamiltonian learning
papers.abstract: Density functional theory (DFT) gives the electronic structure of materials, but its cost limits large-supercell calculations and materials screening. Machine-learned Hamiltonians bypass the self-consistent cycle but are usually system-specific; universal ones could cover new compositions and disordered solids. Such models must generalize across chemistry and keep downstream properties physical, while staying inexpensive for large cells. Here we introduce UniTB, a universal E(3) equivariant Hamiltonian representation framework that integrates physical priors rooted in density-functional tight-binding theory with deep learning. UniTB's network, which corrects a prior Hamiltonian, generalizes across chemistry through a mixture of experts routed by that prior and a charge-equilibration head as in self-consistent-charge tight binding. A projection bounds band shifts from the prior, suppressing spurious states and keeping downstream properties physical. We provide the fastest SO(2) tensor-product GPU kernels for the network. The variant UniTB-Flash assembles its prior from two-center tables at $O(N)$ cost for $N$ atoms, against $O(N\log N)$ on a grid. Trained on 29,242 crystals, UniTB reaches a 0.48 meV matrix-element error on nonmagnetic test crystals spanning 68 elements. Without amorphous training data, both models agree with DFT optics and conductivity of amorphous Ge-Sb-Te. UniTB-Flash ranks candidates with no significant difference from UniTB, whose property values are more accurate; together they screen 16,195 crystals for five application domains of industrial relevance.
papers.ja_title: 材料科学向け汎用ハミルトニアン学習モデル UniTB

papers.title: Plenty of Room in the Middle: Revealing Opportunities on a GPU Cluster via Fine-Grained Monitoring
papers.abstract: GPU clusters have become essential computing resources for AI and scientific research in academia and industry. However, their high cost and growing demand often result in long queueing delays. While previous monitoring efforts have operated at second- or minute-level frequencies, they primarily informed job-level scheduling for clusters and lacked the detail needed to optimize GPU-level utilization. This paper presents an in-depth study of a university research GPU cluster, analyzing resource usage at 100 ms intervals. We have developed a lightweight monitoring tool that leverages Nvidia's DCGM library to capture fine-grained "compute utilization" metrics within GPUs. Deployed on a cluster with 89 nodes and 319 GPUs, our tool collected data over several months. This paper focuses on a 10-day period with 7,399 jobs submitted by 150 users from 12 departments. Our study reveals three key findings: (1) the GPU cluster exhibits significant underutilization, with over 70% of jobs using less than 20% of GPU memory and 50% averaging below 5% Streaming Multiprocessor (SM) utilization; (2) 80% of jobs have a drastic mismatch between their requested and actual durations, significantly limiting the scheduler's effectiveness; and (3) the multi-GPU jobs we examined show highly periodic communication patterns. These findings suggest there is plenty of room in the middle: substantial utilization gains are available through better job scheduling and GPU multitasking, independent of hardware or application improvements. Our monitoring solution is available as open-source software at https://github.com/als244/gpu_server_monitoring.
papers.ja_title: 100 ミリ秒間隔の計測で見えた GPU クラスタの空き時間
papers.summary: 大学の研究用 GPU クラスタは高価で順番待ちが長いのに、実際にどれだけ使われているかは秒〜分単位の粗い監視しか無く分からなかった。研究者らは Nvidia の DCGM ライブラリを使い 100 ミリ秒間隔で使用率を測る軽量な監視ツールを作り、89 ノード・319 GPU のクラスタで数か月間データを集めた。7,399 件のジョブを調べた結果、70% 以上のジョブが GPU メモリの 20% 未満しか使わず、50% は GPU の計算ユニット使用率が平均 5% 未満だったほか、80% のジョブで申請した実行時間と実際の実行時間が大きくずれていた。
papers.why: スケジューラ改善や GPU の相乗り(マルチタスク化)だけで、ハードウェアを増やさずに大きな利用率改善の余地があることを実測で示しており、クラスタ運用の優先課題を定量的に裏付ける。
papers.summary_en: GPU clusters are essential but expensive and in high demand, yet prior monitoring at second- or minute-level frequency informed job-level scheduling without the detail needed to optimize GPU-level utilization. The authors built a lightweight tool using NVIDIA's DCGM library to capture fine-grained compute utilization at 100ms intervals, deployed it on an 89-node, 319-GPU university research cluster over several months, and focus on a 10-day period covering 7,399 jobs from 150 users across 12 departments. They find the cluster exhibits significant underutilization (over 70% of jobs use less than 20% of GPU memory, 50% average below 5% SM utilization), 80% of jobs show a drastic mismatch between requested and actual duration (limiting scheduler effectiveness), and multi-GPU jobs show highly periodic communication patterns; the monitoring tool is released as open-source software.
papers.why_en: The authors argue these findings show 'plenty of room in the middle': substantial utilization gains are available through better job scheduling and GPU multitasking alone, independent of hardware or application improvements.

papers.title: INC-MoE: Overlapping In-Network Collectives and Expert Computation for Expert-Parallel Mixture-of-Experts Inference
papers.abstract: In expert-parallel mixture-of-experts (MoE) serving, dispatch moves tokens to the accelerators hosting their selected experts, and combine returns expert outputs to each token's owner. Both operations lie on the critical path and can dominate MoE layer latency in multi-node deployments. We present INC-MoE, an expert-parallel MoE layer that offloads dispatch and combine to the network switch and overlaps both collectives with each other and with expert computation. Dispatch uses in-network AllGather through switch-side multicast, while combine uses in-network ReduceScatter through switch-side reduction. Both collectives use message semantics between the end hosts and the switch. Because the in-network collectives load opposite directions of each link, executing them concurrently reduces bandwidth-bound communication time by $(N-2)/(2(N-1))$ relative to concurrent ring-based collectives: 33% for four ranks and 43% for eight. INC-MoE partitions tokens into bands and processes them through a three-stage AllGather-feed-forward network (FFN)-ReduceScatter pipeline inside a single persistent kernel. At steady state, role-specialized thread blocks gather the next band, compute the current band, and reduce the previous band concurrently, overlapping both collectives with each other and with computation using device-side synchronization. INC-MoE integrates as a drop-in replacement for the MoE layer of vLLM. We evaluate it in an emulated four-node scale-out deployment with a dedicated accelerator emulating an in-network computing (INC) switch. On OLMoE prefill with four-way expert parallelism, INC-MoE reduces time to first token (TTFT) by up to 33% and increases throughput by up to 50% relative to vLLM's default collective path, while matching its outputs.
topics: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.theme: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.ja_title: ネットワークスイッチに通信を肩代わりさせる MoE 推論 INC-MoE
papers.summary: 複数ノードにエキスパート(専門家ごとのサブネットワーク)を分散させる MoE(Mixture-of-Experts、複数の専門家に処理を振り分けるモデル構造)推論では、トークンを担当エキスパートに送る dispatch と結果を集める combine の通信が遅延の主因になりやすい。INC-MoE はこの 2 つの集団通信をスイッチ側のマルチキャストと縮約処理に任せ、計算と通信を一つの GPU カーネル内で同時に重ねて進める。4 ノードでの疑似評価では、通信時間の理論削減が 4 ランクで 33%、8 ランクで 43% となり、OLMoE の prefill 処理で初回応答までの時間を最大 33% 短縮、スループットを最大 50% 向上させた(vLLM 標準の通信経路比)。
papers.why: MoE のボトルネックである dispatch/combine 通信をネットワーク機器側にオフロードする具体的な設計で、集団通信とカーネル実行をどう重ねるかの実装パターンが参考になる。
papers.summary_en: In expert-parallel MoE serving, the dispatch collective that moves tokens to the accelerators hosting their selected experts and the combine collective that returns outputs both lie on the critical path and can dominate MoE layer latency in multi-node deployments. INC-MoE offloads dispatch and combine to the network switch (dispatch via switch-side multicast AllGather, combine via switch-side reduction ReduceScatter, using message semantics between end hosts and the switch) and overlaps both collectives with each other and with expert computation inside a single persistent kernel, where role-specialized thread blocks concurrently gather the next band, compute the current band, and reduce the previous band. Because the in-network collectives load opposite directions of each link, running them concurrently reduces bandwidth-bound communication time by (N-2)/(2(N-1)) relative to concurrent ring-based collectives (33% for four ranks, 43% for eight); on OLMoE prefill with four-way expert parallelism in an emulated four-node deployment, INC-MoE reduces time to first token by up to 33% and increases throughput by up to 50% relative to vLLM's default collective path, while matching its outputs.
papers.why_en: Offloading MoE dispatch/combine to the network switch and overlapping both collectives with computation inside one persistent kernel is a concrete pattern for interleaving communication and computation at the kernel level to cut MoE serving latency.

papers.title: Executable Archaeology of Programs That Model Programming: Reanimating the Heuristic Compiler (1961) and KBEmacs (1984)
papers.abstract: Early AI programs were often also theories of how people think, and programs that wrote programs were, in part, theories of how people program. Here we report on the reanimation of two such programs that offer two seemingly different theories of programming and were developed for quite different purposes. The first, Herbert Simon's Heuristic Compiler (1961), was an experimental model of programming as problem-solving, applying the means-ends analysis methods of the General Problem Solver to investigate the nature of the programming task. The second, KBEmacs (1984), was a working prototype of an intelligent programming assistant developed by MIT's Programmer's Apprentice project, built on the view that expert programmers recognize and combine familiar patterns, or "cliches." It let a programmer build up programs by combining cliches through a stylized English command language. We approach both through the methodology of Executable Archaeology, the study of historical computational systems by running their original code, a process we call "reanimation." Our reanimation of the Heuristic Compiler reproduces the compiled code appearing in Simon's 1963 paper, and our reanimation of KBEmacs reproduces the SQRT sequence of its December 1984 self-test. Examined side by side, the two theories turn out to have much in common: the Heuristic Compiler also works by adapting existing routines, and Simon later argued that search alone requires a large body of programming knowledge. To highlight the reflexivity of this project, we deliberately used a modern AI-assisted programming tool, Anthropic's Claude Code (Opus 5.5), to carry out much of the detailed reanimation work, building on a significant base of existing software. The explicit, executable theories of programming that both systems embodied are largely absent from today's far more capable AI coding assistants.
papers.ja_title: 古い AI プログラムを実行し直す「実行可能な考古学」

papers.title: JustGoal: With Only a Goal, the AI Baseline Is Above the Expert Kernels
papers.abstract: A small number of GPU kernels often determines the efficiency of large language model training and inference.
