High-performance kernel development typically relies on expert knowledge through manual implementation, collaboration with general-purpose models, or specialized agents equipped with domain knowledge, evaluation methods, and search workflows. We investigate how much value this knowledge provides as foundation models become stronger. We introduce JustGoal, a goal-only baseline in which a general-purpose agent receives only the optimization objective and constraints, without kernel-specific infrastructure, knowledge bases, or predefined workflows, and builds its own evaluation loop. On NVIDIA B200 GPUs, JustGoal outperforms open-source libraries on 8 of 10 operators, achieving per-operator geometric mean speedups of 1.14x to 2.34x. It also surpasses the fastest publicly released specialized-agent kernel on 5 of 9 operators with available comparisons. In a controlled same-model comparison using Fable 5.1 on single shapes, the KDA-0.5 harness reaches 0.95x of JustGoal's performance, while single-mechanism ablations show no consistent benefit from domain knowledge or predefined workflows. These results indicate that specialized machinery should be justified by clear gains over a same-model, same-scope goal-only baseline and reevaluated whenever the foundation model changes.
papers.ja_title: 目的だけ渡した汎用エージェントが専用カーネルを超える JustGoal
papers.summary: GPU カーネル(GPU 上で動く計算処理の最小単位のプログラム)の性能は LLM の学習・推論速度を左右するが、高性能な実装には専門家の知識やカーネル専用の探索の仕組みが必要とされてきた。JustGoal は最適化の目標と制約だけを汎用エージェントに渡し、カーネル固有の知識ベースや既定の探索手順を与えずに自分で評価ループを組ませる手法である。NVIDIA B200 GPU 上で 10 個の演算のうち 8 個で既存のオープンソースライブラリを上回り(幾何平均で 1.14〜2.34 倍の高速化)、比較可能な 9 個のうち 5 個で公開済みの専用エージェントのカーネルも超えた。
papers.why: 基盤モデルが強くなるほどカーネル専用の仕組みの価値が薄れることを示しており、カーネル最適化自動化に投資する前に「目的だけ与えた素のエージェント」を基準線として比較すべきだという教訓になる。
papers.summary_en: High-performance GPU kernel development typically relies on expert knowledge through manual implementation, collaboration with general-purpose models, or specialized agents equipped with domain knowledge, evaluation methods, and search workflows; the authors investigate how much value this knowledge still provides as foundation models get stronger. They introduce JustGoal, a goal-only baseline in which a general-purpose agent receives only the optimization objective and constraints, without kernel-specific infrastructure, knowledge bases, or predefined workflows, and builds its own evaluation loop. On NVIDIA B200 GPUs, JustGoal outperforms open-source libraries on 8 of 10 operators (per-operator geometric-mean speedups of 1.14x to 2.34x) and surpasses the fastest publicly released specialized-agent kernel on 5 of 9 operators with available comparisons; in a controlled same-model comparison using Fable 5.1 on single shapes, the KDA-0.5 harness reaches only 0.95x of JustGoal's performance, and single-mechanism ablations show no consistent benefit from domain knowledge or predefined workflows.
papers.why_en: The authors conclude that specialized kernel-optimization machinery should be justified by clear gains over a same-model, same-scope goal-only baseline, and reevaluated whenever the foundation model changes -- a methodological bar for this whole line of work.

review.note: 専門知識ベースや既定の探索手順を持つカーネル最適化エージェントの価値を、同じモデルを使った「目的だけ渡した素のエージェント」基準線との比較とアブレーションで検証し、単一機構の追加には一貫した効果が無いと示した。ツール・仕組みを追加する前に同条件の基準線と比べ、モデルが変わるたびに再評価すべきという検証のやり方の教訓。
review.note_en: Tests the value of specialized kernel-agent infrastructure (knowledge bases, predefined workflows) against a same-model goal-only baseline and ablations, finding no consistent benefit from any single mechanism -- a methodological lesson to benchmark added machinery against a matched baseline and re-check it whenever the underlying model changes.

papers.title: CoHARL: Co-Evolving Agent Policies and Executable Harnesses with Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents interact with their environments through executable harnesses that govern tool use and feedback. Optimizing a harness for a fixed policy overlooks how its behavior changes during learning, while training a policy under a fixed harness leaves the interface that generates its training experience unchanged. This motivates adapting the harness throughout policy training. We introduce CoHARL, a population-based reinforcement learning framework that co-evolves a shared policy and a population of executable harnesses. The policy learns from rollouts across the population, and a proposer uses its execution traces to revise harness code during training. CoHARL achieves a 27.6% mean resolved rate on SWE-rebench, improving over harness-only search by 6.4 percentage points. Experiments on SWE-bench Verified and Terminal-Bench 2.0 show gains in software engineering and terminal-based tasks. Under matched training budgets, CoHARL also outperforms searching for a harness once before RL and alternating policy updates with revisions to a single active harness.
papers.ja_title: エージェントの方針と実行環境を同時に進化させる強化学習 CoHARL

papers.title: Proposing Better Rollouts for On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) improves language-model post-training by letting the student learn from its own sampled trajectories under teacher supervision, aligning the training process with inference-time behavior. However, the rollout policy in OPD is usually treated as fixed: each round samples directly from the current student. We show that this choice can create a compounding teacher--student mismatch, because it requires the teacher to provide effective supervision on whichever trajectories the student samples, including ones less reachable by the teacher itself. On such trajectories, teacher supervision can become noisy or even misleading, leading to undesirable student patterns such as repetition. Moreover, since the updated student in turn defines the rollout policy of subsequent rounds, these patterns persist and potentially amplify over training. This failure mode suggests that improving OPD requires treating the rollout policy itself as an optimization target, rather than only modifying the distillation objective. We propose Mixture Proposal On-Policy Distillation (MPOPD), which derives a student-anchored, teacher-guided rollout distribution from a local trust-region objective based on relative teacher support. The resulting target is a geometric mixture of the student and teacher policies, and we introduce a proposal policy that approximates this mixture, enabling rollout generation in a single forward pass. Experiments on 16 math, knowledge, and medical reasoning benchmarks show consistent gains over OPD and recent variants. On math reasoning, our method improves average accuracy by 6.91 over OPD on Qwen3-4B-Base while reducing average generation length by 41%, suggesting that rollout policy design provides an effective way to improve OPD.
papers.ja_title: オンポリシー蒸留は「誰が答案を書くか」を変えると良くなる（MPOPD）
papers.summary: オンポリシー蒸留（生徒が自分で書いた答案を先生が 1 語ずつ直す学習）では、ふつう答案は今の生徒がそのまま書く。すると先生自身が書きそうにない答案まで直すことになり、先生の指導がぶれて、同じ言葉のくり返しのような悪い癖が回を追うごとに強まる。そこで生徒と先生の中間にあたる書き手を 1 回の計算で作り、その書き手に答案を書かせる MPOPD を提案した。数学では Qwen3-4B-Base で、ふつうのオンポリシー蒸留より平均の正解率が 6.91 ポイント上がり、答案の長さは平均で 41% 短くなった。
papers.why: 損失の形ではなく、答案を作る側（ロールアウトの方策）を設計の対象にする提案である。答案が 4 割短くなるので、蒸留の基盤で一番重い生成の計算量も減る。
papers.summary_en: On-policy distillation (OPD) usually samples rollouts directly from the current student, but the authors show this can create a compounding teacher-student mismatch, since it requires the teacher to supervise whichever trajectories the student samples, including ones less reachable by the teacher itself; on such trajectories teacher supervision can become noisy or misleading, producing undesirable patterns such as repetition that persist and amplify because the updated student in turn defines the next round's rollout policy. They propose Mixture Proposal On-Policy Distillation (MPOPD), which derives a student-anchored, teacher-guided rollout distribution from a local trust-region objective based on relative teacher support, approximated by a proposal policy -- a geometric mixture of student and teacher -- that enables rollout generation in a single forward pass. Across 16 math, knowledge, and medical reasoning benchmarks, MPOPD shows consistent gains over OPD and recent variants, improving average accuracy by 6.91 points over OPD on Qwen3-4B-Base on math reasoning while reducing average generation length by 41%.
papers.why_en: Treats the rollout policy itself, rather than only the distillation objective, as an optimization target, and the 41% shorter generations also cut the compute cost of the heaviest part of distillation.

papers.title: Efficient Quantization Training with Stochastic Rounding via Structured Subspace Randomness
papers.abstract: Low-precision training often relies on stochastic rounding (SR) to keep quantized gradients unbiased and prevent small updates from rounding to zero. Standard SR draws an independent random threshold for every gradient element. However, accelerators generate random numbers on vector units whose throughput lags far behind their matrix units. Drawing one threshold per element saturates the vector unit and can make INT8 training with SR slower than BF16 training. Sharing random thresholds across tensor elements removes this cost but forces those elements to round in the same direction and shifts their rounding errors by a common offset. We find that this offset degrades training primarily through the activation gradient, which propagates the error backward into earlier layers. Because earlier layers cannot cancel an incoming offset using their own local rounding errors, the offset must be removed at the layer where it originates. We propose Structured Subspace Stochastic Rounding (S3R), which quantizes each upstream gradient once for both the activation and weight gradient matrix multiplications and shares a single threshold per token across the hidden dimension. Its error correction, S3R-EC, subtracts the structured mean rounding error from the activation and weight gradients while leaving the optimizer unchanged. In LLM pre-training experiments, uncorrected threshold sharing degrades convergence, whereas S3R-EC eliminates this degradation and matches the validation loss of independent SR. Furthermore, S3R-EC accelerates full INT8 training steps of dense LLMs on TPU v5p by 1.24x to 1.32x over BF16 and by 1.11x over independent SR.
papers.ja_title: 乱数しきい値を共有しても精度を落とさない量子化学習 S3R
papers.summary: 低精度学習では確率的丸め(小さな更新がゼロに丸まって消えるのを防ぐため乱数を使って丸める方式)が使われるが、全ての要素ごとに乱数を引くと、行列演算を行う装置より遅い乱数生成装置が追いつかず INT8 学習が BF16 学習より遅くなってしまう。乱数のしきい値を要素間で共有すれば速くなるが、丸め誤差が同じ方向に偏り、その偏りが逆伝播で前の層に伝わって学習を乱す。S3R はこの偏りが生じた層でその場で補正する手法で、TPU v5p 上での LLM 事前学習において乱数共有による精度劣化を解消しつつ、INT8 学習を BF16 比で 1.24〜1.32 倍、乱数を共有しない従来方式比で 1.11 倍高速化した。
papers.why: 量子化学習のスループットを乱数生成というハードウェア制約の観点から詰めており、低精度学習パイプラインで乱数共有と精度のトレードオフをどう設計するかの具体策になる。
papers.summary_en: Low-precision training often relies on stochastic rounding (SR) to keep quantized gradients unbiased, but drawing an independent random threshold per element saturates accelerators' vector units (whose throughput lags their matrix units), which can make INT8 training with SR slower than BF16 training; sharing thresholds across elements removes this cost but shifts rounding errors by a common offset, which the authors find degrades training primarily through the activation gradient propagating the offset backward into earlier layers that cannot cancel an incoming offset with their own local rounding errors. They propose Structured Subspace Stochastic Rounding (S3R), which quantizes each upstream gradient once for both activation and weight gradient matmuls and shares a single threshold per token across the hidden dimension, with S3R-EC subtracting the structured mean rounding error from activation and weight gradients while leaving the optimizer unchanged. In LLM pretraining experiments, S3R-EC eliminates the degradation from uncorrected threshold sharing and matches independent SR's validation loss, while accelerating full INT8 training steps of dense LLMs on TPU v5p by 1.24x to 1.32x over BF16 and 1.11x over independent SR.
papers.why_en: Traces an INT8-training slowdown to a hardware constraint (random-number-generation throughput on vector units) rather than a purely algorithmic one, and gives a concrete correction that recovers both speed and accuracy.

papers.title: InfraDev: Can Coding Agents Develop AI Infrastructure, and How Can We Tell?
papers.abstract: Coding agents are beginning to develop the production-grade AI infrastructure that trains and serves large models, yet existing benchmarks cover only single kernels or single-GPU tasks, and grade with tests and prompts that misjudge both correct and incorrect patches. We introduce InfraDev, a benchmark of 36 tasks built from real-world pull requests to Megatron-LM, vLLM, and verl, covering infrastructure development for training, inference, and reinforcement learning. Each task asks an agent to reimplement a real change that spans many files and must run correctly across many GPUs. To grade such changes, we jointly synthesize hidden probes, which enforce the requirements the original tests leave unchecked, and a prompt that states every interface the probes call without revealing the solution. We also design a shared execution environment that reuses dependencies and artifacts across tasks, cutting storage by 52-57% and build time by 13-14% on Megatron-LM and vLLM. Across six frontier models, the best resolves only 38.9% of the tasks; the probes reject 32% of the submissions that pass every official test, and with the original pull request descriptions as prompts, no model resolves a single task. Failure analysis shows that structural and state errors dominate and that agents' own tests rarely check memory, time, or traffic. Turning these findings into an agent skill raises the resolved rate of a frontier model on the Megatron-LM tasks by 10.5%.
papers.ja_title: コーディングエージェントが AI 基盤そのものを開発できるかを測る InfraDev
papers.summary: コーディングエージェントの評価は単一カーネルや単一 GPU の課題にとどまり、Megatron-LM や vLLM、verl のような実際の学習・推論・強化学習基盤の開発を測れていなかった。InfraDev はこれら 3 つのプロジェクトへの実際の pull request から作った 36 個の課題で、複数ファイルにまたがり複数 GPU で正しく動く変更を再実装させ、元のテストでは見逃す要件を検出する隠しテストと解答を明かさないプロンプトを合わせて自動生成して採点する。6 つの最先端モデルのうち最良のものでも解けたのは 38.9% のみで、公式テストを全て通った提出のうち 32% が隠しテストで不合格になり、元の pull request の説明文をそのままプロンプトにすると 1 件も解けなかった。
papers.why: LLM の学習・推論基盤のコード変更がどこで失敗しやすいか(メモリ・時間・通信の確認漏れが多いなど)を定量的に示しており、AI 基盤開発にエージェントを使う際の限界と注意点を具体的に把握できる。
papers.summary_en: Existing coding-agent benchmarks cover only single kernels or single-GPU tasks and grade with tests and prompts the authors say misjudge both correct and incorrect patches, leaving no benchmark for the production-grade AI infrastructure that coding agents are beginning to develop. InfraDev introduces 36 tasks built from real pull requests to Megatron-LM, vLLM, and verl, each asking an agent to reimplement a multi-file change that must run correctly across many GPUs, graded by jointly synthesized hidden probes that enforce requirements the original tests leave unchecked plus a prompt stating every interface the probes call without revealing the solution; a shared execution environment reusing dependencies and artifacts across tasks also cuts storage by 52-57% and build time by 13-14% on Megatron-LM and vLLM. Across six frontier models, the best resolves only 38.9% of tasks, the probes reject 32% of submissions that pass every official test, and no model resolves a single task when given the original pull request descriptions as prompts; failure analysis shows structural and state errors dominate and that agents' own tests rarely check memory, time, or traffic, and turning these findings into an agent skill raises a frontier model's resolved rate on the Megatron-LM tasks by 10.5%.
papers.why_en: Quantifies where LLM training/inference/RL infrastructure changes are most likely to fail (memory, timing, and traffic checks are rarely covered by agents' own tests), giving concrete, countable evidence for the limits of using coding agents on AI infrastructure.

review.note: 隠しテストは公式テストが見逃す要件を検出し、公式テストを全て通った提出の 32% を不合格にする。失敗分析ではメモリ・時間・通信の確認漏れが最も多いとわかった。PR レビューでテストが通っているだけでなくメモリ・時間・通信の面を見るべきという、具体的なチェック観点を示す。
review.note_en: Hidden probes catch requirements the project's own tests miss (rejecting 32% of submissions that pass every official test), and failure analysis finds agents' own tests rarely check memory, time, or network traffic -- a concrete checklist of what an infra PR review should verify beyond passing tests.

papers.title: Select-TTT: Query-Conditioned Selective Fast Weight Updates for In-Place Test-Time Training
papers.abstract: Test-time training (TTT) enables a deployed language model to internalize incoming context on-the-fly into a small set of fast-weight parameters, rather than merely treating it as transient context for attention. In-Place TTT recently made this idea practical for large language models by repurposing the down-projection of standard MLP blocks as fast weights. However, we find that its benefit largely disappears on realistic web long-context question answering. We attribute this to In-Place TTT's uniform write schedule: every chunk is written with equal strength, so irrelevant content dilutes query-relevant information in fast-weight memory. Building on this insight, we propose Select-TTT, a model-agnostic, query-conditioned rule for In-Place TTT that scales each chunk's write strength by its relevance to the user query. This relevance signal requires no supervision and no new parameters: it is read directly from the model's frozen output head, as the probability mass that a chunk's hidden states assign to the query tokens. A temperature-scaled softmax turns these scores into learning-rate multipliers, leaving the chunk-wise, context-parallel computation of In-Place TTT intact. Select-TTT consistently improves long-context question answering on two benchmarks and two backbones. These findings highlight the value of query-conditioned fast weight writes for practical test-time training on long-context question answering, which is also potentially promising for long-horizon agent tasks involving multiple user queries over evolving contexts.
papers.ja_title: 質問との関連度で書き込みの強さを変えるテスト時学習 Select-TTT
papers.summary: テスト時学習(モデルを動かしながら入力された文脈を少数の追加パラメータに覚えさせる手法)の一種である In-Place TTT は、長い文脈のどの部分も同じ強さで記憶に書き込むため、質問と関係ない内容が記憶を薄めてしまい、実際の長文 Web 質問応答ではほとんど効果が消えることが分かった。Select-TTT はこの問題を解決するため、各文書の断片が質問とどれだけ関連するかをモデル自身の出力層から追加の学習なしで読み取り、その関連度に応じて書き込みの強さ(学習率)を調整する。2 つのベンチマークと 2 つのモデルで長文脈質問応答の性能を一貫して改善した。
papers.why: 長い文脈を扱う推論基盤でテスト時学習を使う場合、関連度に応じた書き込み制御が効くという実装上の具体的な改善策を示している。
papers.summary_en: In-Place TTT made test-time training practical for large language models by repurposing the down-projection of standard MLP blocks as fast weights, but the authors find its benefit largely disappears on realistic web long-context question answering, which they attribute to a uniform write schedule that writes every chunk with equal strength, letting irrelevant content dilute query-relevant information in fast-weight memory. They propose Select-TTT, a model-agnostic, query-conditioned rule that scales each chunk's write strength by its relevance to the user query -- a relevance signal requiring no supervision and no new parameters, read directly from the model's frozen output head as the probability mass a chunk's hidden states assign to the query tokens, turned into learning-rate multipliers via a temperature-scaled softmax that leaves the chunk-wise, context-parallel computation of In-Place TTT intact. Select-TTT consistently improves long-context question answering on two benchmarks and two backbones.
papers.why_en: Gives a concrete, parameter-free fix for a reported failure mode of test-time training on realistic long-context QA, which the authors suggest could also help long-horizon agent tasks involving multiple user queries over evolving contexts.

papers.title: Evolving Agent Teams
papers.abstract: The rapid progress of software engineering agents drives interest in applying them to open-ended problems such as GPU kernel optimization. However, we find that existing coding agents converge to local optima on real-world, expert-written kernels (e.g., FlashInfer). We introduce Evolving Agent Teams, a multi-agent framework that escapes such local optima. It features (1) a central supervisor that diagnoses each local optimum and restructures a team of agents; and (2) a persistent file system that comprises a learning document, an evolution history, and per-team artifacts, grounding restructuring with accumulated experience. Under a matched token budget, Evolving Agent Teams consistently outperforms strong coding-agent baselines. With an extended token budget, Evolving Agent Teams generates a CUDA kernel that reaches 1.2x mean speedup over the production FlashInfer MLA paged decode kernel from scratch and wins on 36 of 47 production workloads from FlashInfer-Bench (0.86-0.99x on the remaining 11). It also demonstrates superior performance on tasks such as KDA prefill on AMD MI350X (3.01x over vLLM) and NVIDIA B200 (3.44x over FlashKDA), MoE expert-offload serving on Apple silicon (30.3 tokens/s decode for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next in MLX 4-bit on a 48 GB M4 Pro), and RoboDojo robot manipulation (62.1 on held-out seeds vs. 55.3 for the best leaderboard entry). Code is available at https://github.com/caoshiyi/EAT.
papers.ja_title: 局所解から脱出するエージェントチームでカーネルを進化させる Evolving Agent Teams
papers.summary: 既存のコーディングエージェントは FlashInfer のような専門家が書いた実際の GPU カーネルの最適化において、ある程度よい解に達すると改善が止まってしまう局所最適に陥りやすい。Evolving Agent Teams は各局所最適の原因を診断してエージェントチームの構成を立て直す監督役と、学習内容や進化の履歴を蓄積するファイルシステムを組み合わせた複数エージェントの枠組みである。トークン予算を拡張した条件では、ゼロから作った CUDA カーネルが FlashInfer の MLA デコードカーネルを平均 1.2 倍高速化し、47 個の実運用ワークロードのうち 36 個で勝利し、AMD MI350X 上の KDA prefill では vLLM の 3.01 倍、NVIDIA B200 では FlashKDA の 3.44 倍の速度を達成した。
papers.why: 単純な繰り返し改善では止まってしまうカーネル最適化を、チーム構成の動的な見直しと経験の蓄積で突破する具体例であり、エージェントによるカーネル自動最適化の実用的な上限を押し上げている。
papers.summary_en: Existing coding agents applied to open-ended GPU kernel optimization converge to local optima on real-world, expert-written kernels such as FlashInfer. The authors introduce Evolving Agent Teams, featuring a central supervisor that diagnoses each local optimum and restructures a team of agents, plus a persistent file system (a learning document, evolution history, and per-team artifacts) that grounds restructuring in accumulated experience. Under a matched token budget it consistently outperforms strong coding-agent baselines, and with an extended token budget it generates a CUDA kernel from scratch that reaches a 1.2x mean speedup over the production FlashInfer MLA paged decode kernel, winning on 36 of 47 production FlashInfer-Bench workloads (0.86-0.99x on the remaining 11), and also shows strong results on KDA prefill on AMD MI350X (3.01x over vLLM) and NVIDIA B200 (3.44x over FlashKDA), MoE expert-offload serving on Apple silicon (30.3 tokens/s decode for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next in MLX 4-bit on a 48GB M4 Pro), and RoboDojo robot manipulation (62.1 vs. 55.3 for the best leaderboard entry).
papers.why_en: Addresses the local-optimum problem in agentic kernel optimization through dynamic team restructuring and accumulated experience rather than just more iterations, pushing the practical ceiling of agent-driven kernel optimization.

papers.title: PailitaoMMSearch2.0 Technical Report: Scaling Generative Retrieval to Unified End-to-End Multimodal Search
papers.abstract: Generative retrieval models have been increasingly adopted in search and recommendation systems. However, industrial generative retrieval models are commonly specialized to a fixed online scenario: they learn from scenario-specific interactions, support a narrow set of query forms and retrieval objectives. We study how to remove these couplings and build a unified end-to-end multimodal search system for open-ended image--text queries, heterogeneous shopping intents, and online scenarios with different resource constraints. We present \textbf{PailitaoMMSearch}, which directly generates product Semantic IDs from a raw query image and free-form instruction and scales along three dimensions. \textbf{Data scaling} uses a reusable toolset that can be composed into intent- and lifecycle-specific workflows for cold-start synthesis, quality control, real-traffic refinement, and continuous data production. \textbf{Intent scaling} progressively equips one model with e-commerce product knowledge, multiple retrieval relations, and adjustable reasoning budgets through continual pre-training (CPT), mixed-budget supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and unified reinforcement learning (RL). The RL stage combines intent-balanced optimization and Sample--Beam rollouts aligned with multi-candidate serving. \textbf{Scenario scaling} exposes quality--cost operating points across model capacity and reasoning budget. The system is deployed in multimodal search applications on Taobao Pailitao. A controlled online A/B test reports statistically significant improvements, including item page views $\textbf{+17.90\%}$, transactions $\textbf{+27.04\%}$, and gross merchandise value $\textbf{+8.94\%}$.
papers.ja_title: 画像検索を統合する生成的検索システム PailitaoMMSearch2.0

papers.title: Meta Models: Models that Model Learning
papers.abstract: Every neural-network training run produces not only a model, but also evidence about how models learn. Can these accumulated experiments enable us to predict and compare new training runs before executing them? We study meta-models: models that predict the learning behavior of other models. From this perspective, final-performance prediction, learning-curve prediction, and hyperparameter selection are different queries to the same training response function. We take a first, humble empirical step toward this goal: treating real language-model training records as native numeric data, we find that an off-the-shelf tabular in-context learner, TabPFN, can match or outperform a fine-tuned LLM meta-model in multiple evaluated settings. Whereas recent work fine-tunes LLMs on tokenized configurations at a cost of tens to hundreds of GPU-hours, TabPFN requires seconds of fit-and-predict time without task-specific weight updates. We argue that meta-modeling is better treated as its own numeric modality rather than as a text task for LLMs. Going one step further, augmenting TabPFN with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) further improves accuracy on selected prediction tasks. Finally, we pre-registered a forecast of the Marin Hero Run, a 535B-parameter public training run, whose ground truth is revealed point by point as training progresses, putting meta-model predictions to the test against training outcomes not yet observed at the time of forecasting.
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 学習の挙動そのものを予測するメタモデル Meta Models
papers.summary: ニューラルネットワークの学習を 1 回実行すると、できあがったモデルだけでなく「どう学習が進んだか」という記録も得られるが、この蓄積された記録から新しい学習を実行する前に性能を予測できるかを調べた研究である。LLM の学習ログを表形式の数値データとして扱うと、既製の表データ用モデルである TabPFN が、数十〜数百 GPU 時間をかけて専用に学習させた LLM による予測と同等かそれ以上の精度を、数秒の計算だけで達成できた。さらに Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks という手法を組み合わせると一部の予測課題で精度が向上し、535B パラメータの公開学習プロジェクト Marin Hero Run に対する予測を学習の進行前に登録して検証した。
papers.why: 学習曲線や最終性能、ハイパーパラメータ選択を「同じ予測問題への異なる問い合わせ」として統一的に扱う視点を示し、大規模学習の事前見積もりに LLM を使わない安価な代替手段を提案している。
papers.summary_en: Every neural-network training run produces not only a model but also evidence about how models learn, which raises the question of whether accumulated experiments can predict and compare new training runs before executing them; the authors frame final-performance prediction, learning-curve prediction, and hyperparameter selection as different queries to the same training response function. As a first, humble empirical step, treating real language-model training records as native numeric data, they find an off-the-shelf tabular in-context learner, TabPFN, can match or outperform a fine-tuned LLM meta-model in multiple evaluated settings, requiring seconds of fit-and-predict time without task-specific weight updates versus the tens to hundreds of GPU-hours recent work spends fine-tuning LLMs on tokenized configurations; augmenting TabPFN with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks further improves accuracy on selected prediction tasks, and the authors pre-registered a forecast of the Marin Hero Run, a 535B-parameter public training run, to test predictions against training outcomes not yet observed at forecasting time.
papers.why_en: Argues meta-modeling of training behavior is better treated as its own numeric modality than as a text task for LLMs, offering a much cheaper alternative for predicting large-scale training outcomes in advance.

papers.title: V-LUMEN: Visual Lookup Memory for Embedding Scaling in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Embedding-level scaling expands the capacity of language models through lookup-based memory rather than by increasing model depth, width, or dense computation. Extending this idea to vision-language models (VLMs) is challenging because visual features are continuous, spatially structured, and query-dependent, unlike discrete text tokens that naturally support n-gram lookup. We introduce V-LUMEN, a visual lookup memory for VLMs. V-LUMEN discretizes visual features with a frozen codebook, builds spatially aware memory keys through spatial aggregation-based hashing, and modulates them with text-conditioned relevance signals; all addressing is non-parametric, and the retrieved embeddings are fused into the backbone through a gated residual pathway. On five reasoning-intensive benchmarks, V-LUMEN substantially improves a frozen Qwen3-VL-2B backbone and transfers zero-shot to three benchmarks whose images are disjoint from the training data. At a matched parameter budget, moving part of a LoRA or MoE adapter's capacity into V-LUMEN preserves accuracy on two backbones, indicating that external visual memory is an independent capacity axis rather than a stronger adaptation method. Because lookup cost is constant in table size and incurred only once at prefill, this capacity grows in storage rather than in per-token compute. Code is available at https://github.com/miso-choi/V-Lumen.
papers.ja_title: 視覚情報を検索可能な記憶として外付けする V-LUMEN
papers.summary: テキストの n-gram のような検索可能な記憶によってモデルの容量を増やす手法は、連続的で空間的な構造を持つ視覚特徴には単純には使えなかった。V-LUMEN は視覚特徴を固定された符号表で離散化し、空間的な位置を考慮したハッシュで記憶のキーを作り、テキストに応じた関連度で調整したうえで、ゲート付きの残差経路でモデル本体に取り込む。5 つの推論寄りのベンチマークで固定した Qwen3-VL-2B のベース性能を大きく改善し、学習データに含まれない画像の 3 つのベンチマークにもそのまま転用でき、検索のコストは表のサイズに関わらず一定で prefill 時に 1 回だけ発生する。
papers.why: 記憶容量をパラメータ数ではなく外部ストレージ側に積む設計で、1 回限りの prefill コストで容量を増やせるため、per-token の計算コストを増やさずにモデル容量を拡張したい推論サービング側に示唆がある。
papers.summary_en: Embedding-level scaling expands model capacity through lookup-based memory rather than increasing depth, width, or dense computation, but extending this to vision-language models is hard because visual features are continuous, spatially structured, and query-dependent, unlike discrete text tokens that naturally support n-gram lookup. V-LUMEN discretizes visual features with a frozen codebook, builds spatially aware memory keys through spatial aggregation-based hashing, modulates them with text-conditioned relevance signals (all addressing is non-parametric), and fuses retrieved embeddings into the backbone through a gated residual pathway. On five reasoning-intensive benchmarks it substantially improves a frozen Qwen3-VL-2B backbone and transfers zero-shot to three benchmarks whose images are disjoint from the training data; at a matched parameter budget, moving part of a LoRA or MoE adapter's capacity into V-LUMEN preserves accuracy on two backbones, indicating external visual memory is an independent capacity axis rather than a stronger adaptation method, and because lookup cost is constant in table size and incurred only once at prefill, this capacity grows in storage rather than per-token compute.
papers.why_en: Adds model capacity via external storage rather than per-token compute, with lookup cost paid only once at prefill, relevant to serving setups that want more capacity without raising per-token inference cost.

papers.title: Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception
papers.abstract: Multimodal perception forms the foundation of multimodal intelligence. In particular, spatial perception and multimodal long-context understanding are two pivotal tasks that underpin embodied AI and multimodal agents. However, synthesizing targeted, high-quality training data for these tasks remains difficult and costly. Our key insight is that these tasks share an underlying capability, which we call connecting evidence: identifying relevant visual facts, binding them to the correct entities, recovering their relations, and composing them into an answer. Crucially, targeted training data are far easier to synthesize for this capability than for these tasks themselves. To strengthen this capability, we propose EvidenceConnect, an easy-to-implement data synthesis framework that uses zoomed views of related regions within a single image to generate questions requiring comparison, aggregation, or chaining of visual evidence. To ensure quality, a reference answer is retained only when independent VLMs agree on it, and region-ablation tests discard questions whose answer survives the removal of selected regions. We then train base VLMs on the resulting data with RLVR, obtaining Zooming without Zooming v2 (ZwZ2). Although the synthesized data are not tailored to any downstream benchmark, ZwZ2 improves fine-grained and spatial perception, with further gains on embodied spatial reasoning, multimodal long-context understanding, multimodal agent tasks, and general visual reasoning. These results establish EvidenceConnect as an effective framework for supervising evidence connection and suggest that strengthening this shared capability leads to more generalizable multimodal perception.
papers.ja_title: 視覚的な根拠をつなぐ能力を鍛える ZwZ2

papers.title: PipeLink: Contract-Guided Linking of GPU Kernel Components
papers.abstract: The fastest machine-learning kernels are compositions of components, such as loaders, matrix-multiply mainloops, epilogues and communication stages, that run concurrently on one GPU streaming multiprocessor and share its on-chip memory, barriers, warps and registers. Because these components hard-code where they sit in this shared space, they cannot be compiled, shipped or replaced on their own: combining components from different sources means forking them by hand or keeping them in separate kernels. We present PipeLink, a contract-guided linker for GPU kernel components. Each component is compiled separately into an LTO object that carries a contract stating what it requires and what it promises; PipeLink checks the contracts against each other, relocates every component by solving one joint placement of the SM's resources, and generates the transfers between them, and the vendor LTO backend folds the result into constants. Across 51 configurations on Hopper and Blackwell GPUs, linked kernels run within 0.2% of the same sources compiled as one unit. Linking makes new compositions practical: a CuTe attention operator inside a ThunderKittens decode megakernel speeds up decoding by 2.16$\times$, a four-owner MoE training megakernel matches the original monolith, one unchanged attention core yields sparse and context-parallel variants that outperform FlexAttention, vLLM and Transformer Engine, and a GEMM + SwiGLU composition whose consumer serves three GPU architectures runs 1.2$\times$ faster on Blackwell than cuBLAS with a compiled activation.
papers.ja_title: 契約に基づいて GPU カーネルの部品を結合する PipeLink
papers.summary: 最速の機械学習カーネルはローダーや行列積の本体処理、エピローグ、通信段階といった部品を 1 つの GPU の演算ユニット上で同時に動かして組み合わせているが、各部品がオンチップメモリやバリア、レジスタ上の自分の配置場所を決め打ちしているため、単体でコンパイル・配布・差し替えができず、組み合わせるには手作業での改造か別々のカーネルとして保つしかなかった。PipeLink は各部品を「何を要求し何を提供するか」を記した契約付きで別々にコンパイルし、契約同士を照合して SM(ストリーミングマルチプロセッサ、GPU の計算コアの単位)上の資源配置を 1 つの問題として解き、部品間のデータ受け渡しを生成する。Hopper と Blackwell の GPU 上の 51 通りの構成で、結合後のカーネルは元から 1 つのまとまりとしてコンパイルした場合と比べて性能差 0.2% 以内に収まり、ThunderKittens の decode メガカーネルに CuTe の attention を組み込むと decode が 2.16 倍速くなった。
papers.why: GPU カーネルの部品を再利用可能な単位として組み合わせる手段を提供し、現状手作業での改造に頼っているカーネル開発のモジュール化という課題に直接応える。
papers.summary_en: The fastest machine-learning kernels are compositions of components (loaders, matrix-multiply mainloops, epilogues, communication stages) that run concurrently on one GPU streaming multiprocessor and share its on-chip memory, barriers, warps, and registers, but because these components hard-code where they sit in this shared space, they cannot be compiled, shipped, or replaced on their own -- combining components from different sources means forking them by hand or keeping them in separate kernels. PipeLink is a contract-guided linker: each component compiles separately into an LTO object carrying a contract stating what it requires and what it promises, PipeLink checks the contracts against each other, relocates every component by solving one joint placement of the SM's resources, generates the transfers between them, and the vendor LTO backend folds the result into constants. Across 51 configurations on Hopper and Blackwell GPUs, linked kernels run within 0.2% of the same sources compiled as one unit, and linking makes new compositions practical: a CuTe attention operator inside a ThunderKittens decode megakernel speeds up decoding by 2.16x, a four-owner MoE training megakernel matches the original monolith, one unchanged attention core yields sparse and context-parallel variants that outperform FlexAttention, vLLM, and Transformer Engine, and a GEMM + SwiGLU composition serving three GPU architectures runs 1.2x faster than cuBLAS with a compiled activation on Blackwell.
papers.why_en: Provides a reusable, contract-based way to compose GPU kernel components without hand-forking, directly addressing the modularity problem that currently forces manual, one-off kernel engineering.

papers.title: TAO: Tool-Aware Joint Scheduling for LLM-Based Agentic Serving
papers.abstract: Agentic services alternate between model inference on clustered GPUs and external tools on distributed CPUs. In this scenario, existing systems (1) overlook tool-return readiness in service evaluation, wasting limited resources, and (2) use heuristic strategies to decide admission and placement on GPUs, resulting in suboptimal scheduling decisions. To bridge this gap, we present TAO, a tool-aware joint scheduling framework for LLM-based agentic serving. Its value interface combines near-term tool readiness, node-specific cache credit with time-aware decay, and token footprint; a dynamic program jointly selects and places waiting sessions under capacity constraints. Across the 12 reported model-workload-concurrency settings, TAO reduces latency by up to 26.8%, reduces mean time to first token (TTFT) by up to 36.3%, and increases decode throughput by up to 29.5% relative to the best evaluated state-of-the-art baseline for each metric.
papers.ja_title: ツール呼び出しの状況も見てスケジューリングする LLM エージェントサービング TAO
papers.summary: エージェント型サービスは GPU 上でのモデル推論と CPU 上で動く外部ツール呼び出しを交互に行うが、既存システムはツールの結果が戻ってくるタイミングを評価に取り込まず資源を無駄にし、GPU への受け入れと配置の判断も経験則に頼っていた。TAO はツールの戻り準備度、ノードごとのキャッシュの価値(時間減衰付き)、トークンの使用量を組み合わせた評価指標を作り、動的計画法で待機中のセッションをどのノードにいつ割り当てるかを同時に決める。12 通りのモデル・ワークロード・同時実行数の設定で、各指標について最良だった既存手法と比べ、レイテンシを最大 26.8%、初回応答までの時間(TTFT)を最大 36.3% 削減し、デコードのスループットを最大 29.5% 向上させた。
papers.why: ツール呼び出しを含むエージェント型サービングのスケジューリングでツールの戻りタイミングを明示的に評価に組み込む発想は、これまで経験則に頼っていた受け入れ・配置判断を定量化する具体策になる。
papers.summary_en: Agentic LLM services alternate between model inference on clustered GPUs and external tools on distributed CPUs, but existing systems overlook tool-return readiness in service evaluation (wasting limited resources) and use heuristic strategies to decide admission and placement on GPUs, resulting in suboptimal scheduling decisions. TAO is a tool-aware joint scheduling framework whose value interface combines near-term tool readiness, a node-specific cache credit with time-aware decay, and token footprint, with a dynamic program jointly selecting and placing waiting sessions under capacity constraints. Across 12 reported model-workload-concurrency settings, TAO reduces latency by up to 26.8%, mean time to first token (TTFT) by up to 36.3%, and increases decode throughput by up to 29.5% relative to the best evaluated state-of-the-art baseline for each metric.
papers.why_en: Explicitly incorporating tool-return timing into GPU admission and placement decisions is a quantitative replacement for the heuristic scheduling that agentic serving systems currently rely on.

papers.title: Watermark Basins: Black-Box Detection of Distilled LLMs
papers.abstract: Proprietary language models and their reasoning traces are vulnerable to API-based distillation, where an adversary trains a student model on the teacher model's outputs. To obtain evidence of distillation, model providers can watermark the teacher's outputs, aiming to leave a radioactive signal in the student's outputs. Existing black-box detectors search for such radioactivity using token-level statistics of the suspect model's outputs. However, token-level signals are not always detectable, for instance when the distillation traces are sampled at a low temperature. In this work, we discover the watermark basin, a persistent signal that enables more reliable watermark detection: during fine-tuning, watermarked teacher traces embed a distinct, key-specific geometric signal in parameter space that lies orthogonal to the ordinary task-specific fine-tuning subspace. Building on this, we introduce Watermark Basin Alignment (WM-Basin), a black-box watermark detector that queries the suspect model through its API, without access to its weights or logits. WM-Basin maps generated text to gradient representations using a fixed clean probe model, projects out the ordinary fine-tuning task directions, and tests whether the residual gradient aligns with the watermark basin induced by the watermark key. We evaluate WM-Basin extensively across diverse teacher models and student architectures (from 135M to 8.2B parameters) distilled on mathematical reasoning. At a strict 0.1% false-positive rate, WM-Basin detects 79% of distilled models at n-gram=1 and 45% at n-gram=3, substantially improving over the state-of-the-art token-level baseline (29% and 1.3%, respectively). Because the watermark signal resides in a persistent basin, it survives post-distillation modifications including quantization, pruning, and reinforcement-learning post-training.
papers.ja_title: 蒸留されたモデルを検出する電子透かしの痕跡 Watermark Basin

papers.title: EdgePace: Deadline- and Freshness-Aware LLM Scheduling on Unified-Memory Platforms
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly run on edge devices alongside tasks that continuously process sensor data. In many applications, these foreground tasks prepare observations as inputs to the LLM, whose outputs guide subsequent processing or actions. The observations must be processed by foreground deadlines, and LLM feedback must arrive while its source observations remain useful. Yet the CPU and accelerators share a unified-memory system, so LLM inference can delay foreground processing through memory-bandwidth contention even when compute resources remain available. We present EdgePace, a bandwidth-aware runtime that protects foreground deadlines while sustaining timely LLM feedback. EdgePace creates safe suspension points across prefill and decode, monitors foreground memory demand and stalls at low cost, and schedules inference according to contention risk, deadline slack, and output freshness. We evaluate EdgePace on a OnePlus 13 and three NVIDIA Jetson platforms using multi-camera processing and robotic target tracking. Relative to unmanaged inference, it reduces foreground deadline misses by 24.1%--96.1% while retaining 64.9%--98.5% of LLM throughput. All measured LLM outputs arrive within their task-defined freshness windows. On OnePlus 13, for example, camera deadline misses fall by 91.3% while 90.4% of LLM throughput is retained.
papers.ja_title: 締め切りと新しさを両立させるエッジ向け LLM スケジューリング EdgePace
papers.summary: エッジ端末では LLM がセンサーデータを処理する他のタスクと同じメモリを共有しており、計算資源が空いていても CPU とアクセラレータがメモリの帯域を取り合うことで LLM 推論が他のタスクの締め切りを乱してしまう問題がある。EdgePace は prefill と decode の処理の中に安全に中断できる地点を作り、他のタスクのメモリ要求を低コストで監視し、帯域の競合リスクや締め切りまでの余裕、出力の新しさ(情報が古くなっていないか)に応じて推論のタイミングを調整する。OnePlus 13 と 3 種類の NVIDIA Jetson 機で評価した結果、何も管理しない場合と比べて他のタスクの締め切り違反を 24.1〜96.1% 減らしながら LLM のスループットを 64.9〜98.5% 維持し、OnePlus 13 ではカメラ処理の締め切り違反が 91.3% 減る一方で LLM のスループットの 90.4% を保てた。
papers.why: CPU とアクセラレータがメモリ帯域を共有する統合メモリ環境での LLM 推論のスケジューリングという、エッジ推論基盤特有の資源競合問題に具体的な対処法を示す。
papers.summary_en: LLMs increasingly run on edge devices alongside foreground tasks that continuously process sensor data under their own deadlines, but because CPU and accelerators share a unified-memory system, LLM inference can delay foreground processing through memory-bandwidth contention even when compute resources remain available. EdgePace is a bandwidth-aware runtime that creates safe suspension points across prefill and decode, monitors foreground memory demand and stalls at low cost, and schedules inference according to contention risk, deadline slack, and output freshness. Evaluated on a OnePlus 13 and three NVIDIA Jetson platforms using multi-camera processing and robotic target tracking, it reduces foreground deadline misses by 24.1%-96.1% relative to unmanaged inference while retaining 64.9%-98.5% of LLM throughput, with all measured LLM outputs arriving within their task-defined freshness windows; on OnePlus 13, for example, camera deadline misses fall by 91.3% while 90.4% of LLM throughput is retained.
papers.why_en: Addresses memory-bandwidth contention between LLM inference and other latency-critical tasks on unified-memory edge platforms, a resource-contention problem specific to edge inference infrastructure.

papers.title: CoS-VQ: Coordinated Shared-Scale Vector Quantization for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) require substantial memory, motivating low-bit weight quantization for efficient deployment. Existing vector quantization (VQ) methods often improve accuracy by increasing the effective coding dimension, which can complicate independent lookup and local codeword updates. We propose CoS-VQ (Coordinated Shared-Scale Vector Quantization), which preserves low-dimensional codewords while jointly optimizing hard indices and their shared scale across positions. The key challenge is scale-induced coupling: the optimal scale depends on the entire codeword combination and, in turn, changes candidate rankings across positions, so pointwise updates can stall even after scale re-optimization. CoS-VQ collects candidates at multiple probe scales and constructs a tangent separable upper bound for the residual-aware quadratic objective. By reducing candidate comparisons to lower envelopes of lines over positive scales, it identifies finitely many representative intervals for joint index--scale updates without exhaustively enumerating codeword combinations. On Qwen3.8-27B, CoS-VQ outperforms QTIP and LLVQ on the evaluated language modeling, coding, and reasoning benchmarks. Ablations from the same initialization further show larger gains from joint updates than from scale-only refinement, highlighting joint selection as an alternative to increasing codeword dimensionality. The code is available at https://github.com/xzktx003/Cos_VQ.
papers.ja_title: 指数と共有スケールを同時に最適化するベクトル量子化 CoS-VQ
papers.summary: LLM の重みを少ないビット数で表現するベクトル量子化(複数の値をまとめて 1 つの符号に変換する圧縮手法)は、精度を上げるために符号の次元を増やすとランダムアクセスや部分更新が難しくなるという問題があった。CoS-VQ は低次元の符号を保ったまま、各位置が共有するスケール値と符号の組み合わせを同時に最適化し、スケールを変えると各候補の順位も変わってしまう「結合」の問題を、複数のスケールで候補を集めて線分の下側の輪郭に変換することで効率的に解く。Qwen3.8-27B での言語モデリング・コーディング・推論の評価で、既存手法の QTIP や LLVQ を上回り、同じ初期状態からの比較ではスケールだけの再最適化より符号とスケールの同時更新の方が効果が大きいことを示した。
papers.why: 低ビット量子化の精度を符号の次元を増やさずに上げる手段を示しており、メモリ容量が厳しい環境での LLM 重み圧縮の設計選択肢を広げる。
papers.summary_en: Existing vector quantization (VQ) methods for LLM weights often improve accuracy by increasing the effective coding dimension, which can complicate independent lookup and local codeword updates. CoS-VQ preserves low-dimensional codewords while jointly optimizing hard indices and their shared scale across positions, addressing the scale-induced coupling where the optimal scale depends on the entire codeword combination and in turn changes candidate rankings across positions, so pointwise updates can stall even after scale re-optimization; it collects candidates at multiple probe scales and constructs a tangent separable upper bound for the residual-aware quadratic objective, reducing candidate comparisons to lower envelopes of lines over positive scales to identify finitely many representative intervals for joint index-scale updates without exhaustively enumerating codeword combinations. On Qwen3.8-27B, CoS-VQ outperforms QTIP and LLVQ on the evaluated language modeling, coding, and reasoning benchmarks, with ablations from the same initialization showing larger gains from joint updates than from scale-only refinement.
papers.why_en: Highlights joint index-scale selection as an alternative to increasing codeword dimensionality for improving vector-quantization accuracy, widening the design space for LLM weight compression under tight memory budgets.

papers.title: EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations
papers.abstract: We present EmbeddingGemma 2, an open multimodal embedding model which natively represents text, images, audio, video, and combinations thereof in a unified space. Our approach introduces improvements such as simplified per-layer embeddings and a multi-stage curriculum with modality and objective progression which ensure strong quality across unimodal, cross-modal, and mixed-modal evaluations. Notably, in comprehensive embedding benchmarks across all modalities, EmbeddingGemma 2 establishes a new Pareto frontier, outperforming both specialist models and models two to twelve times larger. Furthermore, our design offers flexibility for resource-constrained environments, supporting selective modality encoder loading, adjustable vision token budgets, truncatable embedding dimensions, and quantized weights. We present ablations analyzing key decisions and release EmbeddingGemma 2 to promote further research.
papers.ja_title: テキスト・画像・音声・動画を 1 つの空間に埋め込む EmbeddingGemma 2
papers.summary: EmbeddingGemma 2 はテキスト・画像・音声・動画とその組み合わせを同じ埋め込み空間(意味の近さを座標の近さとして表す空間)でまとめて表現できる公開のマルチモーダル埋め込みモデルである。層ごとの埋め込みの簡略化と、扱うモダリティや目的を段階的に増やしていく多段階の学習カリキュラムによって、単一モーダル・モーダル間・混合モーダルの評価全てで高い品質を確保した。モダリティごとのエンコーダを選んで読み込む仕組みや、画像トークンの予算調整、埋め込み次元の切り詰め、重みの量子化にも対応し、資源が限られた環境にも適応できる。全モダリティを通じた包括的な埋め込みベンチマークで、専門特化モデルや 2〜12 倍大きいモデルを上回る新しい性能と効率のバランスを達成した。
papers.why: 埋め込みモデルを本番環境で動かす際のメモリ・計算コストを、モダリティ選択読み込みや量子化、次元切り詰めといった複数のノブで調整できる設計であり、サービング側の資源制約に合わせた運用の選択肢を増やす。
papers.summary_en: EmbeddingGemma 2 is an open multimodal embedding model that natively represents text, images, audio, video, and combinations thereof in a unified space, introducing simplified per-layer embeddings and a multi-stage curriculum with modality and objective progression to ensure strong quality across unimodal, cross-modal, and mixed-modal evaluations. In comprehensive embedding benchmarks across all modalities, it establishes a new Pareto frontier, outperforming both specialist models and models two to twelve times larger, while its design offers flexibility for resource-constrained environments, supporting selective modality encoder loading, adjustable vision token budgets, truncatable embedding dimensions, and quantized weights.
papers.why_en: Its flexibility knobs (selective encoder loading, truncatable dimensions, quantization) give several concrete levers for tuning memory and compute cost when serving a multimodal embedding model under resource constraints.

papers.title: Channel Selection for Mixture-of-Experts Decoding Needs No Calibration Data
papers.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models are bottlenecked by loading routed-expert weights from memory during interactive decoding at small batch sizes. Because most intermediate channels in a routed expert contribute little to any single token, channel selectors predict which channels matter and read only their weights, typically keeping channels above a threshold calibrated on offline data. We show that channel selection needs no calibration data. First, a calibrated threshold does not fix how much a selector reads, because the number of channels passing it varies across inputs; Prox with thresholds calibrated for an 18% read budget actually reads only 12.9% on average across our benchmarks. Second, top-k keeps each token's k highest-scoring channels and needs no calibration data. At the calibrated budget, a selector's top-k version matches or beats its threshold version on the same score in 40 of 43 comparisons at 13% and 18% budgets, including all 23 on generation tasks. The top-k versions also avoid the repetition-loop collapse that calibrated thresholds cause on Gemma 4. Calibrating a threshold thus provides neither of the two things selectors use it for: a known read budget and a consistent accuracy gain at that budget. We furthermore introduce a reader built entirely from the model's weights, which screens channels with a ternary sketch and recovers the skipped ones with a low-rank map. Across three post-trained MoE models, our reader retains 98.1% of full-model accuracy at 17.8% of routed-expert reads, with Triton kernels running MoE blocks 1.60 to 1.90x faster than optimized vLLM at batch one and up to 2.69x at larger batches on the same three models.
papers.ja_title: キャリブレーション不要の MoE デコード用チャネル選択
papers.summary: MoE モデルの対話的なデコード(少数ずつ逐次生成する処理)は、少ないバッチサイズでは選ばれたエキスパートの重みをメモリから読み込む処理が遅さの原因になり、どのチャネル(重みの中の一部分)が重要かを予測して必要な分だけ読み込むチャネル選択が使われる。この研究は事前にキャリブレーションしたしきい値方式には欠陥があり、読み込む量が入力によって変わってしまい 18%を狙っても実際には 12.9%しか読まれなかった例があること、各トークンの上位 k 個のチャネルを読む方式がキャリブレーション不要で同等以上の精度を 43 件中 40 件で達成したことを示す。重みだけから作った新しい選択器は 3 種類の MoE モデルで、全チャネルを読む場合の精度の 98.1%を、ルーティング先の重みのわずか 17.8%を読むだけで保持し、Triton カーネルは最適化済みの vLLM よりバッチサイズ 1 で 1.60〜1.90 倍、大きいバッチでは最大 2.69 倍速く MoE 層を処理した。
papers.why: チャネル選択のキャリブレーション不要化と上位 k 方式への切り替えという単純な変更が精度と速度の両方を改善することを示しており、MoE デコードの軽量化手法の設計に直接使える知見である。
papers.summary_en: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models are bottlenecked by loading routed-expert weights from memory during interactive decoding at small batch sizes, and channel selectors predict which channels matter and read only their weights, typically keeping channels above a threshold calibrated on offline data. The authors show channel selection needs no calibration data: a calibrated threshold does not fix how much a selector reads, because the number of channels passing it varies across inputs (a selector calibrated for an 18% read budget actually reads only 12.9% on average across their benchmarks), whereas top-k, which keeps each token's k highest-scoring channels and needs no calibration data, matches or beats the threshold version on the same score in 40 of 43 comparisons at 13% and 18% budgets (including all 23 generation-task comparisons) and avoids a repetition-loop collapse that calibrated thresholds cause on Gemma 4. They further introduce a reader built entirely from the model's weights, which screens channels with a ternary sketch and recovers skipped ones with a low-rank map; across three post-trained MoE models it retains 98.1% of full-model accuracy at 17.8% of routed-expert reads, with Triton kernels running MoE blocks 1.60-1.90x faster than optimized vLLM at batch one and up to 2.69x at larger batches on the same three models.
papers.why_en: Shows with counted comparisons that a widely used offline-calibrated threshold delivers neither of the two properties it is used for (a known read budget or a consistent accuracy gain at that budget), and that a calibration-free top-k alternative is both simpler and better.

review.note: オフラインでキャリブレーションしたしきい値方式を 43 件の直接比較で検証し、狙った読み込み量(18%)を実際には下回る(12.9%)など、キャリブレーションが主張する性質を提供していないことを示した。評価条件の「狙った予算」という設定値そのものが実際には成立していない可能性があるという、評価設計の落とし穴の教訓。
review.note_en: Directly compares a calibrated-threshold channel selector against a calibration-free top-k rule across 43 head-to-head tests, showing the calibrated threshold does not actually hit its stated read budget (18% target, 12.9% actual) and underperforms top-k on most comparisons -- a cautionary case that an evaluation setup's stated knob may not measure what it claims to.

papers.title: Kernel Performance Engineering under Physical Non-Idealities
papers.abstract: Physical non-idealities in integrated circuit (IC) design and fabrication are concealed by conventional hardware abstractions, yet they can limit kernel performance and obscure optimization opportunities. Using distributed shared memory (DSMEM) on NVIDIA H100 GPUs as a case study, we show how floorsweeping restricts hardware resources available for clustered execution, potentially offsetting the benefits of reduced data movement enabled by DSMEM. Guided by these insights, we develop a wave-aware clustering strategy that accounts for these resource constraints to improve kernel performance. Evaluations using a global-load-and-broadcast microbenchmark, GEMM, and the Hopper version of FlashAttention 4 demonstrate the performance implications of these constraints, with wave-aware clustering improving FlashAttention 4 throughput by up to 5.30% over its baseline. We further show that, under thermal design power (TDP) limits, reduced data movement enables higher Streaming Multiprocessor (SM) frequencies through Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS), explaining otherwise unexpected throughput improvements. Extending this analysis beyond GPUs, we show that power constraints also limit throughput scaling on Tenstorrent's Wormhole accelerator, highlighting the broader importance of accounting for physical non-idealities when analyzing and optimizing kernel performance.
papers.ja_title: 製造上の物理的な制約がカーネル性能に与える影響を解明する研究
papers.summary: 半導体チップの設計・製造時に生じる物理的な不完全さは通常のハードウェア抽象化の裏に隠れているが、カーネルの性能を制限し最適化の機会を見えなくしてしまう。NVIDIA H100 GPU の分散共有メモリ(DSMEM、複数の計算コア間で直接データをやり取りする仕組み)を例に、フロアスイーピング(製造時の歩留まり対策で一部の回路を無効化する処理)がクラスタ実行で使えるハードウェア資源を制限し、DSMEM によるデータ移動削減の利点を打ち消しうることを示した。この知見をもとに資源制約を考慮した「ウェーブ対応」クラスタリング戦略を開発し、Hopper 版 FlashAttention 4 のスループットを基準より最大 5.30% 改善し、データ移動の削減が電力上限下での動作周波数向上を通じて性能改善につながることも示した。
papers.why: GPU の理論性能だけでなく製造上の非理想性まで踏まえてカーネルを設計する視点を提供し、高性能カーネル開発で見落とされがちなハードウェア側の制約を具体的な数値で示している。
papers.summary_en: Physical non-idealities in integrated circuit (IC) design and fabrication are concealed by conventional hardware abstractions, yet the authors show they can limit kernel performance and obscure optimization opportunities. Using distributed shared memory (DSMEM) on NVIDIA H100 GPUs as a case study, they show floorsweeping restricts hardware resources available for clustered execution, potentially offsetting the benefits of reduced data movement enabled by DSMEM, and develop a wave-aware clustering strategy that accounts for these constraints; evaluations using a global-load-and-broadcast microbenchmark, GEMM, and the Hopper version of FlashAttention 4 demonstrate wave-aware clustering improving FlashAttention 4 throughput by up to 5.30% over baseline. They further show that, under thermal design power (TDP) limits, reduced data movement enables higher Streaming Multiprocessor (SM) frequencies through Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS), explaining otherwise unexpected throughput improvements, and that power constraints also limit throughput scaling on Tenstorrent's Wormhole accelerator.
papers.why_en: Argues that kernel performance analysis and optimization needs to account for physical non-idealities (floorsweeping, power/DVFS interactions) that conventional hardware abstractions hide, beyond NVIDIA GPUs.

papers.title: Multi-State Linear Attention with Generalized Second-Order Routing
papers.abstract: Self-attention plays a key role in long-sequence modeling, but its quadratic time complexity fundamentally limits the scaling of Large Language Models. Recently, Multi-State Linear Attention (MSLA) mechanisms have been proposed to make sequence modeling more efficient by splitting the context into segments and compressing each in its own memory state. MSLA aggregates the information extracted from each memory state using only the mean alignment between a query and each segment's keys, ignoring how the alignment is distributed within the segment. In order to model the relevance of a segment to a query more comprehensively and incorporate the variance of the alignment in the aggregation, we propose MERLIN (MomEnt Routing for multi-state LINear attention), a method that tracks the first and second moments of each segment's keys. Using the moments of keys, a query can recover both the mean and the variance of its alignment with each segment to perform a more content-aware aggregation of per-state readouts. Experiments on multi-state variants of Gated DeltaNet-1.3B and Mamba-2-780M show that MERLIN consistently outperforms existing aggregation methods on various long-context tasks. In particular, MERLIN outperforms baselines on RULER needle-in-a-haystack and long-context QA (+8.3% for Gated DeltaNet-1.3B and +7.0% for Mamba-2-780M) and diverse subtasks in LongBench (+13.5% and +12.0%). It even outperforms baselines that consume 4x more memory. MERLIN provides a simple and general routing mechanism for improving long-context capabilities of MSLA models.
papers.ja_title: 平均と分散の両方を使う線形アテンションのルーティング手法 MERLIN
papers.summary: 通常の自己注意機構(自己アテンション)は系列長の 2 乗に比例して計算量が増えるため長い文脈のモデル化を妨げるが、文脈を区間に分けてそれぞれを圧縮した記憶状態として持つ Multi-State Linear Attention (MSLA) という手法でこれを回避できる。既存の MSLA は各区間へのクエリの一致度を平均値だけで集約していたが、MERLIN は各区間のキーの平均と分散(ばらつき)の両方を追跡し、より内容を反映した集約を可能にする。Gated DeltaNet-1.3B と Mamba-2-780M を使った実験で、RULER の長文脈探索課題や長文脈質問応答で既存の集約手法を上回り(+8.3%や+7.0%)、LongBench の複数の課題でも改善し(+13.5%や+12.0%)、4 倍多いメモリを使う手法さえ上回った。
papers.why: 長文脈を扱う効率的な注意機構の集約方法に平均だけでなく分散も使うという単純な改良を加えており、SSM 系や線形アテンション系アーキテクチャの長文脈性能を上げる実装上の具体策になる。
papers.summary_en: Self-attention plays a key role in long-sequence modeling, but its quadratic time complexity fundamentally limits LLM scaling; Multi-State Linear Attention (MSLA) mechanisms make sequence modeling more efficient by splitting context into segments compressed into separate memory states, but they aggregate information using only the mean alignment between a query and each segment's keys, ignoring how the alignment is distributed within the segment. MERLIN (MomEnt Routing for multi-state LINear attention) tracks the first and second moments of each segment's keys, so a query can recover both the mean and variance of its alignment with each segment for more content-aware aggregation of per-state readouts. On multi-state variants of Gated DeltaNet-1.3B and Mamba-2-780M, MERLIN consistently outperforms existing aggregation methods on long-context tasks, including RULER needle-in-a-haystack and long-context QA (+8.3% for Gated DeltaNet-1.3B, +7.0% for Mamba-2-780M) and diverse LongBench subtasks (+13.5% and +12.0%), even outperforming baselines that consume 4x more memory.
papers.why_en: Offers a simple and general routing mechanism (using variance as well as mean of key alignment) for improving the long-context capability of MSLA models, potentially without increasing memory use.

papers.title: Scaling Laws for Tool-Use Agents via Controllable Environment Synthesis
papers.abstract: We explore how to build performant large language model (LLM) tool-use agents that complete complex, multi-step tasks. Specifically, we study how data composition in synthetically generated tool-use environments affects the training of such agents. To do so, we propose the SynthAPI pipeline, which explicitly controls the diversity of generated environments along the axes of tools, tasks, and the databases on which the tools operate. By systematically varying SynthAPI's generation controls in 458,752 tasks across 849 trained models of four different sizes, we derive a scaling law that predicts downstream tool-use agent generalization based on the scale and composition of the synthesized environments. These predictable relationships reveal several lessons for scaling tool-use agent data. As data budgets grow, scaling tool and database diversity becomes more effective than increasing the number of tasks, and increasing data complexity yields larger gains. Scaling according to these findings yields agents that outperform models trained on data from prior work in large-scale tool-use agent and synthetic environment generation across four evaluation benchmarks.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: ツール利用エージェントの学習データ設計をスケーリング則で決める
papers.summary: 複雑で多段階のタスクをこなす LLM のツール利用エージェントを作るため、合成的に生成した「ツール利用環境」のデータの組み合わせ方が学習にどう影響するかを調べた研究である。SynthAPI というパイプラインでツールの種類・タスク・ツールが操作するデータベースの多様性を独立に制御し、4 種類のサイズで 849 個のモデルを合計 458,752 タスクで学習させることでスケーリング則(データ量とモデル性能の関係)を導き出した。この法則から、データ予算が増えるほどタスク数を増やすよりツールとデータベースの多様性を増やす方が効果的であること、データの複雑さを上げるほど利益が大きくなることが分かった。
papers.why: ツール利用エージェントの学習データをどの軸(ツール数・タスク数・データベース多様性)に投資すべきかを定量的なスケーリング則として示し、合成データ生成の設計判断に具体的な指針を与える。
papers.summary_en: The authors explore how to build performant LLM tool-use agents for complex, multi-step tasks, specifically how data composition in synthetically generated tool-use environments affects training. They propose the SynthAPI pipeline, which explicitly controls the diversity of generated environments along the axes of tools, tasks, and the databases on which the tools operate, and by systematically varying these generation controls across 458,752 tasks and 849 trained models of four different sizes, they derive a scaling law that predicts downstream tool-use agent generalization based on the scale and composition of synthesized environments. As data budgets grow, scaling tool and database diversity becomes more effective than increasing the number of tasks, and increasing data complexity yields larger gains; agents trained according to these findings outperform models trained on data from prior work in large-scale tool-use agent and synthetic environment generation, across four evaluation benchmarks.
papers.why_en: Gives a quantitative scaling law for deciding which axis (tools, tasks, or database diversity) to invest a data budget in when generating synthetic tool-use training environments.

blogs.title: Serving DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at Scale: vLLM Matches DeepInfer and Scales to GB300 NVL72
blogs.excerpt: With P/D disaggregation and Wide-EP on a GB300 NVL72 rack, vLLM serves DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on SemiAnalysis AgentX at 954K tokens/s per GPU at a P90 of 196 tokens/s per user, 7.9x our aggregated single-node result.
blogs.ja_title: vLLM が GB300 NVL72 で DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash を大規模配信、DeepInfer に匹敵
blogs.summary: GB300 NVL72 ラック 1 台で、vLLM は P/D 分離 (prefill と decode を別 GPU で処理する方式) と Wide-EP (エキスパートを多数の GPU に広げる並列化) を組み合わせ、DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash を SemiAnalysis の AgentX ベンチマークで GPU 1 台あたり 95.4 万 token/秒、ユーザー 1 人あたり P90 で 196 token/秒で配信した。これは前回記事の単一ノード集約構成と比べて 7.9 倍のスループットで、GPU 1 時間あたり 38.96 ドル (DeepSeek のオフピーク料金換算) になる。DeepSeek 自身の専用エンジン DeepInfer と比べても、decode スループットはバッチサイズ 8〜256 の範囲で 6% 以内の差に収まり、prefill も DeepInfer の公開曲線をなぞった。
blogs.why: 汎用エンジン (vLLM) がモデル専用エンジン (DeepInfer) に匹敵できることを実測で示し、分離配信・Wide-EP・EPLB などの最適化を組み合わせる具体的な設計判断を公開している点が、分散推論基盤を作る人にとって参考になる。
blogs.summary_en: On one NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 rack, vLLM with P/D disaggregation and Wide-EP serves DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on SemiAnalysis AgentX at 954K tokens/s per GPU at a P90 of 196 tokens/s per user, 7.9x the single-node aggregated result from the first post, at $38.96 per GPU-hour at DeepSeek's off-peak prices. Against DeepInfer, DeepSeek's own engine, vLLM's decode throughput is within 6% across batch sizes 8-256, and its prefill tracks DeepInfer's published curve.
blogs.why_en: Shows a general-purpose engine can match a model-specific one, and lays out which optimizations (DEP2 prefill, Wide-EP decode with EPLB, a specialized low-latency decode path) got it there.

blogs.title: GLM-5.3 Optimizations, Part 2: PCP, DCP, and Hybrid HiSparse on 16 H200s
blogs.excerpt: vLLM serves GLM-5.3 on 16 H200s with PCP and DCP prefill and Hybrid HiSparse decode, reaching 1M-token contexts and 1.7–3.2× the per-user speed of data-parallel P/D on the AgentX agentic benchmark.
blogs.ja_title: GLM-5.3、PCP と DCP と Hybrid HiSparse で 16 台の H200 上で 100 万トークン文脈を配信
blogs.summary: 長いやり取りを繰り返すエージェント型の使い方では文脈 (これまでの対話の記憶) がどんどん長くなり、GPU のメモリと prefill (入力を読み込む処理) の速度の両方を圧迫する。vLLM チームは 16 台の H200 を prefill 用 1 ノードと decode 用 1 ノードに分け、prefill では Prefill Context Parallelism (PCP、プロンプトをトークン単位で分割する並列化) と Decode Context Parallelism (DCP、KV キャッシュもトークン単位で分割) を組み合わせ、decode では Hybrid HiSparse (KV キャッシュの一部をホストメモリに置く仕組み) を使った。AgentX ベンチマークでは、同じスループットのもとでデータ並列構成と比べてユーザー 1 人あたりの速度が 1.7〜3.2 倍になり、100 万トークンの文脈を配信できたのはこの構成だけだった。
blogs.why: GLM-5.3 のスパースアテンションに合うように並列化の軸をヘッド単位でなくトークン単位に変えた設計判断と、prefill/decode 分離環境での長文脈対応を具体的な数値で示している。
blogs.summary_en: On 16 H200s split into one prefill node and one decode node, Prefill Context Parallelism (PCP) splits each prompt across GPUs by token (suiting GLM-5.3's sparse attention better than tensor parallelism), Decode Context Parallelism (DCP) shards the prefill engine's KV cache by token so a 1M context fits on the prefill node, and Hybrid HiSparse lets decode keep KV in host memory. On AgentX, PCP8 x DCP8 prefill with Hybrid HiSparse decode gives 1.7-3.2x the per-user speed of a data-parallel deployment at the same throughput, and it is the only configuration tested that serves 1M-token contexts.
blogs.why_en: Demonstrates why standard TP/DP don't suit long agentic contexts under memory pressure, and shows a composable alternative (PCP+DCP+Hybrid HiSparse) enabled by vLLM's new modular core (Model Runner V2).

blogs.title: vLLM Delivers Day-0 Support for MiniMax-M3.1-Flash
blogs.excerpt: Day-0 vLLM support for MiniMax-M3.1-Flash on NVIDIA Blackwell, NVIDIA Rubin, and AMD MI350-series GPUs, with NVFP4 MSA kernels, NVFP4 MegaMoE, DSpark speculative decoding, AgentX results, and day-0 RL.
blogs.ja_title: MiniMax-M3.1-Flash、Blackwell/Rubin/AMD 向け NVFP4 カーネルで vLLM が Day-0 対応
blogs.summary: MiniMax-M3.1-Flash は NVFP4 (4 bit の低精度形式) の KV キャッシュと MoE (複数の専門家モデルを切り替える構造) の重み、投機的デコード用の DSpark というドラフトモデルを使う設計で、vLLM は発売初日から NVIDIA Blackwell・Rubin・AMD MI350 系 GPU に対応した。NVIDIA Blackwell 向けの MSA (MiniMax Sparse Attention) カーネルは CUDA 13.4 の新命令 QMUL4 でカーネル内で NVFP4 を FP8 に変換し、インデクサの QK decode を最大 1.7 倍、スパースアテンションの decode を最大 1.3 倍速くした。NVFP4 MegaMoE は prefill のカーネル遅延を 20% 減らし prefill スループットを 7% 上げ、decode 用の Context Parallelism はインデクサを 512K 文脈で最大 3.3 倍速くした。
blogs.why: 低精度 (NVFP4) のカーネルをハードウェアの新命令に合わせて書き分けた具体例と、各最適化の効果を個別に数値で切り分けている点が、カーネル実装の参考になる。
blogs.summary_en: MiniMax-M3.1-Flash uses MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA) with an NVFP4 KV cache for both the indexer and the attention path, plus NVFP4 MoE weights and a DSpark drafter; vLLM supports it day-0 on NVIDIA Blackwell, NVIDIA Rubin, and AMD MI350-series GPUs. Blackwell MSA kernels use the new CUDA 13.4 QMUL4 instruction to dequantize NVFP4 into FP8 inside the kernel: up to 1.7x faster indexer QK decode and 1.3x faster sparse attention decode. NVFP4 MegaMoE with MXFP8 shared-expert fusion and early TMEM release gives 20% lower kernel latency in prefill and 7% higher prefill throughput, and indexer decode context parallelism (DCP) is up to 3.3x faster per sparse layer at 512K context on 4x GB300.
blogs.why_en: A concrete example of hand-matching low-precision (NVFP4) kernels to new hardware instructions, with each optimization's effect isolated and measured separately across Blackwell, Rubin, and AMD.

blogs.title: SGLang security update: improving request isolation
blogs.excerpt: On September 9, 2026, Cloudflare notified us of cross-request KV cache exposure in its GLM-5.3 deployment on Workers AI. We worked with Cloudflare to address the request-rejection path involved and strengthen related cache-lifetime handling in disaggregated serving.
blogs.ja_title: SGLang のセキュリティ修正: 分離配信で KV キャッシュが別ユーザーに漏れた原因と対策
blogs.summary: 2026 年 9 月、Cloudflare は自社の GLM-5.3 配信 (Workers AI 上) で、別ユーザーのセッションの内容が返ってくる事故を SGLang チームに報告した。原因は、設定上の最大文脈長 (1,048,576 トークン) が実際に確保していた KV キャッシュの容量 (681,280 トークン) より大きかったことで、本来拒否されるはずのリクエストが prefill から decode への受け渡し (disaggregated 配信) を通過してしまい、decode 側がまだ書き込まれていないキャッシュのページを読んでしまった。SGLang チームは拒否対象のリクエストを確実に止める admission (受け入れ) の修正と、KV キャッシュの解放タイミングを遅らせる Deferred Release などの対策を入れた。
blogs.why: 分離 (prefill/decode disaggregation) 配信では単一ノードで効いていた拒否処理がそのままでは効かないという、配信アーキテクチャ特有の失敗モードを実例で示している。
blogs.summary_en: On September 9, 2026, Cloudflare notified the SGLang team of cross-request KV cache exposure in its GLM-5.3 deployment on Workers AI, affecting that model between August 27 and September 9, 2026. Cloudflare's deployment had a configured context length of 1,048,576 tokens but a prefill KV cache pool that could hold only 681,280 tokens, so a request could fit the configured context window while exceeding available memory; in SGLang's disaggregated prefill/decode path a request marked for rejection could still proceed through the handoff, and decode could then read cache pages that had not been populated for that request. The fix includes deferred KV cache release and an admission fix, among other changes to the disaggregated serving path.
blogs.why_en: Shows a disaggregated-serving-specific failure mode: a single-node rejection path doesn't automatically carry over to the prefill/decode handoff, and a config-vs-actual-capacity mismatch is what makes the unreachable path reachable.

review.note: 単一ノードで動いていた拒否・エラー処理が、分離 (prefill/decode) 構成でも同じように効くかを確かめる観点。設定値 (最大文脈長) と実際の確保量 (KV キャッシュ容量) の不一致を突く再現テストが有効。
review.note_en: A review angle for checking whether a rejection/error path that works on a single node still holds once prefill and decode are split into separate workers; a reproduction test that deliberately mismatches a configured limit (max context length) against the actually reserved capacity (KV cache pool) is what surfaces this.

blogs.title: miniTE Technical Report: Stable and Efficient Reinforcement Learning with Native NVFP4
blogs.excerpt: Native NVFP4 reinforcement learning must remain stable under quantization and execution error while delivering practical efficiency gains. We investigate late-training instability by examining quantization formats, activation scaling, KV-cache precision, and framework differences that affect policy probabilities.
blogs.ja_title: miniTE: NVFP4 ネイティブ強化学習を安定させる技術報告
blogs.summary: NVFP4 (4 bit の低精度形式) をそのまま使う強化学習 (RL) は、量子化の誤差や学習・推論間の実行差で学習後半に不安定になりやすい。miniTE は量子化誤差・変換誤差・実行上のずれを、更新の方向性と合わせて解釈する TRIAGE という手法で安定化し、Transformer Engine と統合したレイヤーで NVFP4 の per-token スケーリングやカーネル実装を最適化している。評価では、数値的な正しさ・学習の挙動・実行効率を分けて測り、重みの更新と同期が依然としてボトルネックであることなどを報告している。
blogs.why: 低精度 RL を安定させる手法と、数値監視・プロファイリング・train/inference 間の整合性診断の具体的な作り方が、RL 後学習基盤を作る人にそのまま使える。
blogs.summary_en: Native NVFP4 reinforcement learning must remain stable under quantization and execution error while delivering practical efficiency gains. The report investigates why native NVFP4 RL becomes unstable (quantization error, conversion error, and execution mismatch, interacting with activation precision, scaling granularity, and the KV cache), introduces TRIAGE, a direction-aware stabilization mechanism, and builds miniTE, which aligns numerical execution with Transformer Engine integration, per-token scaling, and kernel optimizations. The evaluation separates numerical correctness, learning behavior, and execution efficiency, and finds that weight updates and synchronization remain a bottleneck.
blogs.why_en: Gives a concrete stabilization mechanism (TRIAGE) and a layered engineering recipe (precision recipes, numerical monitoring, train-inference alignment) for running RL natively in low precision, directly usable by people building RL post-training infrastructure.

blogs.title: More Than DeepInfer: What SGLang Delivers
blogs.excerpt: DeepSeek open-sourced DeepInfer, the inference engine behind its own service, together with the kernels it runs on. It sets the bar for how fast DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash can run, so we measured SGLang against it with DeepInfer's own benchmarks on the same hardware.
blogs.ja_title: SGLang 対 DeepInfer: DeepSeek の公開ベンチマークで同等以上を実測
blogs.summary: DeepSeek が自社エンジン DeepInfer を公開したのに合わせて、SGLang チームは同じハードウェア・同じベンチマークで SGLang と DeepInfer を比較した。prefill は 4 台の GB300 と 4 台の B300 で DeepInfer より最大 1.04 倍のスループット、decode は 64 台の GB300 で decode の 1 ステップにかかる時間が最大 7.4% 短く、残りの計測点では差は 1% 以内だった。SGLang は DeepSeek が公開した Mega 系カーネルや DSpark 投機的デコードなどをすでに取り込んでおり、さらに KV キャッシュ管理・prefill/decode 分離・複数レプリカへの負荷分散という、DeepInfer の README が「含まれていない」と明記する機能一式を備えた配信システムであることを示した。
blogs.why: 専用エンジンが公開したベンチマークに対し、汎用の配信エンジンが同じ条件でどこまで迫れるかを測った実測比較であり、カーネル移植の完成度を定量的に確認できる。
blogs.summary_en: DeepSeek open-sourced DeepInfer, the inference engine behind its own service, together with the kernels it runs on, so the SGLang team measured SGLang against it with DeepInfer's own benchmarks on the same hardware. Results: on par or ahead on DeepInfer's own benchmarks, up to 1.04x prefill throughput on 4x GB300 and 4x B300, up to 7.4% shorter decode steps on 64x GB300, and within 1% at the remaining points. SGLang has integrated DeepSeek's kernels (including the Mega series), DSpark speculative decoding, SWA bounded replay, and both Engram placements, and is a full serving system with a KV cache system, prefill/decode disaggregation, and load balancing across replicas that DeepInfer's own README lists as not included in its release.
blogs.why_en: A direct, same-hardware measurement of how close a general-purpose serving engine gets to a model's own specialized engine, useful for judging how complete a kernel port actually is.

blogs.title: Announcing the SGLang AWS Trainium Plugin Beta
blogs.excerpt: In collaboration with AWS and alongside the TorchNeuron launch, we are announcing the beta of the SGLang Trainium plugin, enabling both inference serving and RL rollouts on AWS Trainium.
blogs.ja_title: SGLang が AWS Trainium 向けプラグインをベータ公開、推論配信と RL ロールアウトに対応
blogs.summary: SGLang チームは AWS と協力し、AWS の新しいネイティブ PyTorch バックエンドである TorchNeuron の上に SGLang の Trainium 向けプラグインをベータとして公開した。プライベートプレビューの段階から TorchNeuron を使って開発したため、SGLang のモデル実装やコアの抽象化は Trainium にほぼそのまま持ち込め、性能が必要な部分は NKI (Neuron Kernel Interface) でカスタムカーネルを書ける。ベータでは Trainium2/Trainium3 上で、Qwen3 (dense)・Qwen3-MoE-30B-A3B・DeepSeek-V2-Lite・GLM-4・GLM-5.2/5.3 などのモデルの推論配信と、RL 後学習のロールアウト生成の両方に対応する。
blogs.why: GPU 向けに書いた配信エンジンの抽象化を、別のアクセラレータ (Trainium) にどう移植するかという設計方針 (ネイティブ PyTorch バックエンド採用) の具体例になる。
blogs.summary_en: In collaboration with AWS and alongside the TorchNeuron launch, the SGLang team announced the beta of the SGLang AWS Trainium plugin, built on TorchNeuron, AWS's native PyTorch backend for Trainium. Because the SGLang Neuron backend was built on TorchNeuron since its private preview, SGLang's model components and core abstractions carried over to Trainium largely intact, and NKI (the Neuron Kernel Interface) enables custom Trainium kernels within the PyTorch workflow for additional performance. The beta supports both LLM inference serving and RL rollout generation for post-training on AWS Trainium2 and Trainium3, with initial model coverage including Qwen3 (dense), Qwen3-MoE-30B-A3B, DeepSeek-V2-Lite, GLM-4, and GLM-5.2/5.3.
blogs.why_en: A concrete example of the design choice (building on a native PyTorch backend from day one) that lets a GPU-oriented serving engine's abstractions port to a different accelerator with minimal changes, while still allowing low-level kernel control where needed.

blogs.title: Announcing SOCI-indexed images for faster SageMaker AI jobs
